review_text: Started in 2002,  Freddys Frozen Custard & Steakburgers has grown coast-to-coast and serves made to order food without a long wait. Before I get to my sandwich, I must note that the fries are excellent! They also have their own fry sauce, which seems to combine mayonnaise and ketchup with some signature spices. As I dont eat burgers I was left picking between the veggie burger and the grilled chicken sandwich. I went with the veggie burger and was presently surprised. The patty is made mostly of black beans, and though mine seemed to be a touch over cooked, the texture and flavor were good. It came topped with cheese, a full slice of onion, Freddys sauce, lettuce, and tomato on a toasted bun. Next time Ill be sure to take the kids as they will love the burger, grilled cheese, and chicken tender options. I also need to try some of the frozen custard.
history_reviews: [['107308665915051259545_604c507ac8168e2fc8a7306f', 'I went with the North Carolina pulled pork sandwich with pickle on a brioche bun. My wife went with the firecracker shrimp platter with fries and coleslaw ($13).'], ['107308665915051259545_6055b23097d555cc6fb0ce80', 'I started with the wedge salad ($3.75) with iceberg, blue cheese, applewood smoked bacon, tomatoes, red onions, and blue cheese dressing. Nothing too out of the ordinary here, though I don\'t recall having red onion on a wedge before. My kids love their garlic knots. My wife really wanted to try their honey Sriracha Brussels Sprouts ($6.95). My dinner I went with the classic combo pizza ($12.50 for the 6") with pepperoni, Italian sausage, mushrooms, and seasoned tomatoes. The deep-dish pizza did not disappoint! My wife enjoyed the EnLIGHTened barbacoa cauliflower pita tacos with seasonal bistro grains ($10.75). Two thick pita shells are filled with roasted cauliflower and red peppers, sweet corn, jack and cheddar cheese, onions, tomatoes, greek yogurt crema, and cilantro.'], ['107308665915051259545_60495d4e1ec03878d66c7871', 'For lunch I chose the pulled pork sandwich with BBQ sauce, cheddar cheese, and pickles on a cornmeal Kaiser bun with a side of Carolina slaw ($9). The side of slaw was immediately dumped on my sandwich and the flavors melted together perfectly. The prices are a bit high since sides are not included, but who can complain when you can get a side of fried pickles for $5! Our kids enjoyed the grilled cheese with fries and drink for $6.50.'], ['107308665915051259545_6045a8ed3ed2666ae7ac1a5e', "The Urban Grill food truck has been a favorite of mine since I first tried it back in 2013. Urban Grill is famous for their grilled mac 'n cheese, which can be found sandwiched on a bun and topped with a variety of toppings. I went with the Urban Mac with pepper bacon and pepper relish ($12). This normally comes with kettle chips but I upgraded to fresh-cut fries for $3. The grilled mac n' cheese actually holds up really well in sandwich form as the crispy cheese on the outside helps keep the creamy inside contained. Each of the grilled mac sandwiches I've tried are great! My wife went with the couscous salad with grilled chicken, vegetables, slivered almonds, golden raisins, cranberries, and goat cheese ($10). She choose to have it topped with Thai peanut sauce. She was in love with this dish. My son had the mini burger with chips ($6) and ate nearly the entire thing. The unique thing hear is that the cheese is grilled onto the bun, similarly to how the mac 'n cheese is grilled. My daughter had the grilled chicken and mac 'n cheese ($6). Urban Grill's chicken is marinated, grilled, and pulled into bite size pieces making it very easy for anyone to eat."], ['107308665915051259545_6045a79b3ed2666ae7ac1a4f', 'MOD Pizza is a chain of over 200 restaurants across the country specializing in fast and casual pizzas. The first decision is whether to have a pizza or a salad. You can choose from 10 signature pizzas, three salads, or create your own. They use a gas-fired oven to cook at 800 degrees in a matter of minutes. For my lunch visit I went with the Caspian pizza with mozzarella, Gorgonzola, BBQ chicken, barbecue sauce, and sliced red onions. The sweet sauce complimented the tangy cheese very well. The pizza was cooked perfectly, with just the slightest bit of char on the edges of the crust. This was a really good pizza and I look forward to trying some other creations soon.'], ['107308665915051259545_604a83b9c6dc737bce7e5b95', 'My wife ordered the New Pass Stuffed Tomato with chicken salad ($9.99). Choice of homemade chicken or tuna salad stuffed in a fresh ripe tomato served on a bed of lettuce, onions, pickles, and greek peppers. Once you start slicing this up, it is essentially a salad topped with chicken salad. The chicken salad was tasty and no dressing was required for the salad. I ordered the chicken salad sub ($8.99) and onion rings ($4.99). The sub was really good, and again a quality traditional chicken salad with celery and mayo. Our kids enjoyed the grilled cheese with fries ($6.99).'], ['107308665915051259545_604a8bc4b1a0aaee3eefbcac', 'They claim these to be award-winning creamy dreamy grits, and they certainly were creamy.'], ['107308665915051259545_604ed3aa04e83abe8d3dcb98', "The house made fried pickles and pepperoncinis were a great start to our meal ($4 during happy hour, $5.95 otherwise). I'm a huge fan of fried pickles but I don't recall having fried pepperoncinis before. For dinner I went with Merlin's Carolina pork with mustard BBQ, cole slaw, crispy onions, and house pickles ($11.95). The sandwich was piled high with well flavored pork. As good as my dinner was I was pretty jealous of my wife's order of the ancho chile chicken bowl with brown rice, black beans, corn, fresh pico de gallo, tortilla strips, lime creama, and cilantro ($13.95). The flavor combination in this bowl was outstanding, similar to a taco style bowl from other places, but the ingredients were fresher and the serving size was huge. history_reviews: [['107530534188116227736_60490265f9e05764f1fa5cfd', "They do they're best to make BBQ that anyone can enjoy. My choices were Ribs, half sauced and half dry-rubbed, Smoked Chicken and BBQ Brisket with sides of green beans and baked beans. First off it tried the ribs, and for mass-produced products, it wasn't bad at all for a chain restaurant. The ribs had a smokiness to them, and they were tender. I tried a few different sauces on them to experiment a little all in all they were pretty good ribs. For the brisket, I made a sandwich with a few of the sauces, to keep it interesting, and was lucky to get a good cut of brisket that wasn't too dry, I mean we all know how finicky brisket can be right? The sandwich was delicious!! I then when to town on the chicken, which I tried with a hot sauce, which made the chicken very tangy and a little spicy. The Green beans were a good size and were alright, a little soft the baked beans, however, had a nice sauce, so they were enjoyable as well."], ['107530534188116227736_605520be3019cb0a478387c8', 'I chose the Mac and Jacks African Amber, the Seafood Stuffed Mushrooms, and the CrabDaddy Feast. The beer was Ice cold and a perfect match for my Stuffed Mushrooms, The mushroom dish was adequately filled with crab, lobster, and shrimp, it was served hot with the cheese still bubbling!! It also came with some crispy and butter-drenched Garlic Toast. The bucket was awesome as usual, three types of crab and the bucket was filled, I was over full with crab by the time I finished.'], ['107530534188116227736_6043b5f0ad733fba1bcfe030', "Full of chunks of Elk, Bison and Venison without to much spice, this was a very hearty and delicious bowl of chilli. I hadn't had a Salisbury Steak in years and the description on the menu - Elk Salisbury Steak with Onion-Mushroom Brown gravy, Cheddar mashed potatoes and asparagus totally appealed to me. The meat was soft, flavourful yet firm and that gravy was heavenly, the cheddar mash was a great accompaniment and the asparagus was fresh, soft and crunchy at the same time, details, details!!"], ['107530534188116227736_604870cab3f169c1781603e0', 'This evening I decided to try something new, I asked my server what they recommended and I ordered the Local Strawberry Salad and the SNAPPER VERACRUZ & SHRIMP. The fish was cooked perfectly and had nice flakiness to it. The Shrimp was also fresh and flavourful. The Market Broiler is always consistent, the food is great and they always have good beer on tap and great wine to pair with your food.'], ['107530534188116227736_6052b42ed8c08f462b93e99f', "The one dish that caught my eye was the 'Spicy Yak Stew' so I filled up a bowl and grabbed a piece of fresh just made Naan. OMG is all I can say as this was one of the most delicious stews I've ever had with tender chunks of yak, vegetables and a savoury broth. The Sherpa house also brews its own craft beer for those of you who enjoy that indulgence, please also note there are only one person bathrooms for men and women. I was very fortunate to be seated alongside two members of Golden CrossFit and went for a workout later that day."], ['107530534188116227736_604d2d1b77e81aaed3cca631', "On this visit, I sat at the bar and looked over the menu for a few minutes until the bartender came over to help me with the menu and suggested the Garlic Shrimp Oreganata with garlic-oregano crusted oven-roasted shrimp, capellini pasta, tomato-basil sauce and since I hadn't had a good oreganata in a while so I was intrigued. If you're unsure what an oreganata is.. the Oreganata style is typically a mixture of breadcrumbs, dried oregano, butter or oil and garlic. Lemon and Parmesan are commonly added to the breadcrumb mixture for extra flavour. I rounded out my meal with the Biaggi's famous Sherry Tomato soup, tomato soup with...well you guessed it, sherry and housemade croutons. Next up was a spinach salad with red onion, gorgonzola cheese, bacon, hard-boiled egg, sun-dried and tomato-bacon dressing. The salad was fresh and the spinach was firm and solid, with no wilted pieces in it. The complexity of all the ingredients blended together made it a very enjoyable salad but leaning a bit on the higher calorie side of salads in general. The shrimp's batter was slightly crispy and the shrimp inside still had flavour. The capellini was cooked just right and the sauce tasted like a classic Italian tomato sauce."], ['107530534188116227736_60570e1dd2ad6b7a67e27f54', 'I made my way over to the Red Yeti which was quite busy with folks on the patio and lots of people inside ( a good sign ) and I saw well...a big Red Yeti outside. The Red Yeti is a Restaurant and a Pub which makes their own beer so I guess that makes a brewpub? I also noticed they had a fried chicken dish as well. Since I had just come from a CrossFit workout I thought "No way I can\'t have fried chicken". I had watched a couple of plates come out from the kitchen and noticed it wasn\'t a typical fried chicken dish. Its made with white boneless chicken breast, so after learning that I went ahead and ordered the refreshing Apple Walnut Salad with shrimp and the Buttermilk Fried Chicken with Boneless, skinless breast, bourbon & rosemary syrup, braised kale with bacon & onion and Weisenberger Mills Smoked Cheddar Grits. Wow, That\'s all I can say, the salad was on point with fresh greens and fresh green apples, and the chicken was soft, tender, juicy and surprisingly not greasy. Please note the chicken is bigger then it looks and 100% Protein, so it was very filling.'], ['107530534188116227736_6045a46e604fc398f591eb09', 'For this visit I decided on the BBQ platter with BBQChicken, PulledPork, Brisket and a side of SouthernSlaw !! Every component of the meal, the Chicken, for example, was very delicately smoked as to not to dry on the inside and too full of smoke flavour.'], ['107530534188116227736_604b1747d2eb6e0d32ff8112', "Burger Nirvana. . Golden is such a great town with so much to offer. What can really put a town on the Foodie Radar is a having a great burger joint. Bob's Atomic Burger does not disappoint. Simplistic in its approach to the art of the burger, Bobs has a small menu, with plenty of add-ons. Bob's keeps' its approach to the burger easy for the burger novice and the burger expert. First, off you pick your protein, whether its plant-based, bird-based or beef-based, Bob's selections are easy to navigate. The selections are beef, grilled chicken, fried chicken, quinoa patty and they have  Nathans hot dogs too. next up you pick your bun, your toppings, your cheese and then one of the hearty sides. Keeping the menu simple, you have fresh hand cuts fries, sweet potato fries, onion petals and you pick a small or large size. My choice on this visit was a Classic Hamburger with the classic trifecta of Lettuce, Tomato, Onions and good 'ole fresh locally sourced bacon with a slice of Pepper-jack cheese.. I asked for my fries to be well-done so they have a little crispness to them and topped with off with typical condiments. To conclude, Bobs is a great little spot for grabbing a very well-made burger with plenty of toppings and accoutrements to satisfy your burger craving."], ['107530534188116227736_604391a6ad733fba1bcfdade', 'For my starter I had the insanely good Edamame Dumplings, a Vegan dish made with dashi, white truffle oil, and asian herbs. Next up was the Ancient Grains bowl made with miso, sesame, glazed sweet potato, turmeric, charred onion, snow pea, grilled portobello, avocado, hemp seed and I added some grass-fed steak too, to make even better.'], ['107530534188116227736_60411beac6fcf1fddba11516', "I did not get to try too many of the menu items but our server suggested I try the Camarones La Plancha, which consisted of grilled prawns marinated in La Pinata's Special garlic sauce. review_text: Outstanding fried chicken. Pies & Thighs is a Williamsburg staple that stands true to the name in delivering mouth watering fried chicken and homemade pies. The fried goodness is crispy, well seasoned and juicy to the bite. I recommend the three piece meal which comes with two sides and a flakey, buttery biscuit. Speaking of sides, youll have several worthy options to pair with your poultry. I am a big fan of the collard greens which have a hearty, meaty seasoning and are well salted. In addition, the macaroni and cheese is deliciously simple and pairs supremely well with any chicken dish. Dont even think about asking for the bill without trying a slice of pie. The pies taste like theyve been prepared by somebodys grandma, cooking with a recipe thats been in the family for generations. I recommend the classic apple, but you cant miss with any of their delicious options. Pies & Thighs is perfect whenever you have a hankering for fried chicken or feel like devouring well prepared (and well priced) fatty, comfort meal.
history_reviews: [['104285062634756642667_6054877d80c04bd7072f25b8', "Pizzeria in Carroll Gardens know for absolutely lip smacking delicious brick oven calzones and pizzas. Once youve finally been seated, your choices couldnt be any easier, the menu offers two dishes: pizza and calzone, or my personal favorite, both. We started our meal with the calzone, which was the highlight of the meal and is clearly in a league of its own. The calzones are generously stuffed with ricotta, mozzarella, and red sauce along with whichever additional toppings you choose to have baked into this luscious treat. The calzone is prepared with a ton of love and genuine expertise, you somehow manage to still feel like an adult as youre devouring this classic childhood dish. Youll enjoy every hearty bite as well as each emphatic dunk of your calzone into the sweet red sauce as garnish. As for the pies, theyre prepared with the same expertise and love, however they fall a tad short of the calzone in overall satisfaction. Its tough for pizza to truly standout in NYC considering there are so many Goliath's that make otherworldly pies, that said, this is still a worthy option. The pie is slathered with the homemade red sauce and peppered with both low moisture mozzarella and buffalo mozzarella, which is delicious. The pizza is garnished with a heap of fresh basil whichs adds a pleasant earthiness to the meal. I recommend adding some garlic and at least one more topping to the pie to maximize your experience."], ['104285062634756642667_605488427fec92c07c6440b9', 'Pennsy offers several notable dining options, including a personal favorite, Pat LaFriedas meat purveyors. The bar has a rotating top of NY beers and regional favorites. Youll find plenty of seating and bar space within the food hall along with additional seating options on the outdoor terrance.'], ['104285062634756642667_60435f27ad733fba1bcfd098', 'As you bite into the dumpling, savory flavors invade your mouth as the soup is blitzes your taste buds and paves the way for the delivery of the tender pork. Aside from their famous soup dumplings, they offer creative variations on classic Chinese dishes but Id recommend trying their Shanghai pan fried noodles.'], ['104285062634756642667_60560255f69c7b117806fe51', 'Shake Shack is a NY born and bred, fast food chain that specializes in fresh beef burgers and delicious milk shakes. The burger scene is competitive in NYC but given its natural limitations to compete with the heavyweight champs (JG Melon, PJ Clarkes, etc.) this is the best fast food burger in the city. The beef is sourced locally from Pat LaFrieda meat purveyors which is the trademark of their tasty creations. The burgers are cooked medium and are dressed with lettuce, tomato and shack sauce.'], ['104285062634756642667_604a81acc6dc737bce7e5b7f', 'One of the oldest pizzerias in NYC and a great take on a New York slice. Grimaldis prepares their pizzas in a large brick oven, which leaves the pizza with an authentic and rustic taste. Top 5 NYC pizza, in my opinion.'], ['104285062634756642667_604c38db77e81aaed3cc9d7f', 'Burger & Barrel Winepub is an excellent burger joint that also offers impressive wine pairings to satiate your palate. No item on the menu is merely present to check the box, so when you find the Fried Chicken sandwich or Prime Rib starting back at you, its totally safe to devour something that isnt the burger. I highly recommend the Kung Pow Chicken Lollipops for starters, they have an unbelievable tang flavor that accompanies the slight heat that the appetizer presents. Youll be shocked to hear that the burgers are noteworthy. First off, Im a fan of any establishment that uses Pat LaFrieda beef because its a clear sign that the establishment is committed to quality. As for their slew of burgers, all are solid but B&B has built a reputation around the city for its Bash Burger. The burger has been named a 6x New York Wine & Food Festival Winner for best burger. The Bash Burger is graced with caramelized onions, bacon jam, gooey American cheese and their special sauce served on brioche bun. Its a great tasting burger, my only reservation is the bun to meat ratio which I feel could be improved to favore the beef. If youre looking for a burger with more heft, try the Double Barrel burger which comes with two meat patties. As a final touch, all of the burgers are served with a few onion rings for good measure and a healthy portion of crispy fries. Burger & Barrel Winepub is a great burger alternative in a city that is saturated in burger options that differentiates itself with a well balanced menu.'], ['104285062634756642667_60444dc5cc4f7990c6579f42', 'Youre in for a treat...Emilys is a boutique pizzeria, based in Clinton Hill, that has built a tremendous reputation for their creative combination of toppings, flavors, and textures that grace their scrumptious pies. Surprisingly, Emilys is famous for crafting one of the best burgers in the city, the Emmy Burger. The burger is prepared with Pat LaFrieda dry aged beef, sweet caramelized onions, American cheese, EMMY sauce while sandwiches together wonderfully between a pretzel bun. Their burger is juicy, savory, and extremely flavorful. It seriously makes you wonder how Emilys is better known for the pizza! The pro-tip is to order a pie and a burger, which is perfect for two people. Weve discussed the burger at the pizza joint, lets dissect the greatness of their signature dish. Emily classifies its pies in four categories: red, pink, green, and white which translates to a number of offerings based in tomato, vodka, tomatillo, and cheese sauces. All of their creations are masterfully architected with a unique blend of toppings, like a pepperoni pie drizzled with honey (dont question it, just order). While all of the pies are tasty in their own right, I have an affinity for The Colony (red), The Big Ang (pink), and The Emily (white). Emilys an up and coming pizzeria giant in the city and is perfect for virtually any occasion.']]

history_reviews: [['111217793845808378532_604a9f57c6dc737bce7e5c77', 'If its your desire to enter a crazy Italian food fantasy land, Eataly is the place to go. Id like to tell you they have hot and cold running pasta, and its probably true, but there is so much Italian goodness going on in this place, you wont have the chance to experience all of it in one visit. After wandering like tourists through the aisle of Eataly, already on sensory overload, we got in the long line to eat at La Pizza & La Pasta, on the second floor at Eataly in the back. I had the Margherita Pizza. The gluten-free marinara pizza served without cheese had my wife questioning her very reality. Our son is a plain pasta kind of guy (sighwe didnt raise him right) So thats what he got. I tried a noodle and the flavor was good but it was a little over cooked. We also had fresh mozzarella served with beets, pistachio pesto and squash (you get to pick any three items to accompany the burrata). La Pizza & La Pasta was definitely worth the wait. Eataly on its own is well worth a visit with its coffee stations, separate pizza restaurant, bread, cheeses, olive oils, gelato, pastries etcWe cant wait to come back.'], ['111217793845808378532_6055148ed335d0abfb415732', 'I had spaghetti with the vegan eggplant based meatballs. Ive been a vegetarian for decades and I really dont remember ever having a plate of spaghetti and meatballsalso I really generally dont like eggplantthis whole thing was delicious and the meatballs gave a very nice meat-like texture. (And it turned out the slight modification she wanted to the gluten free version of their special pomodoro pasta was gluten free (she also wanted it without cheese) and she thought it was well done. (Not always an easy feat with gluten free pasta.)'], ['111217793845808378532_60487b0cf9e05764f1fa5494', 'These were all around delicious and filling. . My wife got the Hongos tostada which came with an extra layer of delicious black retried beans. So we get confused when theres a placed called Bakersfield since already have a city called that hereand on top of which they serve tacos, and our streets are lined with tacosahoy Southern Californians, Bakersfield residents and all taco lovers everywherethese are the tacos you are looking for. The tortillas are all house-made. Actually everything is house made, the salsa, the tortilla chipseverything. There are good and tasty vegetarian options including the blackbeans, one of the salads, a Tostada option and 2 different tacos. I had both of the vegetarian tacos, the Hongos (portobello mushrooms, various peppers, a kale slaw and cotija cheese), and the Huitlacoche (corn truffles [which is actually a kind of mushroom], peppers corn, onion, cilantro and cotija cheese. They were a little similar, both being mushroom based and I ended up having a second hongos. Chips and guacamole was $8 with salsa or $3 with just salsa and no guacamole. The red sauce has a nice smokiness to it. They also do a nightly shot special with a premium liqueurin this case it was a Camarea Tequila shot. In general you cant go wrong with a three dollar tequila shot, but the fact that its a premium curated liqueur really brings it up a few notches. And although we didnt get one, the Margaritas we saw walking by are served in Mason jars and looked amazing. Please send us your fine tacos to Southern California.'], ['111217793845808378532_60473872b1a0aaee3eef862f', "It was the traditional last night before Passover starts pizza offering, and this was our choice. Unfortunately this wine  Also, the line was served in plastic cups which was strange. For an Italian restaurant, which theoretically has lots of vegetarian options, this place wasn't particularly vegetarian friendly. For example they had many many salad options most of which automatically had chicken in them. I'm sure you could order it without the chicken but if you're going to have such an extensive salad menu, shouldn't you have vegetarians in mind in the choices that you offer as defaults? Our kid had the macaroni and cheese. The macaroni wasn't particularly good and the fries, where is they looked good, were coated in something. Rule of thumb for french fries  if you can't make decent regular french fries, and have to rely on coding them in something, you shouldn't be offering french fries at your restaurant. Also rule of thumb for macaroni and cheese for kidsit should always be the basic mac and cheese. If a kid doesnt like your mac and cheese, you have strayed in the wrong direction. Most of us were sharing a large cheese pizza. The first pizza came out under done, the crust was mushy. One of us got their gluten-free pizza. Kudos to you Biaggios for offering gluten-free crust, however you did get the order wrongit was ordered without cheese and, sure enough, came with cheese. Also the mushrooms topping tasted canned. Canned vegetables of any kind do not make for good tasting pizza."], ['111217793845808378532_604a4d8c1ec03878d66c8387', 'They have lots of vegetarian choices which are helpfully labeled as such on the menu, which includes crispy tacos enchiladas and more. At least three of the tacos were vegetarian as were some of the happy hour specials. I ordered the Emmas Choice where you get to choose tier favorite puffy taco (I chose the poblano mushroom from the happy hour menu served puffy style with cheese) and your choice of an enchilada (I chose the spinach). The taco on its own was very filling albeit a bit oily.'], ['111217793845808378532_604ffeb688c7af3f893e688c', 'I started with the Strawberry and Tomato Gazpacho (without the halibut it came with), dressed with sungold and marigold flowers. I also had a side of Tater Tots. For my main I had the (also seasonal) Local Foraged Mushroom Stroganoff. This was a fresh pappardelle with Hen of the Woods mushrooms and Creme Freche. The fresh pappardelle was too al dente and the sauce was a little too tart. My wife had the Green Salad with Goat Cheese. The goat cheese was on the rim and around the inside of bowl and was really tasty. I had the goat cheese with rhubarb leather, sweet crunchy hazelnut crumbles, and pickled rhubarb. (And as I mentioned as of this writing the seasonal menu has changed and theres a completely different vegetarian pasta offering so its well worth revisiting this menu as the seasons change.'], ['111217793845808378532_6044576d27f39b7b5d1dc487', 'First, they gave us free bruschetta because it was our first time. I had the spaghetti marinara as I was in the mood for something hearty tasting and classic! Our kid liked his pasta and they gave us a free side of carrots. So kudos to Maggianos for the free carrots! Also, and this is wild, unique, and made us feel like wed won the pasta lottery, when you order a pasta they give you another one for free to take home. A WHOLE OTHER FREE PASTA DISH packaged to go home with you! It was also nice that they had a gluten-free option for the pasta, although it wasnt my wifes favorite gluten free pasta ever.'], ['111217793845808378532_605314b811a96a1e3740a521', 'I started with a Honey Nut Old Fashioned - It was a good drink, well mixed, with peanuts in it and the unique flavor of Peanut Honey Bourbon. My wife and I shared the Brussels Sprouts Four Ways. 3 of the ways look similar to each other and one looks different, so we actually had to count the ways to make sure we had all fourthere was smoked, pickled, fried and what wed call overdressed. We also had the Stout Gingerbread Carrotsall three of these words are divine on their own, together, they created a new carrot mecca  The dish was not overly sweet and looked yummy, though we would have preferred slightly more al-dente carrotsoverall it came together nicely. I loved the Castle Valley Mills Farrowit served as a hearty main for just me (its on the small plates menu) It included mushroom, asparagus, cherry tomato, roasted fennel, poached egg, pine nuts. My wife had the Charred Asparagus Salad for her main. She said it was a delicious salad with a beautifully poached egg on the top. Not on the main, but reason enough to come to this restaurant are the French Fries.'], ['111217793845808378532_604a9f18b1a0aaee3eefbd41', 'There is a great pizza war waging in the United States with two opposing forcesthe lovers of Chicago style deep dish pizza, and New York style thin crust (though a Lyft driver I had recently assured me that New York style pizza is really from Connecticut..or was at least perfected there.) The New Yorkians will, without hesitation, tell you that Chicago style pizza is not pizza. The Chicagonians pretty much dont care, as long as they can keep eating their, unique, butter crust, deep dish phenomenons. In my world, this is like comparing apples and orangesthe 2 are different entitiesthere is excellent New York style pizza.and there is excellent Chicago style pizza. Masa of Echo Park is the only place (I know of) that you can get truly authentic and really good Chicago style deep-dish pizza. Sure, there are plenty of places that offer deep-dishbut to be truly authentic Chicago, its got to be more than thick doughyouve got to, as Masa does, use a buttery, somewhere between pizza dough and biscuit, crust. Youve got to put the cheese in first, then the toppings and sauce so the cheese seals the dough (and rises in bits through the sea of sauce to the top. Masa does all of this and provides the authentic Chicago pizza experience youre looking for. (Even if youre only looking for it sometimesmy mouth and belly have equal joy for authentic NY slices and occasionally I start thinking about real Chicago pizza and I just need it.) Masa is the real deal. Even my 9 year old who famously doesnt like anything besides plain pasta found his Plain-Jane pizza astonishingly good. If youre looking for authentic, and super good Chicago deep dish pizza in Los Angeles.'], ['111217793845808378532_604ae3fcb1a0aaee3eefbf28', 'I started with the Smoke Rings Cocktail (it was mandatory [in my mind] that every drink in Kentucky was bourbon based, if not straight up Bourbon. I also had the Chilled Carrot Soup (Another common element amongst the various 21c Hotel restaurants is a different chilled soup in the summer) This wasnt sweet like I thought it might be, but had lots and lots of flavors, all goodThis was a unique to eat a soup where different bites tasted differentlyI liked it a lot. I had the Ricotta Cavatalli pasta dish (no longer on the menu as I write this). It was also really good with lots of flavor, perfectly cooked pasta, and a nice lemon flavor to it. My wife had the Roasted Heirloom Squash - She said Last Years Tomato Jam was the star of this nice and satisfying dish. She thought the tamale part tasted good but the consistency was slightly off for being called a tamalea little too wet/thin. Other vegetarian options were available, including cheeses, grits and various veggie sides. I closed out with the Raspberry Fig Mousse dessert which sounded and was amazinga lavender honey infused house made gelatoa thin pretzel-like (but sweet) cracker surrounding the fig mousse. Oh multi-colored penguins of the worldwere coming for you.'], ['111217793845808378532_6052bc96f09a4ffff042fc13', "Its a pull apart bread with cheddar cheese baked in, and served with choices of dipping sauces (marinara, garlic butter, and ranch). I also have the Veggie Steak Tacos. I asked about this and apparently they deep fry the Salei steak which, if you're familiar at all with cooking faux-meats, you probably know it's not what you wanna do, since those items tend to over cook very easily."], ['111217793845808378532_60496137b1a0aaee3eefadda', 'I landed on the street tacos, choosing the portobello mushroom as the filling.'], ['111217793845808378532_60410deac6fcf1fddba10f64', "For example my wife wanted an omelette with avocado and wanted no meat in it. review_text: Tacos y Birria el Guero is a low-key taqueria sharing a parking lot with a nail spa in Santa Ana. I love their "Asada Taco." Like most carne asada street-style tacos, it features thinly-sliced marinated beef mixed with chopped onions and cilantro deposited into back-to-back double corn tortillas. For as much as I believe typical carne asada to be a grossly overrated taco filling, this is the good stuff, the Hennessy XO of carne asada. There is a smooth and tasty avocado-chile salsa at the salsa bar that this taco wears perfectly. The "Birria de Res Taco" is also quite fantastic. This taco features juicy braised beef rib meat pervaded with small luscious specks of salty fat. I drizzled some of the Salsa de Aceite (spicy chile oil) onto this taco and it dialed up the intensity and heat of the birria considerably.
history_reviews: [['108685370139018629938_6051f93188c7af3f893e7394', "I ordered the 2 piece Chicken Meal with Mashed Potatoes ($6.95) with a pint of beer. Beyond the dryness, the chicken had an extremely salty, thin crust. The thin texture of the fried batter was similar to KFC's Original Recipe. Make no mistake though, the Colonel is like Escoffier next to Chicken Charlie. I haven't yet mentioned the mashed potatoes and gravy, WHICH WERE MADE WITH SPOILED DAIRY AND TASTED RANCID!"], ['108685370139018629938_6055afe397d555cc6fb0ce6f', "One of San Diego's finest taco shops. Try the carnitas here. Cabeza tacos are also excellent."], ['108685370139018629938_6045b409604fc398f591ecf7', 'The pork burrito is great, consisting of shredded pork stewed in spices accompanied by cotija cheese and lettuce, wrapped in a homemade lard-heavy flour tortilla. The gloriously greasy rolled tacos are also a good choice, featuring meat in a crispy rolled tortilla shell, deep fried, and then smothered with queso fresco and crema.'], ['108685370139018629938_60421d502e57ebdea29c81eb', 'Yes, it\'s a real good burger, think "In-N-Out Burger on Steroids" - but Hodad\'s kitchen and wait staff, mostly stoned out of their ever-loving skulls, operate on "beach time." This slo-mo style doesn\'t quite scale up to the immense demand for their burgers due to the massive amount of media exposure they\'ve gotten both locally as a long-time beloved San Diego beach staple and nationally on Food Network and other outlets. As for the burgers? I typically order the "Single Bacon Cheeseburger," which is the house specialty if there is one. I sometimes need to compress the burger with my hands a bit before trying to eat it, otherwise I cannot fit enough of it into my mouth to take a proper bite. Like I said, it\'s a real good burger. In fact, this is the quintessential American burger turned up to "11." I usually get my burger with a "basket combo," so that it includes Hodad\'s crispy thick-cut French fries, which are some of my favorite fries in all of San Diego due to their crunchy skin, soft hot innards, and near-perfect amount of seasoning. All everyone talks about are Hodad\'s burgers and shakes, leaving their fries underrated.'], ['108685370139018629938_6046d164b0e2129e475356f6', 'We also both enjoy the "Baja Ceviche," where each ingredient (shrimp, fish, crab) is distinct, but work delectably well together. Perhaps our favorite appetizer is the "Smoked Fish Tacos," essentially smoked fish hash piped into egg-roll-like taco shells. If you\'re looking for something more traditional, try the "Salt and Pepper Calamari." My entre recommendation is the Miso-Glazed Sea Bass with Crab Fried Rice, which is an extraordinary dish that is similar to Nobu\'s Miso-Marinated Black Cod. The flavoring aside, the fish preparation at Truluck\'s is top notch, and the sea bass is moist, firm-fleshed, and cooked to a level where it remains mild and delicate. The crab fried rice is lightly flavored in what I can only describe as "essence" of crab, and complements the sea bass perfectly. If you\'re not ordering the sea bass, then try the "South African Lobster Tail" if it is on the menu. South African lobsters are sweeter than normal lobsters, and here they do all of the work of de-shelling the massive 12 ounce tail, and setting it aside a substantial portion of parmesan mashed potatoes and steamed asparagus.'], ['108685370139018629938_6051045f5b4ccec8d5cae9d5', 'I recommend the mushroom chicken dish first and foremost, though the tamales and the tacos (blackened fish especially) are excellent as well.'], ['108685370139018629938_60489685b3f169c178160577', 'Mitla Caf\'s tacos are the foundation of the Taco Bell empire. As you first bite into one of Mitla Caf\'s Beef Tacos (labeled as just "Taco" on the menu), you can\'t help but think of a Taco Bell\'s taco, except done 100 times better. As grease and juices fall out of the house-made misshapen fried tortilla, you\'ll taste the heavily-browned and spiced ground beef covered with shredded cheddar cheese, refreshing lettuce, and bright red tomatoes, and you will understand why someone would start a fast food company around this. Sometimes it\'s better to be lucky than good, because for as many billions of dollars that the Taco Bell brand is worth, Glen Bell ultimately failed to capture what makes this taco work. Mitla Caf\'s "Shredded Beef Taco" is probably a better taco than their regular "Taco," but it doesn\'t channel the same kind of nostalgia. The "Shredded Beef Taco" does, however, have a cleaner flavor and truer purity of purpose. Either taco greatly benefits from the red sauce (you need to ask for a side of it when you order), a fiery salsa that puts Taco Bell\'s little spicy ketchup packets to shame. During my visit, I also ordered the Pozole, which is served white (i.e. Pozole Blanco), with minimal garnishes (no oregano, for example), and pork that was over-cooked. My advice is to pass on the Pozole and eat more tacos. In fact, always eat more tacos.'], ['108685370139018629938_604e0a1471ced5c7554dda32', "I came here seeking the Korean Fried Chicken and the Panko-Crusted Japanese Fried Chicken. Both were boneless, sufficiently moist, and tasty. The Korean variant had been subjected to a char-sui/teriyaki-like magenta glaze before deep-frying, resulting in a piece of chicken tinged in a pleasant sweetness that didn't really need any saucing. Nonetheless, I enjoyed the sweet soy-infused katsu sauce, but didn't care as much for the lava sauce, which tasted like sweet and sour ketchup and, despite its name, didn't actually deliver any heat. Macaroni Salad is delicious -- much moreso than the Green Salad which is overpowered by an aggressively dark sesame-flavored dressing. The Malasadas (Portuguese fried dough) are also legit here, a great way to end your meal, even if they're not the larger, thinner variety I grew up with."], ['108685370139018629938_60561c8d97d555cc6fb0d0f3', 'My visit was short and I dined solo at the bar, eating some nigiri (Otoro and Hamachi) in addition to the Rock Shrimp Tempura.'], ['108685370139018629938_604da44a77e81aaed3cca9df', 'During my first trip here, I ordered the "Crispy Chicken Sandwich." I wish I had more fried chicken like this in my life, but I can\'\'t afford to. Yes, this is one of the best chicken sandwiches I\'ve had anywhere, but is it worth the $18 price tag? I am confident, however, that the juiciness of the chicken, the sturdy and well-seasoned fried batter, the creamy cole slaw, the earthy swiss cheese, and the fresh sesame-coated roll combine to make this almost as perfect as a fried chicken sandwich can be. Lastly, I had the "Honor Burger" on my second visit, which is a burger topped with a condiment mix that reminded me of Burger King\'s Whopper, but produced by a professional cook. The meat, ordered and prepared medium rare, had plenty of life in it and is not entirely overwhelmed by the melted cheddar, mix of slaw, special sauce, and tomatoes, but I feel they could scale down the condiment-to-beef ratio just a tad and have twice as good of a burger.'], ['108685370139018629938_60412b777cd8bf1303623e48', 'Hambone\'s is a popular BBQ joint in Bellflower owned and operated by pitmaster Kenny Hamilton who has come to Los Angeles via Mississippi. What drew me here was that this is one of the restaurants around south Los Angeles that sells what has become known as "black tacos," which refer to tacos sold by black-owned businesses to predominantly black customers. Hambone\'s serves a very basic "black taco" with chopped barbecued meat with sauce on flour tortillas, dressed with lettuce, shredded yellow cheese, and diced tomatoes. I was a bit bummed on account of not being able to taste the difference between the "Pulled Pork Taco" from the "Beef Tri-Tip Taco" due to the BBQ sauce on the meats being so sweet and pervasive that it made both tacos taste the same. My fascination with "black tacos" aside, I could smell Hambone\'s hickory-smoked meats from my car as I entered the parking lot, which put me in a mood to have something more substantial than a taco. I\'m often disappointed in Southern California\'s BBQ restaurants, so I crossed my fingers as I ordered a "Half Rack of Spare Ribs." The ribs were neatly trimmed in a way that made me a little skeptical (in my experience, "pretty BBQ" is usually bad BBQ), but only in the brief moment before I began eating them. I was delighted by a persistent hickory flavor throughout textured, dense pork that cleanly snaps off the bone with a tug of your teeth. My biggest fault is that, like the taco meats, these ribs are heavily sauced with a thin glaze that is sweet and sticky, reminding me of an Asian-style sauce one would eat on the magenta-hued spare ribs found in Cantonese restaurants across America. Don\'t get me wrong, the sauce tastes fine -- I just wish there was less of it and that I had an opportunity to apply it myself. It\'s a shame, because Hamilton is proud of his rub and speaks of if it as his most secret of weapons, but I could not discern where the rub stops and the sauce begins, and the sauce made everything sooooo sweet. I also ordered "Collard Greens" that were flat greens heaped on one other -- again, almost "too neat-looking" for collards -- but nonetheless tender, piquant, filled with pork flavor, and just a touch of acid. On the whole, a pretty good BBQ spot.'], ['108685370139018629938_6049809fb1a0aaee3eefaf8b', 'TJ Oyster Bar is a family-run San Diego mariscos institution that has been in operation since opening up a small restaurant in Bonita in 2002 and subsequently expanding with two additional locations in South Bay. I began my recent visit with their "Aguachile Verde," a traditional preparation of raw shrimp, cucumbers, and red onions cured in lime juice with serrano chiles. The spicy and sour broth would endear itself with Wilbur Scoville and is not to be trifled with -- it will not only clear out your sinuses but melt them down as well. The flavor is off the hook, and I could eat a bowl of just the red onions marinated in this aguachile broth. Save some for your tacos. I give two thumbs (eight arms?) up to the "Octopus Taco," a petite corn tortilla stuffed with grilled chopped tentacle that is slightly sticky and slightly charred, sweet and chewy, but crispy-edged. Despite this stuff being nothing short of creamy heroin, it is wisely applied sparingly on this taco. Cilantro and onions round out a wonderful octopus-forward taco that you\'ll remember for its chunks of meat rather than its garnishments. The "Grilled Fish Taco" is the same as the "Octopus Taco," but with very soft grilled fish instead. If you must do one or the other, go octopus. I suggest adding TJ Oyster Bar\'s salsa roja to these tacos. Like the other tacos served at TJ Oyster Bar, the "Baja Fish Taco" is compact and petite, but it is everything a fish taco ought to be: crunchy beer-battered fried fish, reasonably ratio\'d vegetal accoutrements (cabbage, onion, tomato, cilantro), and the mysterious white sauce. The tortilla could be better, but wherever they source them from do a decent job as packaged tortillas go -- you can taste and smell corn in them, as you should. The last taco I tried was the "Shrimp Taqueso," which is similar to a "taco gobernador" in that it consists of shrimp that have been grilled so their surfaces brown in a corn tortilla with melted cheese. It was alright, kind of a shrimp quesadilla de maiz. This taco needed something else to really "pop," and I would suggest going full-on gobernador-style with sauted veggies, or providing chipotle sauce on the side. The tortilla is grilled to melt the cheese and make the taco sturdier, which I appreciated because I could sense that this gooey filling, combined with gravity, would otherwise be determined to fall all over my shirt. As with the other tacos, using the salsa roja available here is recommended.'], ['108685370139018629938_6041b9cfc6fcf1fddba14afb', 'For me, there is no more interesting "regional" taco in Los Angeles than the "black taco," a type of taco that has been invented and evolved over the past 40+ years in black neighborhoods located within the urban sprawl beginning in South Central Los Angeles and ending in Compton. Black tacos have their own unique distinctive style, look, taste, and nomenclature, yet are not found outside of this micro-region. Don\'t get me wrong, there are different varieties of black tacos, but the basics are a tortilla (usually a white corn tortilla, but flour can be used as well) filled with ground beef or turkey, lots of shredded yellow cheese, lettuce, diced tomatoes, and either sour cream or some kind of sweet barbecue-like "sauce" or both. There are no onions or cilantro in a typical black taco. Sr. Cliff\'s "Turkey Taco" is what I just described, with seasoned clumps of ground turkey that are grilled until they\'re browned and deposited into a soft corn tortilla with tomatoes, cheese, lettuce, and sour cream. Sr. Cliff\'s can also serve their tacos with onions and cilantro on double corn tortillas, eschewing all of the other toppings. I ordered a "Ground Beef Taco" of this variety, and it was exactly what you would expect it to be, though the grilling technique that Sr. Cliff\'s cooks use for their ground meats imparts plenty of flavor due to the thick browning picked up through the process. Nonetheless, these are not much more than the kind of tacos that have made billions of dollars over the past 80 years for General Mills\' "Old El Paso" brand. However, the combination of soul food and Mexican food on the menus of black-owned restaurants continues to evolve black tacos in South L.A. and Compton. The "Soul Man Taco" served at Sr. Cliff\'s uses pastrami in addition to ground beef for its meat, and has similar toppings to their regular black taco, but it also comes with a legit salsa roja on the side that wouldn\'t be out of place in a Boyle Heights taqueria. Indeed, Sr. Cliff\'s "Soul Man Taco" veers towards an intriguing direction for black tacos, using and combining ingredients that one wouldn\'t think to combine in a taco, but make sense due to local culture. Sr. Cliff\'s may not have invented the black taco, nor do they make the best black taco in L.A., but this is probably the best restaurant to go to for understanding what black tacos are, and how they have become essential eats in the communities they can be found in.'], ['108685370139018629938_60458393882f4d1caf5fd86a', 'Like many barbecue restaurants across the country, Phil\'s uses mesquite wood in the preparation of their meat dishes. The ribs, tri-tip, chicken, and pulled pork offered at Phil\'s are not "mesquite smoked," (which requires a unique skill-set, aptitude, patience, and expertise) but rather they are baked in an oven, slathered in sweet sauce to cover up any problems, and then "mesquite grilled." This is a key distinction, because one method is American BBQ, and the other is not. I don\'t know why anyone would go to Phil\'s BBQ more than once. Sticky and dirty silverware, sticky and dirty floors, sticky and dirty table tops. Also, I may like your potato salad more, by the way, if you actually bothered to fully cook the potatoes and apply appropriate seasoning. Your beef ribs would be better if they weren\'t so difficult to bite into with human teeth, and your baby backs would improve if you stopped cooking them past the point of cosmic heat death. I\'d consider not spitting your onion rings into my napkin if they were fried in such a way that the fried coating did not taste and feel like stale cereal. Imma give Phil\'s a decent rating. Take your 3 stars, Phil\'s BBQ.'], ['108685370139018629938_6055f35e97d555cc6fb0cfc5', 'Yes, the Al Pastor Taco from the Ave 26 Taco Stand, on any given day, could be just as good as an Al Pastor Taco from Leo\'s Taco Truck, or my long-time personal favorite down in San Diego, Tacos El Gordo. What could put it over the edge are the grilled onions cooked down until they sweeten and begin to caramelize, then blended with the meat carved from the trompo. You could be completely satisfied  NO, captivated  by a taco filled with ONLY the Al Pastor pork, without any additional sauces or garnishments. However, I recommend the chopped raw onions and cilantro from the salsa bar, and it would be criminal to not add at least a bit of Ave 26\'s rousing salsa roja. It will reinforce to you that you are indeed eating legit "street tacos as opposed to the heavily-garnished crapola fraudulently peddled as "street tacos" on this side of the border.'], ['108685370139018629938_6049ae05d4b3ada4982e7ab2', 'These are outstanding, plump diver scallops that taste as clean as the plate beneath them. The accompaniments change from season-to-season, with my favorite being the vinegar-spiked frise and chorizo salad with roasted fingerling potatoes. But Mrs. K and I prefer to order their "Cheese Plate," which is always satisfying, and consists of a sharp blue cheese, a funky soft cheese (such as camembert), and a piece of hard, nutty cheese with notes of caramel or butterscotch (like an aged gouda or comt).'], ['108685370139018629938_604979f4aaa2b0649c59c08e', 'Burritos La Palma is a tough restaurant for me to review, because they are such a unique operation, and they do a few key things unexpectedly well. Rather than a deep-dive into why this Zacatecan restaurant serves slender burritos that can fit into one\'s palm that many people (myself included) also would consider to be tacos, I\'ll simply leave it at that. Also, I\'ll save the burrito history lesson for another review. And as much as other reviewers and food critics alike want to write about how Burritos La Palma somehow brought beef birria to Southern California, this notion is mistaken and, in fact, not even close to being accurate -- but since I don\'t have a better or more definitive answer, I\'m avoiding that one as well. The first burrito I tried at Burritos La Palma was their "Tinga de Pollo Burrito." The chicken tinga recipe they use here results in a juicy, mildly-spiced tinga that is dominated by pork nectar and smokiness from its chipotle chiles. It is a messy, drippy guisado that demands a strong tortilla. The hand-pressed flour tortillas used at Burritos La Palma are based on a family recipe and are indeed both stout and fantastic: substantial, moist, a little chewy, with a flavor that makes me think "biscuits" not "burritos." The "Birria, Frijoles y Queso Burrito" makes even better use of the tortilla: they lay it on a griddle for a bit to help melt the cheese inside the burrito. The toasted surface creates a different flavor and texture on one side of the burrito, making it distinctively quirky. The feisty beef birria inside is well-spiced and decadently soft. The combination of their beef birria, refried beans, and salty, creamy queso in their half-toasted flour tortilla creates a whole that is superior to the the sum of its parts. I would avoid ordering the "Flautas de Maiz," basically bone-dry taquitos with a small bit of shredded beef and a mild runny green sauce on it. As with many taquitos, the predominant flavor of these flautas was the deep-fried corn tortilla shell. This dish desperately needs more meat and less tortilla. I wanted to throw something when I realized the same restaurant that makes wonderful little burritos was also capable of producing something like this. Burritos La Palma now operates several stores across L.A. county and Orange County, but this location in El Monte is their original restaurant that opened in 2012. Upon completion of my visit here, I found that the hype and praise this operation receives is legitimate, and next time I\'ll solely stick to the burritos, which is what I advise you to do as well.'], ['108685370139018629938_604a46831ec03878d66c834c', 'My first steak here was the classic "Tournedos Rossini": a butter-basted rare filet mignon served on a crouton, topped with seared foie gras, finished with a Madeira demi-glace sauce, and garnished with shaved black truffles. The whole of this is a buttery, well-crusted steak supported by strong complimentary flavors that will leave you wondering why every steakhouse doesn\'t serve this dish. On my second visit, I enjoyed an 8-ounce "Miyazaki A5 New York Strip," a pre-sliced Japanese black wagyu steak that may be the best steak I\'ve eaten in San Diego, with only Provisional\'s Hokkaido A5 challenging it. You can\'t go wrong with Born & Raised\'s "Coal-Roasted Leeks," or the crispy "Charred Broccoli," or especially the baked breadcrumb-covered "Mac & Cheese" with its tangy mix of cheddar and gruyere cheeses. But my favorite side was the half-pound "Butter-Poached Lobster," a pricey but worthwhile indulgence of melted butter riding on the back of expertly cooked, taut lobster tail meat.'], ['108685370139018629938_6056600f3019cb0a47838d06', "Knowing that the restaurant's chef de cuisine, Scott Pajak, is a Buffalo native, I ordered the Signature Stadium Buffalo Wings. Having attended college in western New York, I'm picky when it comes to buffalo wings and consider any wings I've ever eaten on the west coast to be substandard -- until now. Chef Pajak's wings are massive, have an ultra-crispy skin (sans breading, of course), with moist, juicy white meat inside. The sauce was a just a tad sweeter and thinner than most buffalo sauces I remember from the east coast, the heat level was right, and most importantly the sauce tightly clung to the wings. The creamy dipping sauce, made of Point Reyes' award-winning blue cheese and loaded with garlic, was a nice touch. These were certainly the best wings I've had west of the Mississippi River. I somewhat enjoyed the Spicy Meatloaf Po Boy, which featured meatloaf, a spicy ketchup/BBQ sauce, fontina cheese, black pepper mayonnaise, lettuce, pickle, and tomato on a New Orleans-style French bread roll. While not the best meatloaf sandwich I ever had, it had good enough flavor, and made for a satisfying lunch."], ['108685370139018629938_604dacb677e81aaed3ccaa20', 'Guerrilla Taco\'s chicano chef, Wes Avila, is a taquero after my heart, proudly declaring his own food "inauthentic," and having been quoted as saying "I couldn\'t give a sh*t about authenticity, especially when it comes to tacos. The truth is, there\'s no such thing as an authentic taco." The name "Guerrilla Tacos" was the idea of Avila\'s wife, as he was constantly threatened with being shutdown in his early days as a less-than-legal food stand prior to opening this brick and mortar restaurant in the Arts District, now possibly the most well-known and critically-acclaimed taqueria in the city of Los Angeles. Between the "Grilled Steak Taco" here, Salazar\'s "Carne Asada Taco," and the "Arrachera Taco" at Taco Mara, Southern California doesn\'t lack for delicious ultra high-end steak tacos. The seared, heavily charred edges of the tender, smoky short loin are what makes Guerrilla Taco\'s "Grilled Steak Taco" one of L.A.\'s best tacos. The meat releases flavor galore when you bite into it, and the red and green salsas slathered on in the kitchen provide a heavy dose of piquancy and acidity to help neutralize the richer (but essential) elements in the dish: the well-marbled USDA Prime steak, the melted jack cheese, and the sturdy blue corn tortilla grilled in butter. I also loved the "Baja Cod Taco," which consisted of a large filet of rock cod in a crispy tempura batter with chipotle crema, Japanese mayo, sour pickled red cabbage, and heirloom cherry tomatoes that were both sweet and acetic. The "Sweet Potato Taco" is certainly interesting, even if it is not my thing at all. To make this well-known taco, the sweet potatoes are boiled, and then sauted in butter with thyme and deposited onto a corn tortilla before being smothered with a salsa made of almonds, tomatillos, chiles de rbol, habanero chiles, and fried garlic. Garnishments include feta cheese, chopped scallions, and pulverized corn nuts. A few problems: 1) Too much "tang" and not enough salt in the salsa, 2) The corn nuts are gritty like sand and thus unappetizing, and 3) I personally don\'t enjoy "mushy" tacos so much. Guerrilla Taco\'s "Pork Belly Taco" is garnished with smoked caviar, but is otherwise about what I expected. It\'s a strip of pork belly cooked so it crisps up on the outside and is greasy within, but could probably use a glaze or sauce beyond the charred habanero and chives added to this taco. That said, like all of the tacos here, I\'d almost order it just for the fresh hand-made corn tortilla, which could make a believer out of anyone in $5 tacos. This is a "fast casual" setup, where you order your tacos, then find a table to occupy while your food is prepared and delivered to you.'], ['108685370139018629938_6052e5b625ef3e77019421a7', 'My eyes bathed in the luxurious beauty of the tasting\'s initial offering: the delicate Le Caviar Imperial is perhaps better known as caviar araignee de mer, or caviar "spider of the sea," and is a work of art sprinkled with flakes of gold. The fresh, buttery caviar was so plentiful in my mouth, it felt like I was chewing a caviar steak coated with the flavorful jellied crustacean consomm it sat in. Some of the other tasting stand-outs included the delightful squid ink risotto served with the fish fillet, the rose shrimp served in the umami-rich ocean-y broth, the refreshing shaved ice with hibiscus syrup, and the heavenly chocolate hazelnut dessert with its glamorous edible butterflies made of sugar.'], ['108685370139018629938_6055f38b3019cb0a47838b3a', 'I\'ve never had Al Pastor pork so tasty in the U.S.. . As great as the Al Pastor pork was, I was disappointed by the fact they use packaged corn tortillas that smell less like corn and more like talcum powder. If I was desperately trying to convince someone to love Los Angeles, I\'d probably first take that person to Leo\'s Tacos. Leo\'s Tacos is a highly-esteemed fleet of trucks serving $1 tacos across L.A. This location in a gas station parking lot at Venice and LaBrea is the original truck and known to be the one to visit if you were looking for the very best version of Leo\'s tacos. During my recent visit, I ordered the "Al Pastor Taco" (pork shoulder marinated in adobo, shaved off of a spinning trompo) and the "Cabeza Taco" (braised cow head meat). First of all, forget about the Cabeza Taco: despite having some interesting varying textures within the small pile of meat on the tortilla, the overall flavor is too muddy and the cabeza is not appropriately seasoned, resulting in a below-average cabeza taco in Los Angeles. I implore everyone to instead focus 100% of their attention on Leo\'s "Al Pastor Taco." Think of your typical good Al Pastor pork: some pieces ultra-crispy, others ultra-tender, and the best of those magenta-glazed meat strips share both textures in one piece of meat. That\'s Leo\'s secret: through excellent knife-work, they maximize the amount of crusted, sticky edges in their tortillas. Additionally, you will need to dress these tacos yourself: for the Al Pastor Taco, I recommend onions, cilantro, and their salsa roja (deep red sauce) from the salsa bar; for the Cabeza Taco, a tangy salsa verde is more appropriate. My above quibbles are very minor, and I bring them up only because when you\'re talking about a taco this good, you are talking about the very best tacos you can find, and this invites contextualization and comparison against other tacos in this tier. I have not found a better Al Pastor Taco in L.A.'], ['108685370139018629938_60478d5c90b81483d31acd76', 'Tajima is a Convoy ramen-ya with a craptacular parking situation, but superb ramen. My favorite appetizer is the "Beef Tataki with Jalapeo," described on Tajima\'s menu as "thinly-sliced seared beef sashimi served with ponzu sauce, grated radish and jalapeo," and also features enough bonito flakes to provide a surprisingly crunchy textural layer to this dish. I also like to order the "Omurice" as an appetizer and split it among my party. Omurice is a unique Japanese dish consisting of an omelette stuffed with rice, typically ketchup fried rice. It\'s not what I\'d consider to be authentic Omurice based on what I\'ve had elsewhere, but it\'s tasty! The reason you come to Tajima, however, is the ramen. The "Ramen with Tonkotsu" (Pork Bone Broth) is what to order. Tajima\'s slurpable, soulful tonkotsu broth is thick, gelatinous, and salty, while enriched by tiny bits of pork fat, scallions, deep garlic flavor, and sesame. San Diego provides a myriad of options for ramen -- some of which I\'d advise sophisticated diners to stay clear of (I\'m looking at you, Underbelly), but most of which are at least OK. Tajima is in the top tier, above most other San Diego ramen-yas.'], ['108685370139018629938_6056362cd335d0abfb415a77', 'The first course I ordered at Sinatra was the Polipo, which featured octopus in a roasted red pepper emulsion. This was the best part of the meal for me -- of particular delight was the tenderness of the octopus which, according to my waiter, is due to the octopus being vigorously beaten after it is caught and before its muscles tighten up. (I have a running theory that no two chefs tenderize their octopus the same way, which is why I always get a different answer when I ask.) The red pepper sauce served with the octopus was umami-rich, and featured fried capers with a crispy texture, providing a nice contrast to the soft Mediterranean octopus. My next course was Pennette Pasta (half-sized) with a rag of Italian sausage, bell peppers, and basil. Pasta was cooked al dente. I much enjoyed swirling the fork-tender meat around to pick up more veal broth reduction and lip-smacking collagen. On recommendation of my waiter, I paired the ossobuco with the silky 2011 Masi Costasera Amarone, which was a delicious, medium-bodied wine that paired perfectly with the veal.'], ['108685370139018629938_605677d63019cb0a47838d3c', 'Fajitas are average. My favorite thing to get here is probably the "Southwest Egg Rolls," which feature chicken, black beans, corn, jalapeo jack cheese, red peppers, and spinach in fried flour tortillas with a \'not horrible\' avocado-ranch sauce for dipping.'], ['108685370139018629938_604f472088c7af3f893e63fc', 'I couldn\'t leave here without ordering the grilled fish that is Mitch\'s raison d\'tre, if all of the reviews are to be believed. On a Tuesday in March, Mitch\'s "Grilled Market Halibut" featured a grilled and nearly blackened half-pound halibut filet from the Sea of Cortez. The fish\'s snow-white flesh tasted fine, had firm and dense texture, but a delightful taste aside from a bitterness imparted by whatever they\'re using for their seasoning blend, or the grill itself. I\'d rather have had the fish better-salted prior to cooking than the unctuous salsa verde sauce. The "Grilled Oysters" are pretty good -- not New Orleans good, but San Diego good. On the day I had them, they were six briny oysters from Hawk\'s Point (Washington), grilled with breadcrumbs, bacon, parmesan, corn, and leeks. The reason I came to Mitch\'s was to try their fish tacos. The first taco I ordered was the "Beer Battered Alaskan Cod Taco," which featured one big chunk of cod, both juicy and flaky, deep-fried until crispy but still light in color and flavor. The fish is put in a double layer of middling corn tortillas and topped with lime crema, shredded cabbage, tomatoes, and onions. There\'s no heat in this taco, so I used the glass bottles of "Mitch\'s Pineapple Habanero Salsa" provided at each table to liven it up. Thankfully, however, it added a sweet and sour flavor element to help cut through the batter and tortillas and everything else. I wish Mitch\'s was as good at taco construction and achieving an appropriate balance of ingredients inside tortillas as they were at frying fish. They\'re a seafood restaurant first and foremost, which is why their fried battered fish taco is not the best in the city, despite the actual fish itself arguably being the best. Similarly, the "Grilled Wild Shrimp Taco" - made with same ingredients as the Beer Battered Alaskan Cod taco -- suffers from poor overall taco construction. Also, the shrimp is grilled in the same way as the grilled fish, making the surface a bit bitter. These achingly middling shrimp tacos are another example of "taquero" being a truly skilled role - and that even the best ingredients and meats don\'t always make the best tacos.'], ['108685370139018629938_6042b93ec6fcf1fddba18c0b', 'King Taco has been blessed by the legendary Jonathan Gold as "the first important proliferator of the modern L.A. King Taco introduced a large segment of L.A.\'s population to what was once called "soft tacos" but they now just call "tacos." Even more crucially, King Taco brought the "al pastor taco" and the "carnitas taco" to the SoCal masses. Tacos in the U.S. have evolved, of course, and we live in a quasi-capitalist society, so those who come into something first can\'t always be relied upon to always be the best at it. In the case of King Taco, they\'re not serving bad tacos. In fact, any of their stores would be the best taco shop in 99% of American cities. But we\'re talking about Southern California, and their tacos are middle-of-the-road for the region in 2019.'], ['108685370139018629938_6055f2003019cb0a47838b35', 'The specialty of Tito\'s La Especial are "tacos al vapor," aka steamed tacos. This delicious Mexican street food is also known as "tacos de canasta" (basket tacos) because they\'re traditionally layered in a big basket and sold by street vendors, many of whom hawk them from their bikes. Tito\'s "Carne Deshebrada Taco Al Vapor" is excellent. Aside from steamed double corn tortillas comprising each taco\'s "shell," the chile-steeped shredded beef inside is soft, luscious, and as juicy as you\'d want any meat to be. Despite the fact they traditionally would be drizzled in oil (to help preserve them) and served out of a basket over the course of a day, these tacos are best made-to-order. I would also recommend the "Papas Taco Al Vapor," consisting of seasoned potatoes in a ranchera sauce, a loose mash of creamy crushed potatoes and firmer chunks, all colored orange from the sauce. The "Taco Dorado de Carne Deshebrada" served here is the complete opposite of the al vapor tacos, as the tortilla is instead a crunchy deep-fried shell that is stuffed with stewed beef, lettuce, chopped tomatoes, and shredded cheese. Tito\'s does a decent job with this style of taco, but you really should stick to the al vapor tacos here, which are indeed "especial." Tito\'s La Especial\'s salsa roja is made of fire and miracles and I recommend it be used on everything you eat here.'], ['108685370139018629938_604e40f277e81aaed3ccae6d', 'I\'ve ordered several dishes at the Caf 21 location in Gaslamp, but my favorite has been the "Curry Seared Scallops," served in a cast iron skillet, featuring large sauteed scallops covered in a zesty yellow yogurt curry sauce and bread crumbs, served over a potato leek puree that crisps up and sticks to the pan in a GOOD way. The "Shrimp Corn Cakes" are a great breakfast. This creative and lively take on eggs benedict is one of my favorite breakfast items served in Gaslamp. Strawberry sauce is drizzled into small dots on the plate, and a sweet blueberry compote is served on the side.'], ['108685370139018629938_6050dec5c53d98b3eace1889', 'Bring me slushy frozen margaritas in glasses with sugar-brushed rims! Bring me your booziest blueberry-pom-acai mojitos! I have no palate for these types of drinks, so it tasted a bit like what I actually remember of my last Hand Grenade in New Orleans. I decided to push my boundaries a bit and ordered the "La Familia," an inebriating tipple containing tequila, mezcal, cinnamon syrup, lime juice, and grapefruit juice. This drink was strong with cinnamon and had a clearer and more on-the-nose flavoring scheme than the Bro Tai. I\'ve woken up with enough brutal hangovers from cinnamon spirits like Goldschlger and Fireball that I should have hated this, but perhaps it\'s because I am such a bad drinker that this cocktail ended up being my favorite at Miss B\'s. I\'ve also tried their riff on the Rum & Coke, "Cuba Libre," bottled in-house and containing cane cola, spiced rum, and lime juice. I\'ve had the "Curried Coconut Shrimp," which is closer in style to a southeast Asian curry dish than a Jamaican curry, and the smoky "El Cubano" with crispy fries.'], ['108685370139018629938_6050acea9c93e55e75b72174', "Initially, my favorite thing about Anna's burritos? The beautiful, tasty juices that'd drip from the tortilla into the foil that I'd then slurp out when no one was looking. The steamed flour tortillas, a trick stolen by both Anna's and Boca Grande from the celebrated taquerias of the San Francisco Mission. The steaming process helps make the tortilla edges sticky enough to bind and seal everything in, so that the burrito can be eaten vertically, and that the mixture of hot sauce, vegetable juices, melted cheese, and meat fat mingle and combine. My burrito of choice is a Super Burrito with Carnitas, Pinto Beans, Rice, Cheese, Salsa (Cilantro, Onion, Tomato), all wrapped in a flour tortilla.. I live in San Diego, a city known for its burritos, and I can't enjoy them because they're all both objectively and subjectively inferior to Anna's. In this way, Anna's has ruined burritos for me."], ['108685370139018629938_6041ba6b2e57ebdea29c5e16', 'All of the customers here submit their orders in Spanish, the place makes its own fresh corn tortillas in front of you, it is open 24x7, and they give away blistered chile toreados at the front counter. These are all tell-tale signs of a legit taco operation. My first victim during my visit was the "Buche Taco," (Pork Stomach) a combination of crispy buche and soft buche, marinated and smothered in one of the most flavorful and beautiful sauces I\'ve ever tasted on a taco. The textural contrast was wonderful: crispy salty bits, spicy and sour chewy bits, fresh onions and cilantro, and a heavy, thick corn tortilla. The sweet tortilla tastes like fresh corn, which is how a good tortilla really ought to taste. This is, without a doubt, the best Buche Taco I\'ve eaten. The "Tripa Taco" was dispatched next, and I found it to be worth ordering as well, even if it is not as transcendent as the Buche Taco. The tripa taco also features onions, cilantro, and a snappy salsa verde.'], ['108685370139018629938_60548f4a6204e8cd294f2344', "The churros are decent, I'm just not sure this place is necessary in a city where you can't throw a taco without hitting a place that sells churros. Here you can order your Spanish donut sticks covered in Fruity Pebbles, matcha, Nutella, or just about any trendy sweet topping du jour; in other words, if someone with Snapchat puppy ears can put it on a scoop of conflict-free non-GMO gelato, you'll find it here. Perhaps I was expecting churros that were so extraordinary that they merited a fast-casual spot on Convoy that does nothing but churros. What I got was a warm, crispy, cinnamon-sugar pastry that was par for the course in this region, with some sweet, sticky dips on the side."], ['108685370139018629938_60464d69882f4d1caf5fee25', 'One of my favorites I\'ve visited has been "Tacos Tumbras a Tomas," an operation that has been around since 1995, run by Tomas Martinez with his brothers Jesus and Manuel. The "Carnitas Taco." Here, the pork shoulder is cooked confit-style in simmering lard in a large steel cazo. A generous amount of the resulting carnitas is piled onto double corn tortillas, with two extra tortillas given on the side for good measure -- there is, after all, a ton of meat involved here. Chopped onions, cilantro, salsa roja, and a full lime (halved) are provided on the taco if you say "yes" when you\'re asked if you want "the works" or "con todo." The entire thing cost me $4.50, tax included, but was easily the equivalent of more than two normal-sized carnitas tacos. I suggest Tacos Tumbras a Tomas for a satisfying, filling, affordable lunch served without the lines or fuss of some of the busier stalls in the vicinity.'], ['108685370139018629938_604749eab0e2129e47536090', 'My wife and I dined here recently, beginning our meal with the "Mother Board," a cutting board spread of a cured meats (Bresaola, Duck Pt, Salami) and cheeses (Camembert, Bucheron, Drunken Goat) with some familiar fixins\' mixed in with some not-so-familiar. The "Ahi Poke Tuna Tacos" were much enjoyed by my wife and me. The texture of the ahi is stunning and delicate, its tender, raw chunks will melt in your mouth. The Asian slaw is sweet, but not overly so, and the wonton "taco shell" is crispy but light, the combination of all of this coming across as decadent, but not heavy. Evaluating it strictly as a taco, it may not have conventional taco ingredients, but it is a very well-composed bite of food, balancing the fish, sauce, cabbage, and shell like a legit taquero would. My entre was the "Greater Omaha Prime Flat Iron," a half-pound steak that was cooked to a luscious medium-rare as I requested, its edges and surfaces blasted with heat so its seasonings and fat mix with charred outer-proteins to form a marvelous crust. A creamy parsnip pure, savory slices of grilled trumpet mushrooms, and crisp asparagus in herb butter complete a delectable steak dish that didn\'t break the bank, at just $34 all-in.'], ['108685370139018629938_60520101da79151bfc125c2d', "I'm usually alright with White Castle, but not when it immobilizes me on my Vegas vacation for a day and a half."], ['108685370139018629938_605676dc3019cb0a47838d38', 'The Pork Souvlaki was real good (and I recommend this if you come here), even if I thought the Gyros were so-so.'], ['108685370139018629938_604e0d8b71ced5c7554dda45', 'Obviously here in San Diego, most of the food at "On The Border" is awful compared to what you can get from a myriad of legit, authentic local Mexican restaurants. I say "most" and not "all" because the one thing On The Border has engineered of value are their complimentary chips and salsa, which stand up to the best chips and salsa that even a city like San Diego has to offer. Maybe order some guacamole (which they make in front of you, table-side.)'], ['108685370139018629938_60425ef37dfa7f187183c4de', 'While approaching this taco truck, my eyes were immediately drawn to a large trompo stacked with layers of well-manicured adobo-marinated pork spinning around, reflecting a flame off of a glistening surface sweating with achiote-infused meat juices. Upon ordering an "Al Pastor Taco" here, the taquero will carve off thin slices of pork directly off of this upside-down mountain of meat into single corn tortillas and top it off with a chunk of pineapple. Aside from the customary onions and cilantro, ensure your taco has El Flamin\'s red sauce on it. This is a hypnotic, mouth-numbing salsa roja that complements and completes the al pastor pork, and the "secret sauce" that keeps this truck doing brisk business. El Flamin\'s "Al Pastor Tacos" would be better with a more assertive marinade, so they do not reach the same heights as the al pastor served at Leo\'s or even the Ave 26 Taco Stand, but they are definitely in my "top 5" favorite pastor-style tacos in Los Angeles. As with the other two al pastor purveyors I mentioned, bagged corn tortillas are used here.']]

review_text: Ramen Bar is one the new Japanese restaurant with a sole focus on Ramen to open in the Alpharetta area. The menu is typical of many ramen restaurants. You have appetizers, drinks, and of course ramen. The ramen here has few options when it comes to broth style. You have soy based, miss, and the most popular tonkatsu broth. Be sure to look at the menu descriptions to get a better idea of which one best suits your pallette. My recommendation would be to start off with some pork gyoza dumplings and takoyaki squid balls. That would be a good starter before eating your ramen. The ramen broth is very rich in flavor and doesn't taste to bland and generic. People tend to think that ramen is easy to make and doesn't require a lot of skill. This is a big misconception and the broth takes hours to prepare in order for it to be just right. I've been to my share of ramen restaurants and I can tell right away which ones usually are good. Definitely recommended for any ramen lover or just someone who wants to try it out for the first time.

Their pizzas come either as a 14" thin crust or a 12"x12" square "Sicilian-style" crust - I had the thin crust and it was great - still good crust on the edges, and nice, thin and crispy on the bottom. Would love to venture back to Zoli's to try some other pizzas - very eclectic menu with some funny-sounding names, but some great-sounding combos of flavors! They do have a lunch special - smaller pizza with side salad - only $13, but the choices are limited on what you can select.

history_reviews: [['107444333383263433673_605110445b4ccec8d5caea13', "This is a good little pizza place kind of in the middle of no where. Four of split two pizzas and did half and half on each. For $17 you only got 4 ribs (it came with rice and macaroni salad, but still)."], ['107444333383263433673_6055f66cf69c7b117806fdd2', "We got the Thai Money Bags, Big Daddy Tuna Plate, and  Mama's World Famous Fish Tacos (blackened). We've had fish tacos at several places this week and these were hands down the best ones. The seasoning was fantastic. The fish was delicious. It came with the best lime crema sauce to put on them too."], ['107444333383263433673_604ec4df9755094ba8abde27', "I usually hear about these donuts from Portland travelers, but when I saw there was one in Denver (two actually), I obviously had to try it on my trip. The cookie was crunchy on the outside and gooey on the inside. It was a fat cookie."], ['107444333383263433673_60430741cc4f7990c6577e09', "You can't find better pastries. The seeded roast beef and Croque Monsieur are my favorite sandwiches. Their soups are also very good."], ['107444333383263433673_604ae5066b6b79a4bb4810fc', 'Upon arriving in Miami, our first stop was to get a Cuban.
