history_reviews: [['105853218368004682403_605728a39ffe343acca5fc9c', 'They skimped on the Cajun fries, which was disappointing. That being said, I was glad to finally have been able to try the much hyped spicy chicken sandwich. The sandwich is much bigger than the equivalent chickfila sandwich, but the spiciness comes from the sauce rather than the chicken itself. I liked how the chicken was breaded and it was still crunchy even after the 20 minute car ride home. The sandwich does come with pickles, and you can get a non-spicy sandwich (although the spicy sandwich is definitely manageable, and in the same level as hot Cheetos).'], ['105853218368004682403_6048c7438b84f513e32cdad6', 'He made sure to countdown so we could capture the giant flame he made for the bananas foster for the gram. They have aperitifs as well, and the Irish coffee was nicely sweet with a kick.'], ['105853218368004682403_6051e16bc53d98b3eace1d8b', 'The poutine was good, although I felt the gravy couldve couldve used a tad more salt and the cheese curds werent chewy.'], ['105853218368004682403_60570118c4674474cff9120f', 'I liked that the broth was separated from the noodles so you can mix it up yourself when youre ready to eat. The broth for the beef curry udon was watery and only had a hint of curry. The broth for the spicy pork ramen was better but it was not spicy at all. I would say the ABC ramen was the best of the three we had, although there were less pieces of meat than they typically provide.'], ['105853218368004682403_605680a03019cb0a47838d6b', 'The real MVP were the Irish coffee and strawberry daiquiris. The Irish coffee was mixed well with the coffee overpowering the whiskey (for the most part) but without being overly sweet. The strawberry daiquiri was dangerous as you cant really taste the alcohol and it just seems like a smoothie.'], ['105853218368004682403_604e0202b9a3d5528c50bc5b', 'I could wax poetic about the virtues of the Mexican chocolate pie at The Pie Hole, but to put it simply, the Pie Hole consistently has delicious desserts that are indulgent and rich. The Mexican chocolate pie is thick and creamy, while the earl grey pie is more light and airy, but grounded by the toasted pistachios that adorn its top. You should split the pies with loved ones, although its certainly doable to eat an entire slice by yourself. You can order a whole pie if youd like, and they do offer drinks like matcha tea and coffee. The cashier was very friendly and mentioned that they have happy hour from Monday through Friday where pie slices are $5 and whole pies are ~$30.'], ['105853218368004682403_604913b3b1a0aaee3eefa92e', 'The cheesecakes are a 5 but the food is a solid 3. For a family of four, we got an egg roll sampler, a regular size farfalle pasta with chicken and a garlic cream sauce, and two cheesecakes. The egg roll sampler was a good order since theres a variety to try and theres plenty of dipping sauce to choose from. My favorite was the avocado one, but everyone else really liked the hamburger egg roll dipped into the pink sauce (which I think is thousand island dressing). The pasta was disappointing - it was super oily with sparse amounts of chicken and accoutrements. The cheesecakes were the highlight - the godiva one is so decadent and rich, so its perfect for a chocolate fanatic. The white chocolate macadamia nut with the blondie brownie crust was also a surprise hit. The macadamia nuts were a bit soggy, but paired well with the white chocolate chunks. The bottom layer brownie was nice and and chewy, and complemented the creaminess of the cheesecake.'], ['105853218368004682403_6057007d6fce2069470c60cf', 'I used to love going to Raising Canes when I lived in Phoenix, so I was excited to get my chicken tender fix. This might be an LA thing, but the chicken tenders were a lot smaller and they really skimped on the fries. The chicken tenders are pretty bland, but the sauce is good. Its an extra 30 something cents per sauce but they do keep well if you want to use them for some home cooked chicken tenders. The fries are crinkle-cut and were under seasoned. The Texas toast was very good - it was still warm and buttery by the time we got to eat it. The combo also comes with coleslaw although you can request another piece of toast in lieu of it.'], ['105853218368004682403_60442190b81264dfa846d73c', 'Tried the Chicago hot dog - while it was a good hot dog, it certainly wasnt life changing. I liked the sesame seed bun and how soft it was. I liked the chili dog more - it wasnt soggy but still soft and I like the flavor of the chili.'], ['105853218368004682403_60497a77c7c8ee3104ba1994', 'Your typical fast food restaurant serving fried chicken and biscuits. For the four of us we got the family combo which comes with 8 pieces of chicken, a large side, and four buttermilk biscuits for ~$29. The chicken seasoning on the skin is good but the meat itself is bland, so get the hot sauce. Fries were really good and salty, and the biscuits were too dry.'], ['105853218368004682403_60562767f69c7b117806ff40', 'They only do either chicken tenders or sliders, but they do them extremely well. You can get a combo of 2 tenders plus crinkle cut fries (which were also well-seasoned) for ~$11 and add an extra tender for ~$3 more.'], ['105853218368004682403_6042604f7dfa7f187183c59a', 'I had the pasta pancetta ($16)which I wish had more pancetta pieces, but was very good. I liked the chewiness of the pasta, and the caramelized onions lent a nice mellow flavor. The sauce was a little bit too oily but for those that like a creamy sauce, this pasta is a good call.'], ['105853218368004682403_604dac0271ced5c7554dd7ae', 'Quaint cookie and ice cream shop with very friendly staff. Theres various flavors of cookies and although they all looked appealing, we went with a classic chocolate chip cookie. It was dense and generous with the chocolate chips. We also got a scoop of the Cookie Monster ice cream on the side which the cashier let me sample beforehand. It had cookie dough and Oreos mixed into blue ice cream and I thought it wasnt too sweet. They have ice cream sandwiches available as well that you can customize. Overall a comfy place to hang and eat some cookies!'], ['105853218368004682403_6047348cb1a0aaee3eef858c', 'Local burger joint that uses English muffins for buns. Mexican Coke was $2.95 and the burgers ranged from ~$13 to $16. The veggie burger was better than I expected and comes with two toppings. I got grilled onions and thousand island dressing plus sharp cheddar for an extra 50 cents. The veggie burger was hearty and full of flavor though a tad bit dry. The fries were my favorite - theyre Belgian style and so tasty. We all preferred the fries over our burgers. The Blake Burger came with green chilies that were more salty than flavorful. The Wrigley Field Burger came with bacon (always a plus) and all the burgers had a lettuce, tomato, and pickle spear on the side. The English muffin in lieu of a burger bun seems like a good idea in theory as it holds the patty more firmly but it was also a bit dryer. I like that the beef is grass fed but it also means that the more well-cooked it is, the dryer the meat becomes.'], ['105853218368004682403_604e53656c0a991ff657c0a3', 'Oysters - One is my favorites. Crispy fried quail - Comes in two pieces. House made pasta - I was a bit disappointed but it was still high quality pasta with good texture (cooked al dente). Sweet and spicy glazed duck leg - has an XO sauce and is apparently Szechuan-inspired. Cornbread - underwhelming - I preferred the free house bread rolls provided at the start of the meal. Crispy catfish - came in two pieces and lightly breaded & fried. Flat iron steak - recommended to be medium rare. Reminds me of the Diddy Riese one. Its on the more bitter side and the accompanying biscotti is surprisingly spicy (I liked its unexpected nature). Drinks - The Papa holiday tasted like grapefruit, while the fist of berries has a licorice taste.'], ['105853218368004682403_605616813019cb0a47838bc6', 'Some positives: the bacon wrapped scallops were good.'], ['105853218368004682403_60535e0c88c7af3f893e7af9', 'Popular Cuban bakery with delectable cheese roll pastries. If I could subsist just on these cheese rolls, I would. The cheese filling inside is a good balance of salty and sweet, and the flaky pastry in the outside is melt-in-your-mouth delicious. The guava pastries are also a popular thing to bring in - the jam inside the pastry is sweet and they smell strong of guava (which some like, I personally dont, but Ill eat then anyways). They also have savory items like croquettes and sandwiches. They have cakes which you can pre-order for special events. Overall its truly an LA institution and I love eating one (or two or three) of their pastries.'], ['105853218368004682403_604c780d5a9e6adec8bf8af8', 'We got the chow mein and fried rice (because were unhealthy) but they do have a vegetables option. For the entrees we got the kung pao chicken, honey walnut shrimp (extra cost, and mushroom chicken. I think paying extra for the honey walnut shrimp was worth it, as the shrimp was still crunchy and I enjoyed the glazed walnuts that were mixed in.'], ['105853218368004682403_604a661dd863393130a41496', 'We chose the cha cha chicken half chicken that was marinated in mix sauce, and it wasnt spicy. The spicy fries were cut potato rounds and werent spicy, but theyre good dipped into the jerk sauce.'], ['105853218368004682403_604e9d7b7ce15821f39750eb', 'Had the laksa with chicken (you can pick the meat) and the egg noodles (you also customize the noodles) (~$18). Its not spicy at all; there is another option of laksa that Anthony Bourdain likes and was described by the waitress as medium spicy.'], ['105853218368004682403_6057277af69c7b1178070351', 'Food - We got some mimosas (its brunch - we had to) which were well-crated and the strawberry on the stick was sweet. We ended the meal with the pot du creme - highly recommend getting this. It was very smooth, almost like a mousse, and contested with a smattering of coarse sea salt on the top. There were fresh berries that popped in your mouth that accompanied it, and it came in three dollops.'], ['105853218368004682403_604bf91077e81aaed3cc9ae2', 'My sister and I split an order of the gumbo, which was a bit lacking in the chicken and more heavy on the oysters. If youre feeling particularly hungry, Id recommend getting the basil egg Benedict which is a savory breakfast item (~$6) that has a warm, runny egg inside a soft, malasada type bread. It was about a 25 minute wait, but the perfectly cooked noodles are so wonderfully chewy its okay to wait.'], ['105853218368004682403_6043493eb81264dfa846b11d', 'Burgers and freak shakes (those really heavy milkshakes) can be found here. Be careful when you try to take the brownie out because it almost completely fell to the table when we tried to take a bite, so we ended up just putting them on a plate and eating it alongside the shake. The shake is super thick, and we mostly just ate it like it was regular ice cream. I thought the brownie was a bit dry, but I really liked scraping the chocolate chips with the Nutella from the side of the glass. The burger was large and already cut in half so it was easy to split - a solid burger, and we did like having it medium rare. The fries were more thickly cut and came with ketchup on the side.'], ['105853218368004682403_604b6eb577e81aaed3cc9456', 'The pork belly had a different type of kimchi that tasted more smoky, and also had two different sauces. The baklava ($1.99) was small but sweet, and they have pistachio available!'], ['105853218368004682403_604935bb55041a127f88a880', 'Even the free cheese bread (that came in a little cute bag) tasted amazing. Bucatini: Noodles were cooked al dente and when you mix in the uni, you get an interesting mix of Italian and Japanese flavors. Cavatelli: My favorite dish - the pasta was perfectly squishy and the pork sugo was well seasoned with Calabrian chilis. Parker rolls: Yes its $6 for bread, but its worth it. The rolls are so soft and chewy, and we fought over the last bits of date butter that came with it. Liberty duck: The best way to describe it would be if you combined the crispy skin of Peking duck with the meat of holiday ham, nestled next to wild rice pilaf with a sweet XO sauce. Wild boar: Definitely not a boar-ing dish. The meat was tender and the gnocchi mixed with greens dripping in a mustard jus was interesting but comforting.'], ['105853218368004682403_60415cb47cd8bf1303624fe4', 'Its a little bakery/cafe located in Greektown that we came across after lunch, so we decided to stop by for coffee and dessert. The woman working behind the counter was very funny - when I asked her what the best pastry was, she said they all were. Theres traditional Greek desserts like baklavas the size of my palm and other pastries like cakes and tarts. We ended up getting the strawberry shortcake and a walnut baklava. The barista there was also very funny and asked a lot of questions to make sure we got the flavor we wanted from our iced Greek coffees (I got sweet with milk, my friend got black). The strawberry shortcake was light and fluffy, and had real strawberry pieces inside. There was a fair amount of white frosting but it wasnt overly sweet. It was sweetened with a generous portion of honey and the crushed walnuts lent such a lovely texture against the phyllo dough. The bill was ~$23 for the two frappes and two desserts. Its authentic, family-owned, the desserts are delicious, and the coffee is strong - what more do you want?'], ['105853218368004682403_60544e9580c04bd7072f24bc', 'Every time I have a friend in town I always take them to Pie Hole to share the delights of the Mexican Chocolate pie. The crust is perfectly crumbly and complements the filling so well. You can share with one or two other people, or you could also just enjoy a slice on your own if you feel up to the task ($6). You can order whole pies in advance for about $40 I believe. I have also tried the Earl Grey pie, pumpkin pie, and chess pie, but my heart belongs to the Mexican chocolate pie. The place is family-run and they have locations in Hollywood and Venice, but I like the Arts District one the best since I think it has the most character. Order the Mexican chocolate pie.'], ['105853218368004682403_6048911af9e05764f1fa564f', 'They specialize in fish tacos, and are definitely among one of the best places to get fish tacos in the LA area. The fish tacos are huge - two is enough for a dinner. The crispiness of the fish against the chopped tomatoes & onions the perfect match. The salsa is deep and husky, and with a squirt of fresh lime, each bite is a little piece of utter bliss. The shrimp ceviche was also good, although the one at Marisco Jalisco is still my favorite.'], ['105853218368004682403_6051ab53c53d98b3eace1c79', 'My go-to is the salmon bowl ($15) which has brown rice, salmon cooked medium rare, a salad, and corn medley that I really enjoy along with cotija cheese. The vegan brownie is surprisingly good and has bits of peanut brittle that add a bit more interesting texture to an otherwise very soft brownie ($4). I also love the chocolate chip cookies - I think theyre some of the best and I love it whenever our office caters tender greens (TG as its affectionately known) and theres leftover chocolate chip cookies to munch on. Theyre the size of my palm and have big round chunks of chocolate embedded throughout. Depending on the batch, they can either be pretty crispy but I like them best when theyre slight chewy. Another favorite of mine is the buttermilk fried chicken - its not as heavy as you think and you could always get it in a salad. The salt and pepper chicken is also a solid bet if you want to get it in a salad or plate. You order at the cash register and move down the line sideways, then you have the option of getting drinks and dessert. The kombucha is $5 and its tall glass of pink fizziness. Green juice is $3.5 and is decent. Theres also wine for $7 if youre looking to have some alcohol. The blueberry dessert is really moist and light.'], ['105853218368004682403_604317cdcc4f7990c65781e7', 'For three girls, we split two appetizers - the nachos and the fries with cheddar cheese and bacon. The nachos were surprisingly spicier than I thought they would be, and they had a generous portion of guacamole. For the fries, we opted not to get the one with the chili since we had already gotten chili exposure with the nachos, so we got the chives and bacon one.'], ['105853218368004682403_6053b83e4b7f30a9c0a50adf', 'The onion rings and fries were standard. My chicken and waffles were good but I prefer the fried chicken at the Misfit.'], ['105853218368004682403_60497bd6b1a0aaee3eefaf3a', 'We got the artichoke crab cake ($15) which was my favorite dish. The buffalo cauliflower had a nice crisp ones around it and good amount of buffalo sauce. I got the boujee pep pizza ($17) for my entree but only ate two slices because it was pretty full from the apps alone. The pizza is vegan and has vegan soppresata which was really thin and crispy and looked like big brown pepperonis. Thin crust and made for good leftovers (I suggest heating it up one slice at a time for 30 seconds so it doesnt get too hard).']]

history_reviews: [['114589915198164681316_60532f337fec92c07c643a78', 'They also have seasonal menus, and as Im writing this review (September 2018), they have incredible pumpkin gnocchi that will leave you craving for more. Make sure you keep room for dessert: their banoffee pie and their sticky toffee pudding are to die for!'], ['114589915198164681316_60532f5088c7af3f893e79d5', 'We started with steak tartare, a tarte, and one of their homemade sausages with sauerkraut. The steak tartare was really well seasoned and served with toasted slices of baguette and a small salad. The tarte flamb - which was basically a flatbread, was topped with fresh veggies and cheese. The sausage was definitely homemade and super flavorful. We then went onto the entrees, our choices were the risotto with morels and asparagus (which is seasonal), the steak frites - that btw comes with bone marrow, and the chicken with mashed potatoes and veggies. The steak was very nicely cooked and flavorful, the fries werent the best ever but were pretty good nevertheless. The piece de resistance was without a doubt the profiteroles - perfect choux pastry filled with ice cream as well as homemade whipped cream, and topped with a delicious dark chocolate sauce.'], ['114589915198164681316_604989dbc7c8ee3104ba1a85', 'Not only is the location really pretty and very typical - you almost feel like being on the second floor of a korean market, where they cook what you bought - but the food is simply AMAZING. You can choose among many options, different beef or pork combos are a great option if youre  in a  group, or you can just pick your favorite cuts. They also have a few options if you want something other than bbq: Japchae, bibimbap, tteokbokki, pajeon, mul naengmyeon, just to name a few. What I recommend you guys to try for sure is the pork belly (samgyeopsal), perfectly layered and absolutely delicious with just a tad of salt or doenjang and made into a wrap with lettuce and kimchi (and raw garlic if you like it). Other dishes Id recommend are the marinated galbi, the bulgogi, and the ribeye. As far as other dishes Im a huge fan of their Japchae, their tteokbokki, and the cold green tea noodles. If you want something small(er) as an appetizer try the kimchi jeon, or the pajeon, theyre pretty good and always made fresh. The banchan dishes are delicious, always order raw garlic on the side if you want the authentic experience, and the pickle onion they bring is to die for. Their kimchi is also very good, and so are the sauces they give you for the meats - The teriyaki sauce with bean flour is sweet and sticky, while the doenjang is nice and salty.'], ['114589915198164681316_6049888a09c8186bc0fdf3cb', 'Love their Malaysian Roti and beef rendang, but they have so manu good options as well! Id definitely recommend the roti Canai, beef rendang, fish head soup, fried intestines, hainanese chicken, and def try their drinks too!'], ['114589915198164681316_60552ed5451ea67743baf19e', 'Id definitely recommend you to try their charcuterie - most imported from Italy, paired with stunning cheeses and marmellate. Do not skip on the new entry, the famous timpano made famous by the foodie movie by definition: Big Night In. Delicious baked pasta inside pastry, with meatballs, meat sauce, peas, salami, cheese - trust me youll thank me!'], ['114589915198164681316_604b91a777e81aaed3cc9631', 'Definitely get the soup dumplings and the pan fried buns - and try their delicious shredded pork with bamboo shoots, which is one of my go to every time Im here. The soup dumplings are really flavorful and with a great amount of filing and soup, my go to are the pork ones but they also have the ones with crab - both are delicious! Sweet and savory tender pork strips with crunchy but hard bamboo shoots - trust me youll come back for more!'], ['114589915198164681316_604372a3aab4c25a4e74e72f', "Knowing that - or at least with that pre conception in my brain - I made my way to Let's Meat, the first korean bbq ayce style that finally opened in Manhattan with no expectations at all, just to have a decent meal with my friends on a gloomy Saturday. The other has more premium cuts like skirt steak, short rib, gopchang, squid, shrimp, octopus... and comes at 38.99$. Either options are great, and I'd say that unless you want seafood the OG is perfect. We did want seafood (and gopchang) so we ended up going for the premium option. We also added a couple sides (most are included, just a few aren't): spicy rice cakes - aka tteokbokki, japchae, and sundubujjigae. The Berkshire pork belly is nice and thick and fatty, and goes perfect with lettuce, kimchi and onion (and garlic if you're not scared of it). The marinated bulgogi was very flavorful and not too sweet - which sometimes can be. The shrimp was nice as well, and every cut of meat was carefully prepared by our waiter who was super nice and made sure no cut was over cooked. We accompanied our meal with makgeolli and soju (they have a combo deal for 15$), that were much needed with such a meaty feast."], ['114589915198164681316_60415b3a7cd8bf1303624f33', "If you didn't know, Gopchang is a real delicacy in Korea and people really do crave it. Gopchang means small intestines and is usually eaten after it's cooked on a hot griddle and paired with chives, rice, and mandatory soju. This place not only has small intestines, but also my favorite: Daechang, which is the larger intestine and is completely different. They also have a plethora of other offal items, but also cater to those who are more into pork belly and beef. Do not dare to skip on other dishes like their fried rice (spicy, but so addictive and delicious), their stews and their soups as well!"]]

We got Salsiccia (grilled Italian sausage), Tartufate (orecchiette, cremini, asparagus, sun-dried tomatoes, black truffle cream, Grana Padano, white truffle oil), and a farfalle pasta special that had smoked and fresh salmon. The sausage had good flavor and wasn't too salty, and the pastas were cooked perfectly al dente. We were surprised by how filling the portions were, both the antipasti and pastas. There was a ton of salmon in the farfalle special, and the Tartufate really hit the truffle-flavor craving I had without being too greasy or creamy."], ['107548322316470513394_604158cfc6fcf1fddba12da2', 'Every "classic" Chinese dish is super solid here, including the spicy beef noodles (not really spicy but noodles are super chewy), soup dumplings, mapo tofu, green beans, etc. One thing you MUST GET is the eggplant in garlic sauce. Best eggplant I\'ve ever had.'], ['107548322316470513394_604157bd7cd8bf1303624c81', "The Peking duck dinner is really the only thing you should be coming for, because they roast a spectacular duck here and I haven't had better in the city. The rest of the food on the menu is just okay--Chinatown has better. For four people, one duck dinner is just about enough, which comes with a large plate of sliced duck, six bao buns, a plate of fried rice, and a large bowl of soup. I'd recommend ordering extra buns since the meat will definitely outnumber the pieces of buns that you have, and a vegetable dish for health. The server brings out the roasted duck whole, and will carve/slice it table-side. It's always a spectacle to watch, and the meat is always super juicy, fatty, and crispy, all in one bite. The fried rice and soup are average, but complements the duck meat nicely. If you have five or more people in your group, it'd be a good idea to get two ducks. Sometimes near the end of the day they run out of ducks which is just about the saddest thing the waiter can tell you after you've been seated."], ['107548322316470513394_60415b797dfa7f1871835f97', 'Compared with other Chinatown dim sum restaurants, everything just tastes more flavorful and larger portions, albeit with slightly higher prices (avg $15 per person). review_text: Joes Pizza is a must stop for everyone who says that they love pizza. Whether you are a Pizza Novice or a regular Dave Portnoy this is a place that must be on the list. It was even in the Spider-Man movies in the 2000s. Real ingredients and a classic recipe make a great slice. There is nothing superfluous or extra about this kind of pizza, no crazy crust, no crazy process. This is a place where you can order a plain slice and be satisfied without any toppings. review_text: Pizzeria in Carroll Gardens know for absolutely lip smacking delicious brick oven calzones and pizzas. Once youve finally been seated, your choices couldnt be any easier, the menu offers two dishes: pizza and calzone, or my personal favorite, both. We started our meal with the calzone, which was the highlight of the meal and is clearly in a league of its own. The calzones are generously stuffed with ricotta, mozzarella, and red sauce along with whichever additional toppings you choose to have baked into this luscious treat. The calzone is prepared with a ton of love and genuine expertise, you somehow manage to still feel like an adult as youre devouring this classic childhood dish. Youll enjoy every hearty bite as well as each emphatic dunk of your calzone into the sweet red sauce as garnish. As for the pies, theyre prepared with the same expertise and love, however they fall a tad short of the calzone in overall satisfaction. Its tough for pizza to truly standout in NYC considering there are so many Goliath's that make otherworldly pies, that said, this is still a worthy option. The pie is slathered with the homemade red sauce and peppered with both low moisture mozzarella and buffalo mozzarella, which is delicious. The pizza is garnished with a heap of fresh basil whichs adds a pleasant earthiness to the meal. I recommend adding some garlic and at least one more topping to the pie to maximize your experience.
history_reviews: [['104285062634756642667_605488427fec92c07c6440b9', 'Pennsy offers several notable dining options, including a personal favorite, Pat LaFriedas meat purveyors. The bar has a rotating top of NY beers and regional favorites. Youll find plenty of seating and bar space within the food hall along with additional seating options on the outdoor terrance.'], ['104285062634756642667_60435f27ad733fba1bcfd098', 'As you bite into the dumpling, savory flavors invade your mouth as the soup is blitzes your taste buds and paves the way for the delivery of the tender pork. Aside from their famous soup dumplings, they offer creative variations on classic Chinese dishes but Id recommend trying their Shanghai pan fried noodles.'], ['104285062634756642667_60560255f69c7b117806fe51', 'Shake Shack is a NY born and bred, fast food chain that specializes in fresh beef burgers and delicious milk shakes. The burger scene is competitive in NYC but given its natural limitations to compete with the heavyweight champs (JG Melon, PJ Clarkes, etc.) this is the best fast food burger in the city. The beef is sourced locally from Pat LaFrieda meat purveyors which is the trademark of their tasty creations. The burgers are cooked medium and are dressed with lettuce, tomato and shack sauce.'], ['104285062634756642667_604a81acc6dc737bce7e5b7f', 'One of the oldest pizzerias in NYC and a great take on a New York slice. Grimaldis prepares their pizzas in a large brick oven, which leaves the pizza with an authentic and rustic taste. Top 5 NYC pizza, in my opinion.'], ['104285062634756642667_604ca10e77e81aaed3cca14e', 'Outstanding fried chicken. Pies & Thighs is a Williamsburg staple that stands true to the name in delivering mouth watering fried chicken and homemade pies. The fried goodness is crispy, well seasoned and juicy to the bite. I recommend the three piece meal which comes with two sides and a flakey, buttery biscuit. Speaking of sides, youll have several worthy options to pair with your poultry. I am a big fan of the collard greens which have a hearty, meaty seasoning and are well salted. In addition, the macaroni and cheese is deliciously simple and pairs supremely well with any chicken dish. Dont even think about asking for the bill without trying a slice of pie. The pies taste like theyve been prepared by somebodys grandma, cooking with a recipe thats been in the family for generations. I recommend the classic apple, but you cant miss with any of their delicious options. Pies & Thighs is perfect whenever you have a hankering for fried chicken or feel like devouring well prepared (and well priced) fatty, comfort meal.'], ['104285062634756642667_604c38db77e81aaed3cc9d7f', 'Burger & Barrel Winepub is an excellent burger joint that also offers impressive wine pairings to satiate your palate. No item on the menu is merely present to check the box, so when you find the Fried Chicken sandwich or Prime Rib starting back at you, its totally safe to devour something that isnt the burger. I highly recommend the Kung Pow Chicken Lollipops for starters, they have an unbelievable tang flavor that accompanies the slight heat that the appetizer presents. Youll be shocked to hear that the burgers are noteworthy. First off, Im a fan of any establishment that uses Pat LaFrieda beef because its a clear sign that the establishment is committed to quality. As for their slew of burgers, all are solid but B&B has built a reputation around the city for its Bash Burger. The burger has been named a 6x New York Wine & Food Festival Winner for best burger. The Bash Burger is graced with caramelized onions, bacon jam, gooey American cheese and their special sauce served on brioche bun. Its a great tasting burger, my only reservation is the bun to meat ratio which I feel could be improved to favore the beef. If youre looking for a burger with more heft, try the Double Barrel burger which comes with two meat patties. As a final touch, all of the burgers are served with a few onion rings for good measure and a healthy portion of crispy fries. Burger & Barrel Winepub is a great burger alternative in a city that is saturated in burger options that differentiates itself with a well balanced menu.'], ['104285062634756642667_60444dc5cc4f7990c6579f42', 'Youre in for a treat...Emilys is a boutique pizzeria, based in Clinton Hill, that has built a tremendous reputation for their creative combination of toppings, flavors, and textures that grace their scrumptious pies. Surprisingly, Emilys is famous for crafting one of the best burgers in the city, the Emmy Burger. The burger is prepared with Pat LaFrieda dry aged beef, sweet caramelized onions, American cheese, EMMY sauce while sandwiches together wonderfully between a pretzel bun. Their burger is juicy, savory, and extremely flavorful. It seriously makes you wonder how Emilys is better known for the pizza! The pro-tip is to order a pie and a burger, which is perfect for two people. Weve discussed the burger at the pizza joint, lets dissect the greatness of their signature dish. Emily classifies its pies in four categories: red, pink, green, and white which translates to a number of offerings based in tomato, vodka, tomatillo, and cheese sauces. All of their creations are masterfully architected with a unique blend of toppings, like a pepperoni pie drizzled with honey (dont question it, just order). While all of the pies are tasty in their own right, I have an affinity for The Colony (red), The Big Ang (pink), and The Emily (white). Emilys an up and coming pizzeria giant in the city and is perfect for virtually any occasion.']]

review_text: With the 3 dino-sized hearty roasted or smoked for hours ribs you can select two sides. In the picture you can see I selected the salad (which is huge) and a side of glazed cauliflower (my hand is in the pic to give you an idea of scale. Here they have baked mac and cheese which my son had two servings of, long green beans, wonderful glazed sweet potatoes and a bunch of other sides that you can interchange by just bringing your receipt back up and picking a different side than you got in the initial round. You can of course get more ribs, but the ribs are delicious (with a bit too much spice on them for me but the family loved the spice) and very filling. None of us finished our ribs, although I did give it the old college try. Our daughter was the odd duck out and had the pulled pork bun and was not impressed with the lack of anything else on it, but after learning about the huge condiment bar full of peppers, onions, sauces and the like she was happy.

review_text: I asked for the Mexican style corn but was brought out regular unseasoned, undressed corn. When I asked the waiter about it he came back with everything for me to dress the corn. I have had some amazing steak at Ruth's Chris, the fat melted in my mouth there, USDA PRIME without a doubt. Here at West Texas, the fat was rubbery and gross. USDA CHOSE at best, and that's a complement. Barely any seer, and they had steak sauce on the plate. STEAK SAUCE?! If your steak needs steak sauce and can't stand alone on it's own, your food isn't worth serving as "premium steak." The desserts were great. The chocolate cake was enormous! review_text: We ordered their signature Crab Cakes ($24) with a chili sesame butter sauce. While the crab cakes are small, theyre encased in a crispy shell with lots of real crab on the inside. We also ordered their Original California Roll ($10) with snow crab, tobiko, cucumber, and avocado. Im not sure how original it is because I thought the California Roll originated by Vancouver-chef, Hidekazu Tojo. In either case, the California roll here was quite good probably all of that fresh snow crab meat on the inside. Last up was the Frying Dragon Roll ($12) with a sweet ginger and wasabi beurre blanc sauce and a decadent filling of unagi, avocado, and misoyaki butterfish. Originally, I thought it was a typo (frying instead of flying) but its called frying because its fried on the outside. Loved the crispy crunchy outer coating on this roll.
history_reviews: [['110429535549061741595_604160297cd8bf130362515d', 'A number of years ago when we stayed at the Aria, we stumbled across Julian Serrano and had an amazing paella dish with our friends. When we finally decided to return to Vegas, the one thing that we knew that we couldnt miss out on was that paella (we pretty much planned our whole trip around it). Before we get to the paella, be forewarned that it takes about 45-60 minutes for them to prepare the paella. We decided to start with the Tuna Carpaccio ($24) made with big eye tuna, serrano peppers, yuzu and plankton oil. The tuna is so tender and the yuzu adds a nice citrus flavour thats enhanced by the spicy kick from the slice of serrano pepper. They actually have a number of different varieties of paella here but we were settled on having the Mixta ($65) which has an assortment of meat and seafood including lobster, mussels, shrimp, calamari, chicken, chorizo, and veggies thats cooked with saffron rice in a paella pan. One of the best paella dishes that Ive had. All of the meat and seafood was so tender and flavourful with the rice. The only thing you should keep in mind is that the mussel shells become really brittle so be careful when you pick them up as the shell might break. Seriously, Ive been looking at these pics of the paella for the last ten minutes and cant stop remembering how good it was.']]

review_text: HuHot is my favorite mongolian BBQ. Many other Mongolian BBQ places are single trip, HuHot is all you can eat. The sauce bar has many items other Mongolian BBQ restaurants lack, such as sesame oil, garlic broth, cooking sherry, and hot chili oil. The cooks here are excellent, they will even take special requests like "crispy noodles" or "add red pepper flakes" having them cooked on the grill rather than added afterwards, or even fry your rice with the food. They will also clean and prep the grill for those with seafood or peanut allergies. Another thing HuHot offers that others don't, is a selection of 3 noodle types, including ramen, & pad thai flat rice noodles. The asian salad included with dinner is a spring salad with crushed ramen noodles on top, a sweet asian vinaigrette, and a few mandarin wedges. Its a salad I've only seen one place come close to replicating. I would highly recommend this restaurant if you like mongolian BBQ.

So having grown up in San Antonio, and eaten puffy tacos at about a half dozen places, I decided to give this place a try. I was here for the food though, specifically puffy tacos. review_text: One may dismiss this pizzeria at first of being highly rated as it is the only one in Telluride with other towns quite a drive away but it has made me a believer. I would without hesitation, come back to Telluride again and again to have their great offering of pies be it the detroit style or american speciality. Though due to the current Covid situation they are not offering dine-in, we can easily say that they still care deeply about the pies they make and serving the community. review_text: Gordon Ramsay Burger is the definitive stop for a gourmet burger with elevated levels of flavor accompanied by service well above average. The onion rings make for a good starter and come with chipotle ketchup and southwest ranch for dipping. The chipotle ketchup is outstanding with the perfect level of smoke from the chipotle and sweetness from the ketchup. I ordered the Backyard Burger as my main and found it to be outstanding as well. A good 80/20 patty served with bibb lettuce, tomato, and cheese. Quality comes as a premium and double because of Gordon Ramsay's association with the restaurant with burgers starting at $17.
history_reviews: [['112327251491788648660_6050dda4d8c08f462b93e0a8', "Having looked at the menu before hand, we opted for the Tomahawk steak with sides of wild mushrooms and an onion petal. The steak was cooked perfectly to order and even though Mr. Gke wasn't there, our steak was still sliced tableside with signature Salt Bae flair from a gentleman who was equally as energetic. I knew well beforehand that it would be an expensive meal but I think it's well justified being as most of the steaks on the menu are certified wagyu."], ['112327251491788648660_60473975b3114911423b84ef', "Fish and chips is a true guilty pleasure of mine and more times than not it's the dish I'll order anytime I go to any seafood restaurant. Fresh, flaky, PERFECTLY cooked cod served with crispy fries (that can be elevated through upgrades like adding chorizo or truffle for an extra charge). Choices of dipping sauces are abundant and all tasty but tartar sauce and malt vinegar are the only two things I need to enjoy the fish. Thankfully the batter is perfectly balanced giving the perfect crunch ratio to the fish. Understand this, all the dishes are cooked to order so the fish is brought to the pass the moment it comes out of the fryer, meaning this is the freshest cooked fish served. The fish and chip combo is pretty affordable by Strip standards at $16 for a filling meal consisting of 3 large filets and fries."], ['112327251491788648660_605197b4c53d98b3eace1c38', 'As most of everyone on the West Coast will tell you, In-N-Out is the best fast food chain to satisfy a burger craving. Is it the absolute best burger money can buy?'], ['112327251491788648660_604162547cd8bf1303625275', "A good majority of Ramsay's famous dishes are available to order from the scallops to beef Wellington. I decided to not opt in for the Wellington, however, since it is only prepared medium rare and that's outside my comfort zone for being able to enjoy a filet. The start was an appetizer of wagyu meatballs with polenta croutons and fried basil. For the main, who could say no to a 32oz Tomahawk steak?"]]

review_text: Were blessed to have so many taco options in Orange County that its overwhelming to figure out which to try, and which ones stand out. I went with the Carne Asada, Chorizo, and Pollo Asado tacos. You might be better off ladling on the salsa straight onto the tacos. history_reviews: [['103107615285388876743_604143f8c6fcf1fddba123e7', 'Blueberry donuts. M&M Donuts is known for being one of the reliable sources of late night donut runs and is sure to make customers question their love for Krispy Kreme, and most notably one of the best blueberry donuts around. Im mainly going to commend them for this item alone, because its done so amazingly well that so far, no other donut shops compare. Its a cake donut thats perfectly dense but not to the point of chewing on bread, and fried so well every bite is like digging into a fritter. The blueberry flavour is very sweet and not hard hitting but not subtle; the flavour is just right. On the other hand, Ive also had the oreo donut that fell short after crushing a blueberry donut. The oreo crumb crust/dusting was soft, and the whole donut was not the same crispy sweet that I expected from the blueberry one. It was a very rich, very dense, chocolatey donut. There was a bit of a sharp sweetness to it like a glaze to sort of balance out the chocolate, but overall, its not something I can see myself trying again. M&Ms is one of OCs gems. Having donuts outside of OC is sure to make you miss this place.'], ['103107615285388876743_6045857c604fc398f591e6cf', 'I love this little place so damn much, I wrote a 700 word essay on why I love hot chicken. What makes this different from any other fried chicken joint? The chicken here was brought slaughtered in their sleep, making the meat more tender in conjunction with the brining. The essence of Nashville Hot Chicken is that the seasoning and spices are flash fried in oil from the fryer (similar to how Chinese hot oil is made) to "bloom" the flavours, and the chicken is then tossed in that seasoned oil. I always recommend to first timers to get the Sando, medium heat. The coleslaw in the Sando is not a typical scoop of heavy handed mayo filled cabbage. The acidity rounds out the sandwich so nicely and tames higher heats with the pickles. It\'s a steep price for a chicken sandwich, but you get a fat slab of boneless breast that\'s fried so well it\'s like biting into an incredibly tender steak with a well developed crust. This is a flavour bomb and I hate being that guy, but this really will ruin other chicken sandwiches for you. Mario style fries are also a must have! The normal fries are already incredibly seasoned, but Mario style fries (an off menu item) are essentially a Sando blown apart all over fries with cheese. Think animal style fries, but with coleslaw and hot chicken. I can\'t sing enough praise about this place, and it\'s hard to avoid the typical buzzwords such as crispy on the outside and juicy/tender "even for a breast" inside, but this really is the epitome of fried chicken done right.']]

Chilaquiles Benedict: A barbacoa style beef with green chili hollandaise and cotija cheese. Good texture on the beef. Their poached eggs were perfection. When you cut into it, the yolk just come oozing out beautifully. OMG French Toast: This is probably the best French toast I have had. The creamy sauce that accompanied it literally had me saying "omg". The milkiness of the vanilla creme and the soft texture of the French toast were amazing together. Now I know why it's called the OMG French toast. The Mmm Mmm Mimosa was an orange-based mimosa. The iced mocha had a dark flavor and not sweet.

I really enjoy their hybrid tacos, and their charro beans are great. Their tortas are also pretty good and filling. It's not truly traditional Mexican tacos, but it's pretty close. review_text: The food came out hot & the waffle had a great taste to it, the chicken was well seasoned & fried perfect.
history_reviews: [['100122726675357261870_604e5a88369254ee3f1d984c', 'I like my steak is rare or blue, which sometimes causes a cold in the meat before it can be reached, of course, when it is difficult to separate from the bone.'], ['100122726675357261870_60469e37b0e2129e47535335', "My friend and I went here this evening, she got the beef bowl and ramen combo and I went for the fried rice combo. Both come with a cabbage salad to start with this..amazing, sweet, Japanese mayo tasting dressing. The rice and beef bowl came out next, pretty fast really, and the first bites were heavenly. I can only speak for my rice but this was fresh steamed wok fried rice with some corn and meat and was so good I gave up on chopsticks and dove in with the spoon. I would have finished this honestly but the ramen came out next and I was dying to see how that tasted. The ramen bowl is huge, we both got the Tonkotsu broth though she got the optional kotteri and I chose their base. The pork chashu was perfect, could cut with chopsticks and practically melted at first bite. It comes, of course, with a soft boiled egg; not, I have never really liked the soft boiled  egg in my ramen just because they've always tasted odd. The ramen though. Not chewy, no weird flavoring that overshadowed the broth it was a perfect neutral to be tasty by itself from being soaked in the broth and paired with a sip of broth as well. Had I not devoured the salad and half the rice I would have drank the ramen bowl down but I was so full."], ['100122726675357261870_604a9f18b1a0aaee3eefbd41', 'I finally GET what the big deal is about with Chicago style pizza. Ordered the lots of meat deep dish pizza. While waiting, might as well have the suppli... basically arancini (breaded risotto stuffed with buffalo mozzarella) on a bed of tangy pomodoro sauce. Now the pizza... crust so light... non greasy. The Italian sausage had the perfect amount of sweetness and the fennel seeds not too heavy.']]

review_text: These are the bagels you've been looking for. Since returning to Houston, the Hot Bagel Shop is the only place that scratches the itch. They have quite a variety of bagels, probably 10-15. Their supreme (everything) bagel is perfect - they do not skimp on the seasoning one bit. My go-to order has become the supreme bagel with chive cream cheese. Im also fan of the jalapeo bagel, which sounded weird before I tried it, but was craveable after. I also enjoy the garlic onion bagel (again not dainty on the seasoning) and the vegetable cream cheese. When feeling extra peckish, I go for the traditional bagel and lox sandwich. In staying on brand, they load it with the toppings and each bite has a good balance of salmon, onion, capers, and tomato. Two bagels toasted with cream cheese is under 6 dollars.
history_reviews: [['106158651309276041679_60465ffa10ec061e056b4327', 'Summary: 6 out of 5, fantastic ramen. If youre so into ramen that you watch ramen documentaries on airplanes, you will enjoy this. One of the first foods we started researching here was ramen, because were obsessed. We went looking for the restaurant and we were just a little lost/confused at first, because High Five is underneath the inside part of Green Street Smoked Meats. Eating this ramen felt like how I imagine McDuck felt when he swam in his money (Im sorry again relapsed while reimagining the ramen). This was the best ramen I have had that was not in Japan and, yes, I know how obnoxious I am for making that statement. I mean this as a major compliment though, because it transported me right back to some of the best ramen I had in Tokyo, and it might be in my top 5 best bowls of ramen ever. Its just hard to find such a rich, cloudy, spicy broth combination over here. For what its worth, I have a friend here in Chicago who regularly entertains business clients from Japan, and they always request High Five ramen if they can fit it into their schedules because its the only place in the city that meets his clients standards.'], ['106158651309276041679_60415c497cd8bf1303624fa4', 'Their buns are absolutely delectable, they have Asahi on tap, and they have a lot of bar seating, which makes it a great place to walk in casually. The Miso Bold & Spicy ramen is my favorite here. The broth is chicken-based, but it still has a creamy and rich quality. There was enough fatty opacity to it for me to come back even though I tend to go for the richest and spiciest pork broths.'], ['106158651309276041679_605506f53019cb0a47838762', 'These burgers are top notch excellence. There are 6-8 beers on tap and probably 20+ in bottles. The Maillard was essentially an elevated take on the classic greasy dive bar onion burger. They really load it up with the crispy onions which makes the texture awesome and the burger look like an advertisement when it comes to your table. El Jefe is a delicious mess. Again the beef was moist throughout, and then you get the fried egg and chipotle mayo on top. Im fairly certain they make the chipotles in house because the flavor was stronger, spicier, and smokier than anything you would get in a can. We asked for a side of it for our fries which I would HIGHLY recommend. After finally trying this place Im confident all of the burgers will be great.I fully intend to return to try their award winning foie gras and truffle pesto burger.'], ['106158651309276041679_60415d2b7dfa7f1871836081', 'The Pork Belly Home Fries are UNREAL.'], ['106158651309276041679_604f568688c7af3f893e644d', 'It tasted like clam chowder, without all the good parts of clam chowder. 2 - Chicken Fried Rabbit. The cooks here are excellent, they will even take special requests like "crispy noodles" or "add red pepper flakes" having them cooked on the grill rather than added afterwards, or even fry your rice with the food. So having grown up in San Antonio, and eaten puffy tacos at about a half dozen places, I decided to give this place a try. I was here for the food though, specifically puffy tacos. The menu contained a variety of your regular Mexican plates, and shortly after ordering, my plate of puffy tacos along with a little basket of chips and salsa arrived. The actual puffy taco here were a little different from other places I'd had them. Many places the taco is doughy, thicker with a flaky outside and moist corn center. Rays tacos were thinner shells, inflated up while frying with little to no center, however a bit chewier than other places. Other than the minor difference in the shell, the picadillo meat, and toppings of (cheese, lettuce, & chopped tomato) were much on par with the puffy tacos I've had many a place. Overall, the tacos were good, the service OK, and the prices fair, but the location is buried a bit on the west side. Its an out of the way location if your not in the neighborhood, but seeing how Ray's is a long local establishment, its worth a trip to check out the place the Puffy Taco started."], ['108976745273958544598_604d234a77e81aaed3cca5e0', 'Tried the new shrimp stuffed poblanos. Many other Mongolian BBQ places are single trip, HuHot is all you can eat. The sauce bar has many items other Mongolian BBQ restaurants lack, such as sesame oil, garlic broth, cooking sherry, and hot chili oil. The cooks here are excellent, they will even take special requests like "crispy noodles" or "add red pepper flakes" having them cooked on the grill rather than added afterwards, or even fry your rice with the food. They will also clean and prep the grill for those with seafood or peanut allergies. Another thing HuHot offers that others don\'t, is a selection of 3 noodle types, including ramen, & pad thai flat rice noodles. The asian salad included with dinner is a spring salad with crushed ramen noodles on top, a sweet asian vinaigrette, and a few mandarin wedges. Its a salad I\'ve only seen one place come close to replicating. I would highly recommend this restaurant if you like mongolian BBQ.'], ['108976745273958544598_60560dc397d555cc6fb0d081', 'On this most recent visit, there was sushi that was either frozen to the tray, or had been sitting long enough it had dried and glued itself to the tray. Over the years I had people mention Rays to me. Apparently a long time argument has been going on about who the original creator of the Puffy Taco is. So having grown up in San Antonio, and eaten puffy tacos at about a half dozen places, I decided to give this place a try. I was here for the food though, specifically puffy tacos. The menu contained a variety of your regular Mexican plates, and shortly after ordering, my plate of puffy tacos along with a little basket of chips and salsa arrived. The actual puffy taco here were a little different from other places I'd had them. Many places the taco is doughy, thicker with a flaky outside and moist corn center. Rays tacos were thinner shells, inflated up while frying with little to no center, however a bit chewier than other places. Other than the minor difference in the shell, the picadillo meat, and toppings of (cheese, lettuce, & chopped tomato) were much on par with the puffy tacos I've had many a place. Overall, the tacos were good, the service OK, and the prices fair, but the location is buried a bit on the west side. Its an out of the way location if your not in the neighborhood, but seeing how Ray's is a long local establishment, its worth a trip to check out the place the Puffy Taco started."], ['108976745273958544598_6055ce7a97d555cc6fb0cf09', "I ordered the General Chicken, the portion size was more than enough. history_reviews: [['118212091475287291147_60512d695b4ccec8d5caeaaa', 'We ordered  Jacks Blazin BBQ Cheeseburger (w/ bbq sauce on side and sub cheddar for Monterrey Jack) with side of fries for $13.99, Tex-Mex Egg Rolls $10.99, Classic French Onion Soup $5.99, and a la carte loaded baked potato and side of onion rings. The meat patty and bacon were so very flavorful on their own, there was no need for anything else to enhance it. The onion rings were large and crisp as they should be.'], ['118212091475287291147_60437353ad733fba1bcfd480', 'Tonight we tried the Balls on a stick( 3 meatballs) and we chose the Lamb meatballs. For dinner we ordered Meatball Smash which is a smashed meatball served on a ciabatta bread and it was served with a house salad, and we ordered the Lasagna Bolognese and added a Chicken Parmesan meatball. The lasagna was quite flavorful and big enough that Im taking 1/3 of it home for lunch tomorrow. The Meatball Smash was a decent size and also quite tasty. For dessert, we tried a Cannoli (small and pretty good)and the Mascarpone Impastata which was really really delightful and worth stopping in just for that. I ordered mine with just onion (I dont like lettuce and tomato on a burger) and it was a whole thin thin slice of onion. Without condiments, the burger really didnt have much taste...even adding Mayo and ketchup wasnt enough. The bun was brioche and tasty. The fries are crinkle cut and seasoned and the onion rings were thick onions with the perfect amount of crispy batter on the outside. The grilled chicken was of a good portion and tasty. The green beans (veg of the day) and mashed potatos with brown gravy were both tasty. The chicken noodle soup was also tasty. Each of these entrees were between $8.99 and $9.99. The Bayou Burger is a handcrafted Andouille sausage and turkey burger and topped with blackened shrimp, finished with remounted, sriracha and house made Rajun Cajun slaw. I have to say that the Bayou Burger was quite a bit more spicy than I could enjoy. The spice masked the flavors of the burger so much that I cant really say what or how its tasted. The shrimps were cooked a bit too long as they were a bit rubbery. The Black and Blue burger is one of our standard orders when we visit and it was tasty as always. The fries were cooked right but quite a bit over salted tonight. I love that Burger21 features a new specialty burger each month and Im glad I tried the Bayou Burger. I knew it would be spicy but was a little surprised at how spicy it is. There are many people that like a whole lot of spice and I know they will love this burger.']]

review_text: MXICO . Eat the World NYC review:. Without much fanfare, the fourth branch of Los Tacos No. The wildly popular Tijuana-style taco spot, lauded as the "best tacos NYC has to offer" by many folks has still been unable to keep up with demand as lines at the original Chelsea Market location are almost always out of control. Eating a taco is a spiritual experience for some people, an attack on your senses from all directions if done properly. You might see smoke from the carne asada blocks away from a street vendor you are approaching, then start smelling it when getting closer. If there is any complaint about Los Tacos No. The tortillas themselves make the taco worth double of its street counterparts, and that is not even mentioning the much higher quality ingredients.
history_reviews: [['100628241609761386745_6050fb6bd8c08f462b93e175', 'As might be determined from the name, biriyani is the absolute star here and nothing like some of the dishes labeled as such around town. There are too many instances of spiced rice and meat dishes getting this name, but kacchi biriyani (here spelled kachey) needs a long cooking process, the meat and the rice must slow cook together. This type of preparation requires someone with extraordinary attention to detail to make sure the meat is cooked just right.'], ['100628241609761386745_6043525ac6fcf1fddba1aa8a', "EL SALVADOR . Eat the World NYC review:. Sometimes a human being just needs a quick pupusa fix. A recent return visit also found the hearty soups to be worth exploring, full of chayote and warmth perfect any time of year. : Don't eat pupusas with a fork and knife you animal!"], ['100628241609761386745_605228ecf09a4ffff042f923', ' USA (New Mexico). Excerpt from Eat the World Los Angeles:. The Green Chile calls itself the "Home of the Stuffed Sopapilla," so it only makes sense to start with one. Depending on your choice of meat or vegetables to stuff it with, the price can fluctuate a dollar, but the pork green chile filling for this one comes in at $9.99, with the $2 addition of sauces smothered on top.'], ['100628241609761386745_60545e8d80c04bd7072f2507', 'Noodle soups come in three options all for $5 each here, small portions that allow for the table to order quite a few other dishes without filling up too fast. What translates on their English menu as "braised pork noodle" is nam tok, full of thinly sliced cuts and balls. The broth trends a bit towards the sweet side but naturally this soup desires to be spicy, so ask for the condiment rack and go for it.'], ['100628241609761386745_604133887cd8bf13036240db', 'The spicy broth contains potatoes, some greenery, onions, peppers, and ground sesame. A longtime favorite Korean late night drinking food is budae jjigae ($12.50), which probably translates to "hot dog soup" in English. That is a lie, but hot dogs make up a good volume underneath the vibrant red broth along with Spam, kimchi, recently unpackaged dry ramen noodles, and chewy rice cakes.'], ['100628241609761386745_604ef3f1d91e93df8e796c70', "Afternoons are a great time to come here to sample the kitchen's wonderful food, including this fish pepper soup, ranking high on the list of top spicy dishes."], ['100628241609761386745_6048728cf9e05764f1fa5400', 'MXICO (BAJA) . Excerpt from Eat the World Los Angeles:. In its 21 years of life in San Diego (and almost 50 in Tijuana), Tacos El Gordo has reached essential status. You would think the heart and soul of Tijuana-style tacos would be easy to replicate so close to the border and in Southern California in general, but as with everything the scene takes on a life of its own and goes elsewhere. If you happen to come to Tacos El Gordo on H Street during a rare off hour, you might be bewildered by the amount of open space in the entry, seemingly unused. To be sure, the lines near the trompo and for carne asada are always hefty, and this should guide a meal for any beginner. When eating tacos here there are many things that set them apart, starting with the fresh little tortillas that are still warm from the station creating them. Tacos de adobada ($2.60 c/u) are a natural place to start, what the place is known for above all else, and just such a pleasure. They slather each with that legendary creamy runny avocado salsa that could never be replicated in a hundred attempts in your own kitchen.'], ['100628241609761386745_6048b147f9e05764f1fa5805', "One way to stay in the zone of a sports bar while sampling a South African favorite is by eating the Jan Van Riebeecks boerewors roll ($14.95), named for a Dutch colonizer from the 1600's. This all beef sausage is made in house but in the style of a typical South African link, which has standards of low fat content, spicing, and never using offal or processed meats."], ['100628241609761386745_604b6f9920f26f37fb9d7bd1', 'The combination above included jollof rice, seasoned beef, and fried sweet plantains. On a second trip back to the cart (below), baked seasoned chicken and sweet potatoes were swapped out. His vegan jollof rice had to stay, as it was very tasty. West African food that leaves you feeling light as a feather.'], ['100628241609761386745_6052510125ef3e7701941f5f', '. For another filling Balkan specialty try evapi. Here the perfectly prepared leaves are stuffed with a mixture of ground beef, pork, and rice and drowned in a wonderful savory sauce. These sausages are skinless as always and heroically juicy in their preparation. Use your hands to tear of a piece of the warmed pita, wrap a sausage and dip into the red pepper ajvar.'], ['100628241609761386745_60545f7c4b7f30a9c0a50dc8', 'Every option is seafood, and the fish and octopus tacos definitely stand out. Try the shark (dogfish) flautas for something truly unique, shredded shark meat with cheese inside of fried tortillas, and smother it with their oily homemade green salsa.'], ['100628241609761386745_6042594a2e57ebdea29c9c2b', ". Anyone that loves Japanese food, and especially ramen, is supposed to come here for their famous tsukemen, tonkotsu broth that is simmered for a full 60 hours, sweetened and thickened by seafood. . The standard bowl of tonkotsu ramen is also available here for those that prefer everything at one time. JAPAN . Eat the World LA review:. Not to be outdone by downtown's Little Tokyo, the small area on Sawtelle Blvd with many Japanese businesses became known as Little Osaka. Tsukemen is served as components, you do the addition and subtraction yourself, usually dipping the noodles as you go. If you need more broth, it can be refilled. Ajitama tsukemen is broth with a seasoned soft boiled egg, it is also available plain or with char siu. After you finish your noodles, ask for them to pour in some light broth to the dipping sauce and enjoy the resulting soup on its own."], ['100628241609761386745_604b26c977e81aaed3cc91df', 'The steam table is stocked with the namesake ribs and many other types of meats, as well as a wide variety of southern-style side dishes.'], ['100628241609761386745_605641293019cb0a47838c94', 'Sichuan food is of course known for its high heat levels, but Land of Plenty prides itself in bringing all seven important components of desired tastes: Hot, sour, pungent, sweet, bitter, aromatic, and salty. Spicy dry cold noodle dishes always seem to excel in Sichuan cooking and the chilled noodles with spicy sesame peanuts dressing ($7.45) was no exception and my favorite dish of the meal.'], ['100628241609761386745_604369479b00092d7286c389', 'The offerings in this dish included shrimp, squid, meaty hunks of whitefish, one large clam, and some strips of yuca, all fried.'], ['100628241609761386745_604603c810ec061e056b3aca', 'The promise of "just pho" is almost accurate, as the menu concentrates on four versions of the noodle soup, cooked in the Northern Vietnamese style which you might find in Hanoi. Pho b ti ($11 for small/$13 for large) is their signature "raw" beef pho. The thin strips of beef will cook themselves in the bowl, arriving slightly pink but quickly changing to brown. As you will find in Hanoi, the broth does not arrive super complex and full of different savory, sweet, and/or funky elements as a bowl in Saigon might. The soup base is simple and savory, with hints of anise and cinnamon and possibly cloves. Instead, thinly sliced green onion and cilantro is added before serving. This is the real magic, as their house made vinegar-garlic-chili sauce (toi ngam giam) is just waiting to do tricks for you. Once the pungency levels are to your tastes, add a squirt of sriracha for the necessary kick and pick up the wide noodles found in northern-style phos.']]

review_text: After we were seated, we ordered the fried cod and shrimp tacos (this was where we made the mistake--should have just gotten the lobster roll). The cod came with fries and some coleslaw. Fish was fried well but so greasy and almost dripping with oil. I barely wanted to eat it and ended up peeling off the fried skin and just ate the fish inside. The fries and slaw were great though. The fried shrimp tacos were pretty big, but the shrimp was soggy and suuuper salty. The tortilla was very soggy as well, so I ended up just eating everything in the taco with a fork. The tacos also came with a bag of chips but we already felt so greased up by the fish that we ended up not opening the bag up.
history_reviews: [['107548322316470513394_60415a40c6fcf1fddba12e25', 'While browsing the menu, we were served some spicy picked cabbage which definitely had quite a kick to it. Some other highly recommended dishes: buttermilk fried chicken, octopus a la plancha, hanger steak, short rib, bruschetta, and paella. I have yet to have a better paella dish in Chicago.'], ['107548322316470513394_60415df32e57ebdea29c3c0c', "I was so surprised by how much I liked my experience at Prosecco! We got Salsiccia (grilled Italian sausage), Tartufate (orecchiette, cremini, asparagus, sun-dried tomatoes, black truffle cream, Grana Padano, white truffle oil), and a farfalle pasta special that had smoked and fresh salmon. The sausage had good flavor and wasn't too salty, and the pastas were cooked perfectly al dente. We were surprised by how filling the portions were, both the antipasti and pastas. There was a ton of salmon in the farfalle special, and the Tartufate really hit the truffle-flavor craving I had without being too greasy or creamy."], ['107548322316470513394_604158cfc6fcf1fddba12da2', 'Every "classic" Chinese dish is super solid here, including the spicy beef noodles (not really spicy but noodles are super chewy), soup dumplings, mapo tofu, green beans, etc. One thing you MUST GET is the eggplant in garlic sauce. Best eggplant I\'ve ever had.'], ['107548322316470513394_604157bd7cd8bf1303624c81', "The Peking duck dinner is really the only thing you should be coming for, because they roast a spectacular duck here and I haven't had better in the city. The rest of the food on the menu is just okay--Chinatown has better. For four people, one duck dinner is just about enough, which comes with a large plate of sliced duck, six bao buns, a plate of fried rice, and a large bowl of soup. I'd recommend ordering extra buns since the meat will definitely outnumber the pieces of buns that you have, and a vegetable dish for health. The server brings out the roasted duck whole, and will carve/slice it table-side. It's always a spectacle to watch, and the meat is always super juicy, fatty, and crispy, all in one bite. The fried rice and soup are average, but complements the duck meat nicely. If you have five or more people in your group, it'd be a good idea to get two ducks. Sometimes near the end of the day they run out of ducks which is just about the saddest thing the waiter can tell you after you've been seated."], ['107548322316470513394_60415b797dfa7f1871835f97', 'Compared with other Chinatown dim sum restaurants, everything just tastes more flavorful and larger portions, albeit with slightly higher prices (avg $15 per person). They put real shrimp in the har gow (not paste) and theres like 4 shrimp in each dumpling. The siu mai is ginormous as well and filled with whole shrimp. My favorite dim sum here are the beef short ribs and the pineapple bun custard buns that literally explode with that sweet, gooey filling every single time.'], ['107548322316470513394_6046e75705aec66848d1c66f', "Usually you're only able to do half pies of the classics (margherita, marinara, white, calzone), but we asked if we could do two half pies of the margherita and the no. The mango lassi isn't as mango-y as I would like, but again, I have no complaints based on how large the portions are and how cheap the food is."], ['107548322316470513394_60415fe17cd8bf130362511a', "Brunch is Asian inspired, and I've tried their Vietnamese iced coffee, corn elotes, pandan French toast, and catfish banh mi. For entrees, we got the angel hair aglio e olio, and the penne with chicken, mozzarella, and tomato cream, and a side of the sweet corn. The sweet corn was surprisingly good, it was popping with flavor and buttery goodness. The two pastas were great contrasts, but we didnt find either to be particularly strong-flavored.'], ['107548322316470513394_60415e4f2e57ebdea29c3c2a', "I'd especially recommend the lamb kefta, short rib shakshuka, and khachapuri, which was kind of like pizza but on puff pastry. The noodles are cooked to perfection, and the sauce and toppings are simple but strong in flavor. As with the other pasta dishes, you can get a half order instead of a full order, which is what I got, and I still left feeling very full. The chocolate cake is TO DIE FOR!!! There are so many layers to this cake, and each layer showcases a different texture of chocolate, so there's crispiness in it, ganache, cream, sponge cake, and so on."], ['107548322316470513394_60415e8d7cd8bf13036250e4', "Firecakes is my favorite donut shop in Chicago. These are miles better than the cake donuts (although those are pretty good too). I also love their filled donuts. I'm not usually a big fan of coffee or chocolate flavors, but their valrhona chocolate and espresso donut is particularly scrumptious. I don't think the ice cream donuts are particularly special, but they do make for a delicious treat to share."], ['107548322316470513394_60415dd32e57ebdea29c3bfc', 'For two people, we were recommended to get 5-6 dishes (though I think 4 would have been satisfactory), and got the brioche buns, green beans, salmon poke, pig face, pork shank, and two drinks. review_text: ~Food~. I got the Chef's Favorite Burger which comes with a Parmesan crisp sheet, bacon, ketchup leather (similar to fruit roll up), fried egg and hot sauce. ~Drinks~. The Orange Smash is basically homemade Julius. The burger was presented in a small cast iron container, the bun was slightly tilted to the side, and the perfect sunny side up egg was placed on top! This burger was cooked to perfection, beef patty was juicy, the egg was exquisite, the bacon was long and crispy. This is the first flawless burger I've ever tasted! The second time I came here, I got the Southern Fry, it had Smokey fried Jidori chicken, spicy green pimento cheese, duck breast ham and pickles. We decided to try the Tres Leche Cruller Donut. It is a single Donut with Tres Leche Caramel, toasted coconut, sugar, and whip cream. It was warm, flaky, and sweet; reminded me of a regular sugar donut.

review_text: The main dish I got was the Pad Thai (rice noodles, shrimp, chicken, eggs, bean sprouts, carrots, spring onions, red chili pepper, roasted peanuts, lime). Small Plate 1: Korean Twice Fried Wings (garlic Gochujang sauce, peanuts, sesame, cilantro). I didn't get a strong taste of gochujang, so it's not actually spicy, but the flavor was good, strong with sesame. The shrimp and the pork were formed into a solid mass, like a dense crab cake, and fried in strings and strings of batter rolled into balls. Order extra roti, though, for $1.50 each, because a lot of what you eat will have some extra sauce left over that you can sop up like a tortilla. Small Plate 4: Singapore 'Chilli' Crab (national dish of Singapore, soft-shelled crab, house-made chili garlic sauce, fried bao bun). The crab was fried to perfection and the sauce was so flavorful.
history_reviews: [['118020893387833644953_60512d695b4ccec8d5caeaaa', 'Their nachos is like 8 nachos with all the toppings on each nacho.'], ['118020893387833644953_604ba99020f26f37fb9d7d9a', "It was a soft, buttery, fluffy round flatbread that went well with all of the sauces! We got a Oak-grilled Filet Mignon (Bobotie Macaroni and Cheese, Grilled Asparagus, Kachumbari, South African Red Wine Sauce). Cooked medium rare. This steak was very good. The mac & cheese was awesome. The asparagus was grilled nicely, but I would have liked to have seen more than two sprigs on the plate. The mixed veggies added a great acidity to the dish, and the rich red wine sauce tied it all together. We got the Bo Kaap Malay Seafood Curry (Lobster, Calamari, Red Shrimp, Mussels, Coconut-Curry Sauce, Saffron Rice). The seafood was infused with the flavor of the star of the show, the coconut-curry sauce. It was a nice, slightly sweet curry that blended well with the aromatic saffron rice. I have never ordered a dish like this (seafood slathered in warm sauce with rice or pasta) that there wasn't at least one piece of the seafood that was overcooked. Most surprisingly, the calamari was cooked well!"], ['118020893387833644953_6043749bb81264dfa846bc01', "It's a labor of love, it's accentuated by sauce, and it's usually very obvious which barbecue is better than another barbecue. They sell all the meat by weight, or you can buy a sandwich. I can't remember what it was all about word-for-word, but it was a brisket sandwich with some sauteed onions on there, but the special part of it was that it had fried crispy onion strips on there and a horseradish sauce. I skipped the sauce, sorry, but man, this brisket was out of this world. I think it might have been better than 4Rivers', but to be fair, it's been a long time since I've eaten anything from 4Rivers that wasn't their burnt ends, because those things are heaven. I also had a side of mac 'n' cheese, and it was also darling."], ['118020893387833644953_6055b33697d555cc6fb0ce82', 'After some careful consideration, I decide to get the special of the day, a New York Strip, some amazing mashed potatoes, and a bunch of grilled green onions and peppers of some sort.
