My two fixins of choice were Fresh Fried Okra and Creamed Corn. I gotta tell you, The Coop has some of the best chicken and waffles in all of Orlando. The breading on the tenders is light and flaky and adds that nice crunch you want. The waffles is obviously freshly made in a waffle maker. The okra was good. My girlfriend, on the other hand, got the New Orleans Po-Boy (shrimp) with a fixin of the Bread Pudding. The shrimp was cooked well, but the sandwich just wasn't bursting with flavor like you want."], ['118020893387833644953_6045ac1c10ec061e056b3386', 'I got the Vietnamese Ice Coffee (Vietnamese-Grown Dark Roasted Coffee Brewed into Sweetened Condensed Milk and poured over Ice), which was super sweet. Just imagine an iced coffee thickened with sweetened condensed milk. My girlfriend got the Spiced Lavender Mocha (Espresso, Dark Chocolate, Earthy Spices, Lavender, Steamed Milk), which tasted like we were drinking flowers. Brioche French toast, topped with tender pulled pork, tomato, poached eggs, hollandaise, crispy Cheshire Farms bacon) and the # Tag This Hash (Braised short rib hash, potato hash cakes, avocado smash, sauted squash topped with over easy egg and chimichurri served with sauted fresh vegetables).'], ['118020893387833644953_6043d04dcc4f7990c6579a4d', 'First thing\'s first, we ordered a half-dozen of the Char-Grilled Oysters (Romano, parmesan, Roux compound butter). For my entree, I ordered the Alligator Hash (Crispy beer-battered alligator bites, garlic potatoes, sunny-side up egg, hollandaise and red "remi" remoulade). I\'m used to gimmicky fried gator on a stick when it\'s all chewy and stuff, but this gator was tender and absolutely delightful. I also got to sample the Crawfish Hash (Andouille and crawfish hash, garlic potatoes, sunny-side up egg and hollandaise). There were a TON of crawfish tails. The sausage was a welcome Cajun taste. For dessert, we ordered the NOLA Style Beignets (Five light and puffy beignets covered in powdered sugar).'], ['118020893387833644953_604642d4882f4d1caf5fed3c', "We were putting on a charity event where a percentage of Burger Fi's profits were going towards our class organization, so we all pitched in and did the hard work. My girlfriend and I each got a burger and split an order of the Cry+Fry (Onion Rings + Hand-Cut Fries). The fries were good. Not just fries, because they're fried in peanut oil, just like at Chick-Fil-A. And the onion rings were absolutely fantastic. Now for the burgers. I got the Breakfast All Day Burger (Natural Angus Burger, American Cheese, Bacon, Maple Syrup, Fried Egg, Hash Brown, Grilled Onions, Ketchup), and my girlfriend got The CEO (Double Wagyu + Brisket Blend Burger, Homemade Candied Bacon-Tomato Jam, Truffle Aioli, Aged Swiss Cheese). My burger was very good. The beef patty was delicious, the cheese and the bacon were on point, the maple syrup I actually couldn't tell it was there honestly, the fried egg was good, and the hash brown was strangely enough the thing on the burger that I would be the saddest if it was missing. We've all had breakfast burgers before, but the hash brown was the unique twist here, and I am a big fan. The whole thing also wasn't too greasy, which surprised me consider it was a beef patty, bacon, and a fried egg. Well done, Burger Fi. My girlfriend's burger was very interesting. I understand that Wagyu is a premium ingredient, but when you cut it down with brisket and then make a patty so thin that you can't get anything more out of it than well done, it's honestly a little bit disappointing. It was ok, but I definitely wouldn't have guessed that it was made with Wagyu if I didn't already know. Also, there was nowhere near enough jam on that burger. Tomato jam is such a wonderful addition to meals sometimes, that I was excited, but alas, more disappointment. If you like burgers come here, but don't expect gourmet."], ['118020893387833644953_60540c7b4b7f30a9c0a50c1e', 'I got the Crispy Fried Chicken & Waffles (Crispy Chicken Breast / Belgian Style Waffle / House Syrup). The chicken was cooked perfectly with the breading falling off the chicken like it was hand-breaded and the soft waffle with the crisp exterior. The syrup came poured on the sandwich. My girlfriend got the Fried Green Tomato BLT Biscuit (Smoked Pork Bacon Avocado Puree, Local Greens, Sweet Corn "Caviar" on Two (2) Buttermilk Biscuits). Sauteed up potatoes with peppers and onions.'], ['118020893387833644953_6043d146b81264dfa846ceef', 'On top of it being Valentine\'s Day, I\'m also on a conquest to see The Best of Orlando 2020, and Izziban won the best Korean restaurant in Orlando, according to the readers of Orlando Weekly. We got the All-You-Can-Eat Korean BBQ, which is a flat $37. You get access to their salad bar, along with 13 different meats you can cook, various sides, nigiri, and sushi rolls. I tried to go full meat at first, to "get my money\'s worth," and I found myself bored. What\'s a nice slice of brisket for if not to have with a bite of fried rice? What\'s the point of cooking a head-on shrimp if I can\'t put the results of it on a crunchy baguette? I recommend every meat they offer, but I will say, skip the rib-eye. The steak is too big, and it\'s not good enough to sacrifice that stomach space. Skip the rib-eye in favor of other meats. Speaking of stomach space, a tip is that you can order full portions of the meats, or you can ask for a half order. I had two sushi rolls, the Crunch Shrimp and the Yummi Yummi. Not top tier sushi by any means, but delicious and good relief from all the heavy meat and fried sides. Don\'t forget to start with the miso soup. Cooking your own meat on your personal grill was like an upgraded Melting Pot experience.'], ['118020893387833644953_605384c880c04bd7072f2129', "We split The Family Feast (1lb wangs, 1 Whole Chicken, 1lb Pork, 1lb Brisket, 1lb Serious Sausage, 1 Rack Baby Backs, 1 Rack Spare Ribs. The heaps of pickles and onions that the fest came with made for a great sandwich with some slices of the loaf of bread we got. -The chopped up brisket was the second best thing about the feast. The pork broth for the ramen was great. The ramen egg was over cooked. When cooking ramn egg, there shouldn't be a gritty consistency in the yolk like a hard boiled egg. Most of the yolk should be soft and a hit runny. This is a result of boiling the eggs for a few seconds too long (yes 10 to 15 seconds of boiling matters when making ramen eggs. Look it up) The ramen can be marinated a bit longer. You can tell by looking at the outside of the eggs and seeing that it is dark while the part near the yolk is still white and flavorless. The charsiu needs to be greatly improved to be like Japanese ramen. Look at the attached images, the piece of meat is way too thick. And the shape of the charsiu was not round meaning the piece of meat was not tied together when cooking and marinating. The hard part (getting the broth right) is already done. From a ramen stand point, if the owner improves the cooking method for the ramen eggs and somehow fixes the charsiu issue, this place will be golden. Would still recommend if one does not have very high standards and wants a bowl of good tasting ramen."], ['111216018953115987906_6042608db9a6829e686e95c2', 'Would recommend if you are looking for quality ramen.'], ['111216018953115987906_605395ff7fec92c07c643ca2', 'I recommend the kitchen sink, red velvet pancakes, and the crab mac & cheese.']]

It came with the best lime crema sauce to put on them too."], ['107444333383263433673_604ec4df9755094ba8abde27', "I usually hear about these donuts from Portland travelers, but when I saw there was one in Denver (two actually), I obviously had to try it on my trip. My husband and I decided to split three donuts because we couldn't narrow what to get down more than that. We got Mango Tango, Key Lime Crush, and Guava Colada. The key lime filling wasn't quite as good to me (which isn't surprising given how much I love mango), but the toppings were the best. The coconut didn't really enhance the donut for me, but I'm also not a huge coconut person. The donut carousel would be perfect for deciding what flavor to get. If you're a donut lover, this is definitely a place you need to check out!"], ['107444333383263433673_6050b4a94cd354c57204c140', "We definitely wanted to try oysters so we decided to go all out and got the Cadillac stack which came with 12 oysters, poke, mahi dip, and pickled shrimp. The cookie was crunchy on the outside and gooey on the inside. It was a fat cookie."], ['107444333383263433673_60430741cc4f7990c6577e09', "You can't find better pastries. The seeded roast beef and Croque Monsieur are my favorite sandwiches. Their soups are also very good."], ['107444333383263433673_604ae5066b6b79a4bb4810fc', 'Upon arriving in Miami, our first stop was to get a Cuban. Trigo was like a Cheerios milkshake and Mamey tasted like a cross between a sweet potato and a melon.'], ['107444333383263433673_60430c56c6fcf1fddba19e22', "The service was really friendly, but when I asked what custom soda flavors they had they said they didn't know the full list because they can make a lot of different flavors. review_text: Its a little bakery/cafe located in Greektown that we came across after lunch, so we decided to stop by for coffee and dessert. The woman working behind the counter was very funny - when I asked her what the best pastry was, she said they all were. Theres traditional Greek desserts like baklavas the size of my palm and other pastries like cakes and tarts. We ended up getting the strawberry shortcake and a walnut baklava. The barista there was also very funny and asked a lot of questions to make sure we got the flavor we wanted from our iced Greek coffees (I got sweet with milk, my friend got black). The strawberry shortcake was light and fluffy, and had real strawberry pieces inside. There was a fair amount of white frosting but it wasnt overly sweet. It was sweetened with a generous portion of honey and the crushed walnuts lent such a lovely texture against the phyllo dough. The bill was ~$23 for the two frappes and two desserts. Its authentic, family-owned, the desserts are delicious, and the coffee is strong - what more do you want?
history_reviews: [['105853218368004682403_605728a39ffe343acca5fc9c', 'They skimped on the Cajun fries, which was disappointing. That being said, I was glad to finally have been able to try the much hyped spicy chicken sandwich. The sandwich is much bigger than the equivalent chickfila sandwich, but the spiciness comes from the sauce rather than the chicken itself. I liked how the chicken was breaded and it was still crunchy even after the 20 minute car ride home. The sandwich does come with pickles, and you can get a non-spicy sandwich (although the spicy sandwich is definitely manageable, and in the same level as hot Cheetos).'], ['105853218368004682403_6048c7438b84f513e32cdad6', 'He made sure to countdown so we could capture the giant flame he made for the bananas foster for the gram. They have aperitifs as well, and the Irish coffee was nicely sweet with a kick.'], ['105853218368004682403_6051e16bc53d98b3eace1d8b', 'The poutine was good, although I felt the gravy couldve couldve used a tad more salt and the cheese curds werent chewy.'], ['105853218368004682403_60570118c4674474cff9120f', 'I liked that the broth was separated from the noodles so you can mix it up yourself when youre ready to eat. The broth for the beef curry udon was watery and only had a hint of curry. The broth for the spicy pork ramen was better but it was not spicy at all. I would say the ABC ramen was the best of the three we had, although there were less pieces of meat than they typically provide.'], ['105853218368004682403_605680a03019cb0a47838d6b', 'The real MVP were the Irish coffee and strawberry daiquiris. The Irish coffee was mixed well with the coffee overpowering the whiskey (for the most part) but without being overly sweet. The strawberry daiquiri was dangerous as you cant really taste the alcohol and it just seems like a smoothie.'], ['105853218368004682403_604e0202b9a3d5528c50bc5b', 'I could wax poetic about the virtues of the Mexican chocolate pie at The Pie Hole, but to put it simply, the Pie Hole consistently has delicious desserts that are indulgent and rich. The Mexican chocolate pie is thick and creamy, while the earl grey pie is more light and airy, but grounded by the toasted pistachios that adorn its top. You should split the pies with loved ones, although its certainly doable to eat an entire slice by yourself. You can order a whole pie if youd like, and they do offer drinks like matcha tea and coffee. The cashier was very friendly and mentioned that they have happy hour from Monday through Friday where pie slices are $5 and whole pies are ~$30.'], ['105853218368004682403_604913b3b1a0aaee3eefa92e', 'The cheesecakes are a 5 but the food is a solid 3. For a family of four, we got an egg roll sampler, a regular size farfalle pasta with chicken and a garlic cream sauce, and two cheesecakes. The egg roll sampler was a good order since theres a variety to try and theres plenty of dipping sauce to choose from. My favorite was the avocado one, but everyone else really liked the hamburger egg roll dipped into the pink sauce (which I think is thousand island dressing). The pasta was disappointing - it was super oily with sparse amounts of chicken and accoutrements. The cheesecakes were the highlight - the godiva one is so decadent and rich, so its perfect for a chocolate fanatic. The white chocolate macadamia nut with the blondie brownie crust was also a surprise hit. The macadamia nuts were a bit soggy, but paired well with the white chocolate chunks. The bottom layer brownie was nice and and chewy, and complemented the creaminess of the cheesecake.'], ['105853218368004682403_6057007d6fce2069470c60cf', 'I used to love going to Raising Canes when I lived in Phoenix, so I was excited to get my chicken tender fix. This might be an LA thing, but the chicken tenders were a lot smaller and they really skimped on the fries. The chicken tenders are pretty bland, but the sauce is good. Its an extra 30 something cents per sauce but they do keep well if you want to use them for some home cooked chicken tenders. The fries are crinkle-cut and were under seasoned. The Texas toast was very good - it was still warm and buttery by the time we got to eat it. The combo also comes with coleslaw although you can request another piece of toast in lieu of it.'], ['105853218368004682403_60442190b81264dfa846d73c', 'Tried the Chicago hot dog - while it was a good hot dog, it certainly wasnt life changing. I liked the sesame seed bun and how soft it was. I liked the chili dog more - it wasnt soggy but still soft and I like the flavor of the chili.'], ['105853218368004682403_60497a77c7c8ee3104ba1994', 'Your typical fast food restaurant serving fried chicken and biscuits. review_text: Ordered the burnt end kettle corn and it was fabulous and exactly the kind of thing I expected here, it opened up my pallette for some awesome mains. My vinegar issue sidelined me from huge swaths of the menu and I ultimately settled on the pork belly. The celery was unnecessary but didn't detract. Boom, get to slice 3 and the vast majority of the slice is fat. Slice 8 and 9 were entirely fat. My companion ordered the brisket sandwich. What had been cryptic on the menu plainly showed as more allergen-laden ingredients that weren't fully disclosed-- onions as part of a weird Asian slaw on the sandwich. For $15 you get a sandwich. No sides, no chips, just meat and a bun (if you don't have an allergy also slaw stuff and aioli). Because they left us the slawed sandwich and I was still starving after my $12 pork belly fiasco, I scraped all the slaw and the top layer of brisket and sucked it up to eat the messed up sandwich. Brisket is exactly what you expect from Franklin's, juicy and delicious. The service itself was fine, but the pork belly was a total waste of $12 and the $15 brisket sandwich left me hungry for more. That said the $3.50 burnt end kettle corn is fabulous, the brisket is good even if I wanted more, and they aren't busy around 1pm.

We also really enjoyed the turkey!'], ['106271335081562183513_60503e1088c7af3f893e6a78', 'Authentic Korean- Friendly Staff- Delicious Bibimbap. . My wife and I tried this restaurant at random. The rest of the banchan came out after that and we honestly tore through it in a way that I hope garnered the respect of the wait staff (or pity, Ill accept either). The kimchi was good, very saucy and spicy, but with no horrific after taste like the kind you buy at Whole Foods. The odeok was very soft and chewy and great with gochujang. The salad was also delicious and excellent with a little bit of gochujang. I ordered kimchi dol sot bibimbap and my wife just ordered regular dol sot bibimbap, though she did ask for beef in it. Hers was the superior bap, as mine was a simple mix of kimchi, rice, and a fried egg. We also got gunmandu (fried dumplings) but we ate them all before I could get a photo. This was a simple soup which I found very creamy despite being mostly tofu.'], ['106271335081562183513_604ca32f3ada919c27677b80', 'Zeppole. These were somewhere between the pice de rsistance and a coup de grce. Butternut Squash Agnolotti. This was recommended by the sympathetic Kara and was really surprising! Affogato. At this point, entranced by the warm scenery and glow of the grill fire, we were pliable to the power of suggestion and ordered both of the desserts recommended by Kara. Butter lettuce salad. A light salad, the Gorgonzola vinaigrette dressing was complex and bitter, offering first the mustiness of the cheese followed by creamy, peppery flavors. Fusilli. My wife ordered this and found it exceedingly rich and robust. The onions were sweet and pungent, cutting through the fatty porcine savor of the bacon. The lettuce itself was exceedingly smooth in the mouth, a texture that the creamy avocado and crunchy toasted walnuts helped compliment. It was very sweet and smooth, with the mounted butter sauce coating the mouth but not the lips or, in my case, beard. history_reviews: [['114589915198164681316_60532f337fec92c07c643a78', 'They also have seasonal menus, and as Im writing this review (September 2018), they have incredible pumpkin gnocchi that will leave you craving for more. Make sure you keep room for dessert: their banoffee pie and their sticky toffee pudding are to die for!'], ['114589915198164681316_60532f5088c7af3f893e79d5', 'We started with steak tartare, a tarte, and one of their homemade sausages with sauerkraut. The steak tartare was really well seasoned and served with toasted slices of baguette and a small salad. The tarte flamb - which was basically a flatbread, was topped with fresh veggies and cheese. The sausage was definitely homemade and super flavorful. We then went onto the entrees, our choices were the risotto with morels and asparagus (which is seasonal), the steak frites - that btw comes with bone marrow, and the chicken with mashed potatoes and veggies. The steak was very nicely cooked and flavorful, the fries werent the best ever but were pretty good nevertheless. The piece de resistance was without a doubt the profiteroles - perfect choux pastry filled with ice cream as well as homemade whipped cream, and topped with a delicious dark chocolate sauce.'], ['114589915198164681316_604989dbc7c8ee3104ba1a85', 'Not only is the location really pretty and very typical - you almost feel like being on the second floor of a korean market, where they cook what you bought - but the food is simply AMAZING. You can choose among many options, different beef or pork combos are a great option if youre  in a  group, or you can just pick your favorite cuts. They also have a few options if you want something other than bbq: Japchae, bibimbap, tteokbokki, pajeon, mul naengmyeon, just to name a few. What I recommend you guys to try for sure is the pork belly (samgyeopsal), perfectly layered and absolutely delicious with just a tad of salt or doenjang and made into a wrap with lettuce and kimchi (and raw garlic if you like it). Other dishes Id recommend are the marinated galbi, the bulgogi, and the ribeye. As far as other dishes Im a huge fan of their Japchae, their tteokbokki, and the cold green tea noodles. If you want something small(er) as an appetizer try the kimchi jeon, or the pajeon, theyre pretty good and always made fresh. The banchan dishes are delicious, always order raw garlic on the side if you want the authentic experience, and the pickle onion they bring is to die for. Their kimchi is also very good, and so are the sauces they give you for the meats - The teriyaki sauce with bean flour is sweet and sticky, while the doenjang is nice and salty.'], ['114589915198164681316_605637e03019cb0a47838c77', 'This is my absolute favorite place in NY for a classic lox and cream cheese bagel (but also for babka and dried fruit). I suddenly remembered we hadnt tried Russ & Daughters so we made our way there. My order, since then, has almost always stayed the same: toasted everything bagel with plain cream cheese, belly lox, capers, onion, and tomatoes.'], ['114589915198164681316_60552ed5451ea67743baf19e', 'Id definitely recommend you to try their charcuterie - most imported from Italy, paired with stunning cheeses and marmellate. Do not skip on the new entry, the famous timpano made famous by the foodie movie by definition: Big Night In. Delicious baked pasta inside pastry, with meatballs, meat sauce, peas, salami, cheese - trust me youll thank me!'], ['114589915198164681316_604b91a777e81aaed3cc9631', 'Definitely get the soup dumplings and the pan fried buns - and try their delicious shredded pork with bamboo shoots, which is one of my go to every time Im here. The soup dumplings are really flavorful and with a great amount of filing and soup, my go to are the pork ones but they also have the ones with crab - both are delicious! Sweet and savory tender pork strips with crunchy but hard bamboo shoots - trust me youll come back for more!'], ['114589915198164681316_604372a3aab4c25a4e74e72f', "Knowing that - or at least with that pre conception in my brain - I made my way to Let's Meat, the first korean bbq ayce style that finally opened in Manhattan with no expectations at all, just to have a decent meal with my friends on a gloomy Saturday. The other has more premium cuts like skirt steak, short rib, gopchang, squid, shrimp, octopus... and comes at 38.99$. Either options are great, and I'd say that unless you want seafood the OG is perfect. We did want seafood (and gopchang) so we ended up going for the premium option. We also added a couple sides (most are included, just a few aren't): spicy rice cakes - aka tteokbokki, japchae, and sundubujjigae. The Berkshire pork belly is nice and thick and fatty, and goes perfect with lettuce, kimchi and onion (and garlic if you're not scared of it). The marinated bulgogi was very flavorful and not too sweet - which sometimes can be. The shrimp was nice as well, and every cut of meat was carefully prepared by our waiter who was super nice and made sure no cut was over cooked. We accompanied our meal with makgeolli and soju (they have a combo deal for 15$), that were much needed with such a meaty feast."], ['114589915198164681316_60415b3a7cd8bf1303624f33', "If you didn't know, Gopchang is a real delicacy in Korea and people really do crave it. Gopchang means small intestines and is usually eaten after it's cooked on a hot griddle and paired with chives, rice, and mandatory soju. This place not only has small intestines, but also my favorite: Daechang, which is the larger intestine and is completely different. They also have a plethora of other offal items, but also cater to those who are more into pork belly and beef. Do not dare to skip on other dishes like their fried rice (spicy, but so addictive and delicious), their stews and their soups as well!"]]

We also upcharged cheese sauce for the crack fries (the cheese sauce comes with a side order of fries but is not included with burgers), and a side of macaroni and cheese. The Pils was cold and it paired really well with the Paddy Melt. The Melt was delicious! The burger was topped with corned beef, cheese, mushrooms, and carmelized onion. The fries were great -seasoned nicely with salt and cracked pepper. The "nuggz" were literally 2-3 chunks of pickle spear. My husband only got two pieces of pickle which just seemed silly. The Paddy Melt was good -but $14 for a burger is steep when other burgers around this glorious college town are priced $6-9.

history_reviews: [['110919746599715163818_6050c279da79151bfc125458', "We each chose the same item fajitas and we picked steak and shrimp for the meats so we paid $2 extra. Our fajitas arrived and we both felt that the vegetable should have been cooked just a little longer. At other places where we've had fajitas served on metal skillets they were hot, steaming and sizzling for several minutes, but ours were just warm without any steam or sizzle. The wraps that came with the fajitas seemed rather small and were fairly tough and hard to bite through. The shrimp were on the small side but there was a good handful of them. The beans were supposedly black beans but they looked brown to me although they were very tasty. The rice was really not worth eating although I did put a little of it in the wraps when I put in my fajita ingredients."], ['110919746599715163818_6050c360da79151bfc12545c', "My wife had their steak salad and said she'd eat it again but would put the Italian dressing on the side next time. The pedals turned out to be better and we're actually cooked more thoroughly than the Bloomin Onion had been. When the salads arrived the steak which we had ordered medium was cooked medium-well and on the cold side so we brought that to the attention of the waitress and she immediately offered to get it recooked. Within a short time the manager Tom brought us two new salads out of the kitchen, the steak in them looked delicious and turned out to be so. review_text: Authentic Korean- Friendly Staff- Delicious Bibimbap. . My wife and I tried this restaurant at random. The rest of the banchan came out after that and we honestly tore through it in a way that I hope garnered the respect of the wait staff (or pity, Ill accept either). The kimchi was good, very saucy and spicy, but with no horrific after taste like the kind you buy at Whole Foods. The odeok was very soft and chewy and great with gochujang. The salad was also delicious and excellent with a little bit of gochujang. I ordered kimchi dol sot bibimbap and my wife just ordered regular dol sot bibimbap, though she did ask for beef in it. Hers was the superior bap, as mine was a simple mix of kimchi, rice, and a fried egg. We also got gunmandu (fried dumplings) but we ate them all before I could get a photo. This was a simple soup which I found very creamy despite being mostly tofu.
history_reviews: [['106271335081562183513_604f28158ba95eba01a00b9d', 'Great food-Great Service-Tons of bacon! Shrimp Tacos- My wife got shrimp tacos. Very creamy and tangy with enough bacon to thatch a roof. I got the spicy garlic dipping sauce which wasnt too hot or garlicky, but no one would talk to me afterwards and I couldnt figure out why. Sliders- My father-in-law chose the sliders. He named the Drogon, Rhaegal, and the other one, the ice one. Loaded potatoes- I ordered these because I was hungry. It was fairly well coated with bacon bits, such that every bite had plenty of chew and crunch! Flatbread with mushroom, onion, and bacon- This was meant to be our appetizer, but it came out with our food.'], ['106271335081562183513_604b071db1a0aaee3eefc0cb', 'Really great pizza, really great service. My family went for lunch on a Saturday, a total of nine people at around one oclock. I ordered the Caesar salad and our group ordered the Base Camp Pizza and we ordered the Pepperoni with pesto on it.'], ['106271335081562183513_604a78a93ebca1b150aa165c', 'We commented specifically on how much we enjoyed the onions and pickles with everything. We also really enjoyed the turkey!'], ['106271335081562183513_604ca32f3ada919c27677b80', 'Zeppole. These were somewhere between the pice de rsistance and a coup de grce. Butternut Squash Agnolotti. This was recommended by the sympathetic Kara and was really surprising! Affogato. At this point, entranced by the warm scenery and glow of the grill fire, we were pliable to the power of suggestion and ordered both of the desserts recommended by Kara. Butter lettuce salad. A light salad, the Gorgonzola vinaigrette dressing was complex and bitter, offering first the mustiness of the cheese followed by creamy, peppery flavors. Fusilli. My wife ordered this and found it exceedingly rich and robust. The onions were sweet and pungent, cutting through the fatty porcine savor of the bacon. The lettuce itself was exceedingly smooth in the mouth, a texture that the creamy avocado and crunchy toasted walnuts helped compliment. It was very sweet and smooth, with the mounted butter sauce coating the mouth but not the lips or, in my case, beard. The squash is sweet, but it all runs towards savory, like children fleeing a haunted house. The sage is crispy, joining hands with the crushed amarettos in a seance of savor and texture. It was garlicky and savory, with a potent chicken flavor cut by bursts of savory pancetta (bacons sexy cousin). I got the affogato, which was made with rich and creamy espresso. The ice cream added a further level of diary unctuousness and sweetness, which offsets both the bitterness of coffee and that which exists in our day to day lives.']]

Breakfast is available all day, so I opted for the Andouille Sausage Omelette. My wife was a little bit more ambitious, so she got the Muffaletta. Cafe Beignet's beignets were served in triplets with a ton of powdered sugar, but that's about where the similarity between the two places ends. Cafe B's beignets were significantly larger, which meant a significantly lower surface to volume ratio. However, this was compensated by the fact that beignets were so much more airy (while warm, the darn things turn into rocks overnight from both places), so the powder sugar level wasn't really an issue. The batter itself also tasted different from Cafe D.  Our decision was that we preferred the beignets from Cafe B, but our recommendation is to try both places and decide which one suites your palate."], ['111621433888070656994_604111617cd8bf1303622f72', "So glad In-N-Out has this location right next to LAX. Having been living out of state for so many years, it's always nice to be able to grab a burger right after getting off the plane when visiting family at home in SoCal. Having tried many different burger chains around the US, we still love the simple menu (and secret menu) that In-N-Out offers. Maybe it's just because we grew up with In-N-Out, but the Double Double animal style, animal style fries, and a Neapolitan shake is the perfect meal."], ['111621433888070656994_60418a3b2e57ebdea29c4f21', "My wife claims that this was the best ribs that she has ever eaten... We stopped by Fox Bros while driving through Atlanta and picked up The Everything Plate with sausage, pull pork, chopped brisket, and ribs. Also got a jalapeno cornbread on the side. For a Texas styled BBQ place, the ribs were awfully dry, until you realized that the ribs were deep fried before getting served. If you like your ribs a little bit more saucy, plenty of BBQ sauce are provided. Deep frying the ribs gave it a unique texture and helped lock in the moisture for the juicy parts (or so I've heard). The sausage was smoked to perfection and so was the chopped brisket. I was slightly disappointed with the pull pork, but what I really wanted was the burnt end that was sold out (along with the famous fried okra)."], ['111621433888070656994_605653ccd335d0abfb415ab6', 'As per usual, there is a bunch of different flavored chicken (that all tastes like orange chicken from Panda Express) and a "sushi bar" that serves unrefined maki rolls. The distinguishing feature of this buffet is the Mongolian grill. Typically, people like to fry noodles with their Mongolian grill mix, but I prefer getting fried rice and jazzing it up with a few ingredients from the Mongolian counter.'], ['111621433888070656994_605707e7c4674474cff9122d', "Shabu is really not my favorite cuisine style, but my wife loves boiling her food. The closest comparison that we have for Spring Shabu is Mo-Mo-Paradise that recently opened 2 locations in Southern California. My wife literally dragged me to Mo-Mo every chance we got during our visits to Taiwan, and now that we've found Spring Shabu in Flushing, I now have boiled food at least once every other week (with increased frequency during the colder months). Unlike most other Shabu places in Flushing, Spring Shabu is run by Koreans, and the standard is much closer to actual high-end Shabu places in Asia (thus the comparison to Mo-Mo). They have an interesting pricing system where each person gets charged for their individual pot of soup and that includes access to the large selection of AYCE veggies and noodles. The usual burner setting we use is 3 out of 5, but if you are inexperienced at Shabu, accidentally left your burner at 5 out of 5, and boil off all your soup, the staff will be happy to add more soup to your pot."], ['111621433888070656994_60488c64b1a0aaee3eefa16f', "Thank goodness for the existence of this Red Robin in Hershey. There are a few beers on tap including the local favorite Yuengling. I didn't realize that Red Robin burgers have gotten so small: the patties are McDonald's Quarter Pounder size and similar in taste. Thank goodness for the unlimited fries or else I think I would have needed another burger. This Red Robin gets a 5-star rating from me solely due to its location and relatively attentive service."], ['111621433888070656994_605275c40b92fc485d92a5ee', "Somehow having a sandwich from Earl's reminds us of drunken post-clubbing nights in Vegas despite being located in such a wholesome location..."], ['111621433888070656994_6042fa80aab4c25a4e74c7e9', 'Lucha Libre is still one of the best places to get massive amount of Mexican food at an awesome price. review_text: Fish and chips is a true guilty pleasure of mine and more times than not it's the dish I'll order anytime I go to any seafood restaurant. Fresh, flaky, PERFECTLY cooked cod served with crispy fries (that can be elevated through upgrades like adding chorizo or truffle for an extra charge). Choices of dipping sauces are abundant and all tasty but tartar sauce and malt vinegar are the only two things I need to enjoy the fish. Thankfully the batter is perfectly balanced giving the perfect crunch ratio to the fish. Understand this, all the dishes are cooked to order so the fish is brought to the pass the moment it comes out of the fryer, meaning this is the freshest cooked fish served. The fish and chip combo is pretty affordable by Strip standards at $16 for a filling meal consisting of 3 large filets and fries.

Quality comes as a premium and double because of Gordon Ramsay's association with the restaurant with burgers starting at $17."], ['112327251491788648660_605197b4c53d98b3eace1c38', 'As most of everyone on the West Coast will tell you, In-N-Out is the best fast food chain to satisfy a burger craving. history_reviews: [['111217793845808378532_604a9f57c6dc737bce7e5c77', 'If its your desire to enter a crazy Italian food fantasy land, Eataly is the place to go. Id like to tell you they have hot and cold running pasta, and its probably true, but there is so much Italian goodness going on in this place, you wont have the chance to experience all of it in one visit. I had the Margherita Pizza. The gluten-free marinara pizza served without cheese had my wife questioning her very reality. Our son is a plain pasta kind of guy (sighwe didnt raise him right) So thats what he got. I tried a noodle and the flavor was good but it was a little over cooked. (And it turned out the slight modification she wanted to the gluten free version of their special pomodoro pasta was gluten free (she also wanted it without cheese) and she thought it was well done. (Not always an easy feat with gluten free pasta.)'], ['111217793845808378532_60487b0cf9e05764f1fa5494', 'These were all around delicious and filling. . My wife got the Hongos tostada which came with an extra layer of delicious black retried beans. So we get confused when theres a placed called Bakersfield since already have a city called that hereand on top of which they serve tacos, and our streets are lined with tacosahoy Southern Californians, Bakersfield residents and all taco lovers everywherethese are the tacos you are looking for. There are good and tasty vegetarian options including the blackbeans, one of the salads, a Tostada option and 2 different tacos. I had both of the vegetarian tacos, the Hongos (portobello mushrooms, various peppers, a kale slaw and cotija cheese), and the Huitlacoche (corn truffles [which is actually a kind of mushroom], peppers corn, onion, cilantro and cotija cheese. They were a little similar, both being mushroom based and I ended up having a second hongos. Chips and guacamole was $8 with salsa or $3 with just salsa and no guacamole. The red sauce has a nice smokiness to it. They also do a nightly shot special with a premium liqueurin this case it was a Camarea Tequila shot. In general you cant go wrong with a three dollar tequila shot, but the fact that its a premium curated liqueur really brings it up a few notches. And although we didnt get one, the Margaritas we saw walking by are served in Mason jars and looked amazing. Please send us your fine tacos to Southern California.'], ['111217793845808378532_60473872b1a0aaee3eef862f', "It was the traditional last night before Passover starts pizza offering, and this was our choice. Unfortunately this wine  Also, the line was served in plastic cups which was strange. For an Italian restaurant, which theoretically has lots of vegetarian options, this place wasn't particularly vegetarian friendly. For example they had many many salad options most of which automatically had chicken in them. I'm sure you could order it without the chicken but if you're going to have such an extensive salad menu, shouldn't you have vegetarians in mind in the choices that you offer as defaults? Our kid had the macaroni and cheese. The macaroni wasn't particularly good and the fries, where is they looked good, were coated in something. Rule of thumb for french fries  if you can't make decent regular french fries, and have to rely on coding them in something, you shouldn't be offering french fries at your restaurant. Also rule of thumb for macaroni and cheese for kidsit should always be the basic mac and cheese. If a kid doesnt like your mac and cheese, you have strayed in the wrong direction. Most of us were sharing a large cheese pizza. The first pizza came out under done, the crust was mushy. One of us got their gluten-free pizza. Kudos to you Biaggios for offering gluten-free crust, however you did get the order wrongit was ordered without cheese and, sure enough, came with cheese. Also the mushrooms topping tasted canned. Canned vegetables of any kind do not make for good tasting pizza."], ['111217793845808378532_604a4d8c1ec03878d66c8387', 'They have lots of vegetarian choices which are helpfully labeled as such on the menu, which includes crispy tacos enchiladas and more. I also had a side of Tater Tots. For my main I had the (also seasonal) Local Foraged Mushroom Stroganoff. This was a fresh pappardelle with Hen of the Woods mushrooms and Creme Freche. A WHOLE OTHER FREE PASTA DISH packaged to go home with you! It was also nice that they had a gluten-free option for the pasta, although it wasnt my wifes favorite gluten free pasta ever.'], ['111217793845808378532_605314b811a96a1e3740a521', 'I started with a Honey Nut Old Fashioned - It was a good drink, well mixed, with peanuts in it and the unique flavor of Peanut Honey Bourbon. My wife and I shared the Brussels Sprouts Four Ways. 3 of the ways look similar to each other and one looks different, so we actually had to count the ways to make sure we had all fourthere was smoked, pickled, fried and what wed call overdressed. We also had the Stout Gingerbread Carrotsall three of these words are divine on their own, together, they created a new carrot mecca  The dish was not overly sweet and looked yummy, though we would have preferred slightly more al-dente carrotsoverall it came together nicely. I loved the Castle Valley Mills Farrowit served as a hearty main for just me (its on the small plates menu) It included mushroom, asparagus, cherry tomato, roasted fennel, poached egg, pine nuts. My wife had the Charred Asparagus Salad for her main. She said it was a delicious salad with a beautifully poached egg on the top. Not on the main, but reason enough to come to this restaurant are the French Fries.'], ['111217793845808378532_604a9f18b1a0aaee3eefbd41', 'There is a great pizza war waging in the United States with two opposing forcesthe lovers of Chicago style deep dish pizza, and New York style thin crust (though a Lyft driver I had recently assured me that New York style pizza is really from Connecticut..or was at least perfected there.) The New Yorkians will, without hesitation, tell you that Chicago style pizza is not pizza. The Chicagonians pretty much dont care, as long as they can keep eating their, unique, butter crust, deep dish phenomenons. In my world, this is like comparing apples and orangesthe 2 are different entitiesthere is excellent New York style pizza.and there is excellent Chicago style pizza. Masa of Echo Park is the only place (I know of) that you can get truly authentic and really good Chicago style deep-dish pizza. Sure, there are plenty of places that offer deep-dishbut to be truly authentic Chicago, its got to be more than thick doughyouve got to, as Masa does, use a buttery, somewhere between pizza dough and biscuit, crust. Youve got to put the cheese in first, then the toppings and sauce so the cheese seals the dough (and rises in bits through the sea of sauce to the top. Masa does all of this and provides the authentic Chicago pizza experience youre looking for. (Even if youre only looking for it sometimesmy mouth and belly have equal joy for authentic NY slices and occasionally I start thinking about real Chicago pizza and I just need it.) Masa is the real deal. Even my 9 year old who famously doesnt like anything besides plain pasta found his Plain-Jane pizza astonishingly good. If youre looking for authentic, and super good Chicago deep dish pizza in Los Angeles.'], ['111217793845808378532_604ae3fcb1a0aaee3eefbf28', 'I started with the Smoke Rings Cocktail (it was mandatory [in my mind] that every drink in Kentucky was bourbon based, if not straight up Bourbon. review_text: Finally, a Mexican place which satisfies my craving for good tacos! I ordered the steak (asada), steak (ribeye) and, of course, the pastor (pork) tacos. I judge all new Mexican restaurants by their steak and marinated pork tacos. I order tacos one way:  Onion, cilantro, cheese, on corn tortillas. These tacos were loaded with finely-diced onions, fresh cilantro leaves, and cheese which melted perfectly. The steak tacos contained ample, flavorful meat. I'm a steak taco connoisseur, and I'm pleased to report that these are the finest steak tacos in the area. I also ordered elotes. However, the pastor taco was even better! I know, how can pork be better than steak, right?! Not only are these the best pastor tacos I've had, they are the best tacos I've had, period. The red and green sauces are fantastic. There is no astringency to either of them, and the red comes very close to the sauce La Fajitas had before they were taxed out of Illinois. The owner and I would chat about the goings on in the area, national politics, the importance of charcoal grilling peppers for the red salsa, whatever crossed our minds.

review_text: Probably one of the best sushi places I've had in Utah thus far. One of the ways I rank sushi places is whether or not the sushi tastes "fishy" or even smells fishy. The salmon nigiri and lightly seared salmon tasted amazing and melted in the mouth. The tuna was alright but a little rubbery. The raw scallops unfortunately weren't that great and tasted quite fishy. They offer a sushi buffet option that is definitely worth it. You can try almost any of the sushi on their menu and can order as many items off the menu in three different waves. Not the best sushi I've ever had though.
history_reviews: [['115795335915871262391_60486873f9e05764f1fa53b3', "Ruth's Chris is your typical higher end steak restaurant. I started the evening with the Fresh Mozzarella & Heirloom Tomato Salad, followed by the ribeye cooked medium with a side of Lyonnaise Fingerling Potatoes. The salad was a classic caprese salad which was a great light dish to leave room for the steak. The steak was cooked to perfection and was incredibly tender and juicy."], ['115795335915871262391_604fd15484d95314a9e43714', "I am typically very picky when it comes to sushi. Having lived in Japan for several years, I am very particular and I like to think that I really know good sushi. I usually gauge how great the restaurant is based on its sashimi and the taste of the fish. Does it taste or smell fishy? Does it melt in your mouth or is it gamey/chewy. The sashimi here ended up being pretty good. It didn't taste fishy or smell fishy which goes a long way. The fish itself seemed pretty fresh but did not really melt in the mouth as one would hope. We ordered the spicy edamame as well and the sauce on those is heavenly. We ordered the Vegas, volcano, California (not my idea), and the Paris rolls. We ended the night with the strawberry and chocolate mochis and the new york style cheesecake. The mochi ice cream was average. This is definitely one of the better sushi places in the area!"], ['115795335915871262391_6051303fa740b9d848c0a8eb', 'We followed it up with the 2 of the 4 lunchesque items that were being offered at 2 PM which were the carbonara pasta and the cacio e pepe.'], ['115795335915871262391_60512f5bd8c08f462b93e2d8', "Food & Presentation. I ordered the rose lassi, the cheese naan, the sweet nutty naan, and the butter chicken. The lassi wasn't as rose flavored as I had imagined but even still tasted delicious and was incredibly creamy. That way I could have more lassi than ice in my cup. The butter chicken was good. The cheese garlic naan was delicious, but the nutty sweet naan absolutely took the show."], ['115795335915871262391_605061435b4ccec8d5cae5c5', "We started with a delicious 3 cheese Kirsch liquor fondue that was a little tangy and very creamy perfectly accompanied the fluffy sourdough bread. Next we had the spicy thai tomango peanut soup. Litterally best most creative spin on a tomato soup ever. Cut with a little cream it had the peanuty flavor of curry, the sweetness of a mango, and the great original taste of a tomato soup. My main entree was the wagyu beef and my mother ordered the pork loin. Sweet strawberries, and perfectly season mashed potatoes, yet with a spicy kick from the wasabi. The beef was cooked to perfection and my mother's pork was incredibly tender. A creamy pudding, with carmolized apples walnuts and bourbon ice cream."], ['115795335915871262391_6055d7e697d555cc6fb0cf38', 'I ordered the pepperoni and basil bites as an appetizer, followed by the figgy piggy calzone. They are similar in texture to garlic knots but are more flakey and have a more robust flavor. The calzone I got was very unique. I had never thought of using figs on pizza, much less in a calzone, but the sweetness of the fig really added a dimension of flavor to the calzone which I was not expecting.'], ['115795335915871262391_6046e489811be03312c4bd13', "I've never understood the appeal of waffles and chicken being eaten together and have tried it various places and have never loved it. Without a doubt, it is the best chicken and waffles that I have ever eaten and it was done right. The waffle almost matched the crispiness of the chicken on the outside but was quite fluffy and airy on the inside."], ['115795335915871262391_6043343ecc4f7990c65788f0', 'Beginning with the biscuits, they are mouthwateringly tasty, fluffy, and crispy all in one. I ordered the biscuit bread pudding french toast with a side of eggs and bacon and a hot chocolate to drink. The bread pudding was very dense and flavor-packed. I appreciated the almonds on top and the side of yogurt to dip it in. The yogurt really added another keynote of flavor to the plate. The eggs and bacon were typical of a diner and the hot chocolate was decent. Would have appreciated the hot chocolate having been made with milk/cream rather than with water, but I did enjoy the quantity of whipped cream on it.'], ['115795335915871262391_6050f713da79151bfc1255c7', "Definitely not the best pizza place in the world, but it's also not the worst. The pizza crust is usually slightly crunchy and pretty well flavored, but you can tell that it seems like they don't use fresh ingredients. The pizza is a little too greasy and doesn't really leave me wanting more. Their deep dish is a little bit better but also not very much. I beleive the best thing on their menu is their Italian cheese bread. It is extra cheesey with a crunchy outer crust that's also big and fluffy on the inside. My main issue with this particular location of Little Caesars, though is two fold. First, they've done a terrible job at cutting their pizza. I don't believe I have ever gotten a pizza from this location where the pizza was actually cut more than just through the cheese. Normally the pizza is still all completely together. Definitely not the best place for pizza but for the price and speed you can get it on, it's worth it if you're in a hurry or need to feed a lot of people."], ['115795335915871262391_6045427d9ae54ad76ed57490', 'This time around I ordered the lemon ricotta pancakes, a side of potatoes and some orange juice. The pancakes were actually very filling and pretty delicious, the potatoes were pretty normal compared to everywhere else, and I really appreciated that the orange juice was freshly squeezed.'], ['115795335915871262391_6047afa890b81483d31acf9b', "It was very filling for being a personal size pizza and they definitely didn't skimp out on loading it with cheese and sausage."], ['115795335915871262391_6047bf6db1a0aaee3eef91cd', "The Lobster Bisque was creamy and rich. The roasted salmon was delicious as well. The salmon itself wasn't too different from salmons I've had at other high class restaurants, but the chimichurri and sun dried tomato puree that accompanied it gave it an amazing unique flavor."]]

review_text: We ordered the Ora King Salmon sushi, the By the Border specialty rolls and the tempura Udon. To finish it, I ordered the lemon ginger kefir soda which was on the board as one of their specialty drinks. The sushi was pretty authentic. The specialty rolls were better with the soy sauce but very good. The Udon broth was interesting. Not the spicy broth I usually like, but I liked it. The noodles were pretty bland, which my boyfriend liked but I was like, meh! The tempura included a shrimp, potato, zucchini, carrot and an onion. Shrimp and potato tempura works, but the carrot does not. I prefer an american onion ring to onion tempura.
history_reviews: [['110400146182741479070_60478dd8b1a0aaee3eef8db6', 'We ordered a margarita and gin and juice and a shared plate of the chorizo tostadas. The margarita was pretty good. The lamb rack was ordered medium rare but felt more rare to eat because it was chewy."], ['110400146182741479070_60532d8e11a96a1e3740a632', "I got the slumgolian chowder and also took the Cajun oyster sandwich to go. My friend is a vegetarian and decided to take the chashu rice without the meat and thought it was ok."], ['110400146182741479070_6043869cad733fba1bcfd8a0', 'The main entre was a blackened salmon on a bed of veggies. The salmon was just as expected- blackened and crisp on the outside and melting soft on the inside.'], ['110400146182741479070_604153f5c6fcf1fddba12bd2', 'I chose the seafood gumbo. It's got a beautiful mosaic icing and a center of lemony goodness. The icing was sticky, but the lemon inside was great. Chocolate covered doughnut. My brother took the bro burger which is basically the Angus beef, ham, veggie burger you find in other burger joints.'], ['110400146182741479070_6047fd0ab1a0aaee3eef965f', "We got the kachi dabeli, chole puri and the batata vada with 2 masala chai. I love my chole Punjabi style with lots of spices and a tang that hits you immediately. Batata vada - came with a fried pepper."], ['110400146182741479070_6051e16bc53d98b3eace1d8b', "And those signatures included 4 red meat options, a salmon and a scallop option. So since chicken was out, I decided to go with the Scottish salmon and my boyfriend decided on the braised short rib. We got the calamari for an appetizer. The calamari was good! I was a little underwhelmed by the salmon. The veggies in the cream sauce around was a decent touch. The short rib, again, broke off beautifully. Because of our yelp check-in, we got a free sticky toffee pudding - a desert lover's (not me) delight!"], ['110400146182741479070_605491c84b7f30a9c0a50ed6', "Now the food - we chose the cheese corn with bacon and the thai chilli chicken wings. The corn is sweet, the cheese melting, the spices flavorful and the sizzling just adds to it all. We asked for the spiciest flavor for chicken wings and the thai chilli was suggested. The bread is wonderfully fried, the thai chilli was a good kind of spicy and the chicken meat was well cooked. I would like to try the ramen and other flavors at a later time!"], ['110400146182741479070_604158f57dfa7f1871835dd4', "We chose the friend catfish tails, a dozen raw oysters and a dozen charboiled one. history_reviews: [['106638019782667313599_6047540eb1a0aaee3eef8913', 'Their King platter is delicious with 2 different meat kebabs and rice/pita.'], ['106638019782667313599_604371aab81264dfa846bb45', 'They had good spring rolls precut in half to cool down. So as we are sitting with fried rice, we have nothing to eat it with. Eventually all the food comes, and we see that in the pad Thai they have HAIR intertwined around noodles.'], ['106638019782667313599_605445934b7f30a9c0a50d3c', 'If you have 3 curries and then 2 rice and 1 noodle dish, the balance just isnt right. Their hakka noodles were tasty, but very very oily. Their paneer (cheese) dish has very little paneer. The pav bhaji (curry on a hamburger bun) was was too thin of a curry and tasted more like water than spices. The carrot halwa (dessert) was vegan, so no milk was used, but instead a lot of oil was used which made it quite oily. The jalebi (fried dessert) was also too oily and soft, meaning that it was not fried at a hot enough temperature. Their kheer (rice pudding) and mango pudding desserts were nice. The naan they bring fresh to the table was also nice. We ran out of naan quickly (5 pieces for a family of 5) and they never brought more. The masala dosa (bread filled with potato curry) was ok. Not that crispy and again, oily. The sambar (soup) was just ok. I will say that their rasam (another soup) was A+. The aloo bonda (fried potato ball) was also ok.'], ['106638019782667313599_60469e37b0e2129e47535335', 'Incredible ramen. The fatty, thick broth that my ramen had was excellently seasoned. The noodles themselves were firm, which allows more texture to the meal, allowing for chewing. We got the spicy miso bomb as well which added an excellent kick to the ramen. Overall 10/10 on the Daikokuya ramen. We also got a sushi roll which was just OK.'], ['106638019782667313599_6052c4375266728eda27aa5d', 'The pizza is phenomenal, and the concept of a Subway/Chipotle style pizza joint is perfect. Yes prices are going to be higher than other pizza chains and the portion will be smaller, but the pizza simple cant be compared to the others.'], ['106638019782667313599_60460404604fc398f591f539', 'This is an excellent donut place, but unfortunately the 2 donuts I wanted to try (the cruller and the apple fritter) were not available. The blueberry cake donut I went with was delicious, and maybe trying the must try ones would have made this a 5 star.'], ['106638019782667313599_604f59bd9755094ba8abe2a1', 'You can get a burger, a cheeseburger, and/or fries. I got a housestyle cheeseburger (comes with dijonnaise, onions, and pickles) as well as their fries). Their burgers are thinner, but double patties. They have an excellent selection of condiments for your fries such as Heinz ketchup, Sir Kensingtons ketchup, garlic aioli (10/10 yummmm must get! The fries were excellent. Some of the crispiest fries ever. The burger was unreal. Sure, its your standard burger, but every bite from the soft bun to the crisp pickles, to the juice, medium burger was mesmerizing. It costs just under $15 for the cheeseburger and fries, and Id pay that again in a heartbeat to get that again.'], ['106638019782667313599_604a8ae4b1a0aaee3eefbca3', 'The two BIG menu items they have removed from the list is their beef brisket and their pork belly. These are two of the most ICONIC Korean bbq items to see on a menu, and yet they are not removed. Their bulgogis are sweet, flavorful, and amazing (specifically their beef), their seasoned steak is juicy and tender, their chicken is moist, and honestly everything they have is still delicious. Be sure to order spicy rice cakes (glutinous sticky rice that has been melted down to a cylindrical shape and covered in gochujang (sweet/spicy sauce). These rice cakes are always quick and tasty to eat while waiting for your meats to cook in the center. Im here for the meat! Well, you are here for the salad as well. While just simple romaine lettuce, the dressing and pickled onions in it are the game changers. I could not tell everything in the sauce, but there was a peanut-y component, a sesame oil component, and then a sweet component (maybe kalbi/galbi?). Japchae: cold, sweet potato starch noodles. Vegetables: yes, order mushrooms, onions, potatoes. Grill them, dip them in the sauces. Speaking of sauces, my two personal favorites are their galbi (sweet) sauce and their salt & pepper sesame oil sauce. These are served in a two-compartment dish, so be sure to try your meats dipped in these sauces! These make excellent in between snacks while meat is cooking. They also act as a mouth refresher, cleansing your palate while adding a much needed acidic taste to cut through the fattiness of the meats. Add some cooked meat, some sauces, a spicy rice cake, some grilled veggies, and some pickled veggies and kimchi, and then try to take the best bite of your life.'], ['106638019782667313599_60496403c7c8ee3104ba184d', 'They convinced me to try it when they mentioned peach and mango, but the beer was incredibly flat with no flavor at all.'], ['106638019782667313599_6051308a88c7af3f893e6fe3', 'There was no salt or anything in the Szechuan noodle dish we got, and the only reason we finished it was purely for sustenance.'], ['106638019782667313599_60552795451ea67743baf17d', 'This has their biscuit, fried hot chicken thigh, and their sausage gravy all in one. Also a must try is their bonuts (blueberry biscuit donuts).'], ['106638019782667313599_60435f029b00092d7286c156', 'The creamy tofu falls apart as you cut it, and the spicy broth that it is in is an excellent addition.'], ['106638019782667313599_60476754b0e2129e475362fb', 'This is where you come when you want some of the best tasting tacos in Nashville. It is worth the trip to have these amazing tacos.'], ['106638019782667313599_604ce58d77e81aaed3cca3b9', 'What an amazing introduction to real Cuban food. I got a Cuban sandwich that had a croqueta (meat and cheese fried ball) inside it, all on a sweet bread. The croqueta was soft when biting in, and the ham from the Cuban sandwich had a snap to it that gave a fantastic contrast in texture. The difference was their dipping sauce, a sweet and acidic sauce that really cuts through the fried plantains, AND it is also a great dipping sauce for that Cuban sandwich! Their coffee and toast is unbelievable, strong, great flavor. Only dip bread in coffee if you ask for bread WITHOUT a butter. Their milkshake with mamey, a Cuban fruit, has a distinct banana flavor, and incredibly refreshing. If you want to order the sandwich, chips, and milkshake, just tell them, Una orden de mariquitas con mojo, una croqueta preparada en pan de medianoche, y un batido de Mamey. Get that coffee and toast as an appetizer also!']]

It is served over wok vegetables, which I am terrible with veggies and I ate the hell out of all of them.'], ['111635523018340070679_6040ce24c6fcf1fddba0f0e0', 'Visited Voodoo Doughnut last night to see what all the hubbub was about. review_text: 10 - DUCK FRIED RICE. Before you start judging the amount of food we got, we didnt technically order this. 8 - GREEN BEANS IN BLACK BEAN SAUCE. The waiter recommended we get these to supplement all of our meat dishes. 6 - XI'AN GOAT SLAP NOODLES. This was the showstopper, the dish I have dreamed about since my visit. Just imagine the potential of short rib and bone marrow potstickers, and that is what you will get when you order these. The noodles were slathered in all of that flavor and were cooked perfectly. It was mostly a pile of veggies on top of a couple small pork pieces. Vegetables what a radical idea. If you dont generally like green beans dont let that prevent you from getting these. It was a platter full of crispy chicken, just topped with a few green onions and peppers.
history_reviews: [['106158651309276041679_604e0ed477e81aaed3ccad17', "These are the bagels you've been looking for. Since returning to Houston, the Hot Bagel Shop is the only place that scratches the itch. They have quite a variety of bagels, probably 10-15. Their supreme (everything) bagel is perfect - they do not skimp on the seasoning one bit. My go-to order has become the supreme bagel with chive cream cheese. Im also fan of the jalapeo bagel, which sounded weird before I tried it, but was craveable after. I also enjoy the garlic onion bagel (again not dainty on the seasoning) and the vegetable cream cheese. When feeling extra peckish, I go for the traditional bagel and lox sandwich. In staying on brand, they load it with the toppings and each bite has a good balance of salmon, onion, capers, and tomato. Two bagels toasted with cream cheese is under 6 dollars."], ['106158651309276041679_60465ffa10ec061e056b4327', 'Summary: 6 out of 5, fantastic ramen. If youre so into ramen that you watch ramen documentaries on airplanes, you will enjoy this. One of the first foods we started researching here was ramen, because were obsessed. We went looking for the restaurant and we were just a little lost/confused at first, because High Five is underneath the inside part of Green Street Smoked Meats. Eating this ramen felt like how I imagine McDuck felt when he swam in his money (Im sorry again relapsed while reimagining the ramen). This was the best ramen I have had that was not in Japan and, yes, I know how obnoxious I am for making that statement. I mean this as a major compliment though, because it transported me right back to some of the best ramen I had in Tokyo, and it might be in my top 5 best bowls of ramen ever. Its just hard to find such a rich, cloudy, spicy broth combination over here. For what its worth, I have a friend here in Chicago who regularly entertains business clients from Japan, and they always request High Five ramen if they can fit it into their schedules because its the only place in the city that meets his clients standards.'], ['106158651309276041679_60415c497cd8bf1303624fa4', 'Their buns are absolutely delectable, they have Asahi on tap, and they have a lot of bar seating, which makes it a great place to walk in casually. The Miso Bold & Spicy ramen is my favorite here. The broth is chicken-based, but it still has a creamy and rich quality. There was enough fatty opacity to it for me to come back even though I tend to go for the richest and spiciest pork broths.'], ['106158651309276041679_605506f53019cb0a47838762', 'These burgers are top notch excellence. There are 6-8 beers on tap and probably 20+ in bottles. The Maillard was essentially an elevated take on the classic greasy dive bar onion burger. They really load it up with the crispy onions which makes the texture awesome and the burger look like an advertisement when it comes to your table. El Jefe is a delicious mess. Again the beef was moist throughout, and then you get the fried egg and chipotle mayo on top. Im fairly certain they make the chipotles in house because the flavor was stronger, spicier, and smokier than anything you would get in a can. We asked for a side of it for our fries which I would HIGHLY recommend. After finally trying this place Im confident all of the burgers will be great.I fully intend to return to try their award winning foie gras and truffle pesto burger.'], ['106158651309276041679_60415d2b7dfa7f1871836081', 'The Pork Belly Home Fries are UNREAL.'], ['106158651309276041679_604f568688c7af3f893e644d', 'It tasted like clam chowder, without all the good parts of clam chowder. 2 - Chicken Fried Rabbit. The menu says it comes with a risotto, but what came to us was definitely not risotto. It was a dry rice pilaf. Risotto is supposed to spread out when you put it on a plate, and this little pile of rice was just that - a pile. 3 - Curry braised lamb shank. When I read curry braised lamb shank, I expect a punch of deep flavor. I had to really focus to taste the curry and there was nothing else happening with the flavor. The couscous was fine, and the figs were good on their own, but didnt seem to pair well with the rest of the dish.'], ['106158651309276041679_60415f44c6fcf1fddba13088', 'Au Cheval serves the best burger Ive ever had. I ordered the double burger au cheval (with an egg) and a side of french fries. Important tidbit: the single is actually two patties, and the double is three. Also, they dont bother asking you how you want your burger cooked, which I love. They know the proper way is a nice medium rare just a little pink. I would be lying if I told you I havent looked back at my photo of the burger multiple times since I went and craved it again. Between the perfect meat preparation, the melty cheese, and the dijonnaise, the burger makes for an incredibly juicy bite topped off with the soft warm bun and thinly sliced homemade pickles. The fries are natural cut, perfectly salted, and have a very satisfying crunch to them. They come with a very flavorful aioli. Truth be told, Im not always into dipping my fries into a sauce, but this aioli was different. The fries are a large enough portion to share between 2-3 people. Ive also had their Bloody Mary, which was classic, spicy and peppery.'], ['106158651309276041679_604e9abc7ce15821f39750d6', 'The gyro is good here. You basically have to eat gyro meat off the top for 5 minutes before you can successfully pick up the pita. The fries / onion rings / etc. It scratches the itch for a gyro.'], ['106158651309276041679_60415faf7cd8bf130362510d', 'Ragu alla Napoletana:. Our server was excited to deliver this to our table and explain what was going on since we has not had it before. Egg Yolk Raviolo:. Cutting into this and seeing the yolk flow out was spiritual. Nduja Arancini:. To quote my wife, I want to live in this arancini. We both agreed that this arancini made us feel like we had never eaten arancini before. The inside is a warm, spicy, soft, melt in your mouth mixture of the spicy sausage, manchego, and risotto. They are topped with an insanely good aioli with a ton of spice/herb flavor and also a perfect tomato sauce. One order comes with 4 arancini for $8. The anchovy really has a faint crab-like flavor that goes so well with the sweet corn. For the regular sized pastas, this is the priciest at $24, but its absolutely worth it. It consists of a mound of fusilli pasta, 3 full sausages, 4 large meatballs, and a mountain of a pork shank, all covered in a rich tomato sauce. The fresh pasta had a great texture that stood up to all the meat on the plate. The sausages were thick and juicy; you could see the juice when you cut into it. The pork shank was huge! It was braised to tender perfection in that tomato sauce. The soft pork with the dense pasta made for a really awesome bite. Finally, the meatballs. They are soppressata meatballs, so they have a complex spicy taste. Like the sausage, they were incredibly juicy.']]

review_text: I asked for a cosmo, less sweet and they actually made it as such. They also have a few craft bottled Japanese beers (not on happy hour), which was a nice change of pace from the typical Sapporo and Kirin you see at Japanese restaurants. You can also get $5 select apps (sliders, chicken yakitori, california roll, edamame, gyoza, kani salad, fries). I had a fried chicken slider, which I absolutely loved. The chicken was juicy, and came with a spicy mayo sauce. The California rolls are California rolls - nothing special, and the kani salad was just okay. There were more cucumbers than imitation crab meat. We started off with one of their specials, which was a tofu topped with some spicy salmon. I guess I missed the part where the menu mentioned the salmon part because I was just expecting something like agedashi tofu. Plus sometimes, you're just in the mood for some good old fashioned Americanized sushi with all sorts of crazy concoctions and sauces. I went with the Dynamite Roll (wild blue crab, avocado topped w. seared spicy scallops, crunch, fried vermicelli - $17) and the Harajuku Roll (salmon, mango, cucumber topped wtih spicy salmon, crunchy flakes, scallion, caviar mango sauce - $15), to share. The first piece of the Dynamite roll tasted a bit off. And just in case we weren't already ordering too much food, we threw in a duck ramen for good measure. The duck was surprisingly good, as was the broth, but the noodles were soggy. In fact, I feel like I could have gotten better noodles from a Shin Ramyun package. It was also my aunt's birthday so they brought out some mochi ice cream on the house. I'll definitely be back for some fried chicken sliders (I'd also imagine their chicken karaage would be pretty good as well), and for some of their other rolls.

The sauce is made from fresh tomatoes without paste, and they\'ve got the crust dialed in right that it\'s thin and crisp but never burnt. The meat is incredibly fresh and the meatballs are very tender, but damn if you don\'t pay a hefty premium to eat at the place Jack Nicholson eats at when in town. review_text: Burgers, Chicken, Salads, to Vegetarian Items and Milk Shakes to Fountain Drinks, they had a great selection to choose from. We got the "Little Sloppy" and "Cowboy" burgers. The title for the "sloppy" is exactly that, but equally delicious and worth the mess. It comes with a fried egg, a single 1/3lbs beef patty, cheese, thick cut peppered bacon, a hasbrown "brick" (like McDonald's but more rectangular & just as crispy), and all the other toppings you can choose from. (You can add extra toppings for an extra charge, they even have "froi gras.") The "Big Sloppy" has 2 beef patties and double the peppered bacon (and everything mentioned above), you better bring an appetite, the little one was no small burger. There is a "secret" language on how you want your burgers cooked, but if you tell them medium, they will understand too. The cowboy I believe had peppered bacon, a single beef patty, cheese, grilled onions, mushrooms and all the fixins (lettuce, tomato, pickle, onion) if you wanted them. We got Fries and Sweet Potato Tots. Their regular fries are fresh hand cut potato fries. The burgers were super juicy and cooked to perfection. Not to mention all the other items complimented the burger.

During this visit, I got their popular sushi roll.'], ['116668750889199944129_604a6729d863393130a4149c', 'First we ordered appetizers, takoyaki and oyster fry. Takoyaki here is made with pices of octopus, vegetables & batter like pancake mix, they look like donut holes, but on the savory side. The fried oyster was 3 whole oysters that was battered in panko, fried golden, served with mayo and soysauce on the side. They were fried delicately and had just the right amount of crunch on the outside and the oyster was tender inside. The other party had ordered O-nigiri  (rice triangles with a sheet of seaweed) Takoyaki, and Gyoza (pan fried meat dumplings). Our friends enjoyed the O-nigiri (as he put it, "anime, made it taste better"). They also didn\'t care for their order of takoyaki, but enjoyed the Gyoza. Our main course was the Ramen, since this is more of a ramen shop. They have rice bowls but opted for ramen. I got the "Cha Cha Cham pong" along with my guest, the other two got beef sukiyaki ramen and the spicy Cha Cha shoyu men. The beef sukiyaki ramen and the spicy Cha Cha shoyu men came out very quickly. The party who ordered it said they enjoyed their bowls of ramen. Comparing to different types of hot peppers. It wasn\'t that spicy, and the noodles were nice and chewy, like true ramen is supposed to be. The seafood that was in it, could have been better, and there lacked of (only a few mussels, chewy octopus, looked like american bacon [not traditional Asian pork belly], and bits of Napa cabbage pieces, along with other veggies. The pork belly slices on the "shoyu ramen" looked much better, not to mention they were huge! I tasted the broth on the Cha Cha shoyu men and would recommend that instead of the Cha Cha Cham pong. We didn\'t get dessert but they do have green tea cheesecake, tempura cheesecake, mochi ice cream and ice cream sandwiches from Asia.'], ['116668750889199944129_60521534da79151bfc125cb0', 'Delicious Korean BBQ, open 24/7! Got the Combo Special: "S" of meats and it was excellent. They bring out a good selection of banchan, not to mention the BBQ side salad, Yum! The meat selection of "Combo S" was:  beef brisket, prime ribeye (thin sliced), marinated short ribs, boneless short ribs, and you get a choice of chicken bbq or pork belly, we chose the chicken. The second night we just did al la cart: prime ribeye and beef brisket. It was really good, we wanted to scarf it down quickly, but ate slow and enjoy the true taste of "Prime meats," not choice. review_text: Earlier in the day on a Elmhurst Thai food safari we had picked up an order of crispy rice balls and an order of their signature house made Thai sausage which was extremely tasty and lead is back to explore the menu further. We liked it overall but felt like they were holding back on spices and funky flavors. Lemongrass chicken wings 4 crispy Wingettes for $7 tender and crunchy but again lacking any pow or punch of lemongrass, coriander or the kaffir leaves that were advertised. Tum kanoon, jackfruit salad, ground pork, homemade shrimp paste, cherry tomato, kaffir leaves, cilantro chili and scallion. Fermented pork ribs had a. Crunchy fried exterior and a large hint of garlic inside - if they were served at a Latino restaurant the flavor profile would be similar. It came with sticky rice and crispy pork rinds. Kang Hung Ley pork belly in a masala curry which from descriptions on line sounds like it should have a sour element and thick gravy didn't in lamoon's rendition which had a somewhat thin but tasty curry. The pork belly didn't seemed to have been braised in the sauce which was disappointing as well. The coconut curry with pickled veggies and soft egg noodles along with a topping of crispy noodles. The flavors were rich with a delft hand at seasoning. It's not typically spicy and neither was their version but it rocked the spice rack with great depth of flavors a thick rich coconut curry sauce that made us want to lick the bowl.

review_text: Brought my family from out of town here after my friends recommended Lou's for a great deep dish experience. We got a Caesar salad to share, the trio of dips and pizza chips, and the Lou medium pizza for three of us to share. The salad was great and just the perfect appetizer. The chips were an indulgent sharing platter as well, but the dips were extremely greasy. The pizza was both what I expected and not. Our pizza was about 1/3 inch thick with toppings and all. Also, I'm not sure if because this pizza only had veggies, but the toppings seemed very watery. Nonetheless, this was pizza so it couldn't go wrong, and the crust was cooked through on the bottom and nice and crispy on the edges. Overall, we had a great time, didn't feel like the wait was long, and left feeling so full with half a pizza in hand.
history_reviews: [['107548322316470513394_60415a40c6fcf1fddba12e25', 'While browsing the menu, we were served some spicy picked cabbage which definitely had quite a kick to it.
