All our food came out at once, and I really liked everything, but wished the wontons were spicier.'], ['107548322316470513394_6043932a8be5d4454df9db04', 'Their sangrias are TO DIE FOR!! Some other highly recommended dishes: buttermilk fried chicken, octopus a la plancha, hanger steak, short rib, bruschetta, and paella. I have yet to have a better paella dish in Chicago.'], ['107548322316470513394_60415df32e57ebdea29c3c0c', "I was so surprised by how much I liked my experience at Prosecco! We got Salsiccia (grilled Italian sausage), Tartufate (orecchiette, cremini, asparagus, sun-dried tomatoes, black truffle cream, Grana Padano, white truffle oil), and a farfalle pasta special that had smoked and fresh salmon. The sausage had good flavor and wasn't too salty, and the pastas were cooked perfectly al dente. We were surprised by how filling the portions were, both the antipasti and pastas. There was a ton of salmon in the farfalle special, and the Tartufate really hit the truffle-flavor craving I had without being too greasy or creamy."], ['107548322316470513394_604158cfc6fcf1fddba12da2', 'Every "classic" Chinese dish is super solid here, including the spicy beef noodles (not really spicy but noodles are super chewy), soup dumplings, mapo tofu, green beans, etc. One thing you MUST GET is the eggplant in garlic sauce. Best eggplant I\'ve ever had.'], ['107548322316470513394_604157bd7cd8bf1303624c81', "The Peking duck dinner is really the only thing you should be coming for, because they roast a spectacular duck here and I haven't had better in the city. The rest of the food on the menu is just okay--Chinatown has better. For four people, one duck dinner is just about enough, which comes with a large plate of sliced duck, six bao buns, a plate of fried rice, and a large bowl of soup. I'd recommend ordering extra buns since the meat will definitely outnumber the pieces of buns that you have, and a vegetable dish for health. The server brings out the roasted duck whole, and will carve/slice it table-side. It's always a spectacle to watch, and the meat is always super juicy, fatty, and crispy, all in one bite. The fried rice and soup are average, but complements the duck meat nicely. If you have five or more people in your group, it'd be a good idea to get two ducks. Sometimes near the end of the day they run out of ducks which is just about the saddest thing the waiter can tell you after you've been seated."], ['107548322316470513394_60415b797dfa7f1871835f97', 'Compared with other Chinatown dim sum restaurants, everything just tastes more flavorful and larger portions, albeit with slightly higher prices (avg $15 per person). They put real shrimp in the har gow (not paste) and theres like 4 shrimp in each dumpling. The siu mai is ginormous as well and filled with whole shrimp. My favorite dim sum here are the beef short ribs and the pineapple bun custard buns that literally explode with that sweet, gooey filling every single time.'], ['107548322316470513394_6046e75705aec66848d1c66f', "Usually you're only able to do half pies of the classics (margherita, marinara, white, calzone), but we asked if we could do two half pies of the margherita and the no. Between two people a medium size was plenty, and you could definitely taste the freshness of the ingredients and the handiwork of the dough."], ['107548322316470513394_604ad57db1a0aaee3eefbead', "The quality of the food isn't as good as many other Indian restaurants but you're bound to be stuffed at the end of your meal. The mango lassi isn't as mango-y as I would like, but again, I have no complaints based on how large the portions are and how cheap the food is."], ['107548322316470513394_60415fe17cd8bf130362511a', "Brunch is Asian inspired, and I've tried their Vietnamese iced coffee, corn elotes, pandan French toast, and catfish banh mi. As a fan of sweet and creamy treats, the coffee and French toast are must-gets!"], ['107548322316470513394_6050539bd2f0452c8736d412', 'After we were seated, we ordered the fried cod and shrimp tacos (this was where we made the mistake--should have just gotten the lobster roll). I barely wanted to eat it and ended up peeling off the fried skin and just ate the fish inside. The fries and slaw were great though. The fried shrimp tacos were pretty big, but the shrimp was soggy and suuuper salty. The tortilla was very soggy as well, so I ended up just eating everything in the taco with a fork. The two pastas were great contrasts, but we didnt find either to be particularly strong-flavored.'], ['107548322316470513394_60415e4f2e57ebdea29c3c2a', "I'd especially recommend the lamb kefta, short rib shakshuka, and khachapuri, which was kind of like pizza but on puff pastry. The noodles are cooked to perfection, and the sauce and toppings are simple but strong in flavor. As with the other pasta dishes, you can get a half order instead of a full order, which is what I got, and I still left feeling very full. The chocolate cake is TO DIE FOR!!! review_text: I got the Crispy Fried Chicken & Waffles (Crispy Chicken Breast / Belgian Style Waffle / House Syrup). The chicken was cooked perfectly with the breading falling off the chicken like it was hand-breaded and the soft waffle with the crisp exterior. The syrup came poured on the sandwich. My girlfriend got the Fried Green Tomato BLT Biscuit (Smoked Pork Bacon Avocado Puree, Local Greens, Sweet Corn "Caviar" on Two (2) Buttermilk Biscuits). Sauteed up potatoes with peppers and onions.
history_reviews: [['118020893387833644953_60512d695b4ccec8d5caeaaa', 'Their nachos is like 8 nachos with all the toppings on each nacho.'], ['118020893387833644953_604ba99020f26f37fb9d7d9a', "It was a soft, buttery, fluffy round flatbread that went well with all of the sauces! We got a Oak-grilled Filet Mignon (Bobotie Macaroni and Cheese, Grilled Asparagus, Kachumbari, South African Red Wine Sauce). Cooked medium rare. This steak was very good. The mac & cheese was awesome. The asparagus was grilled nicely, but I would have liked to have seen more than two sprigs on the plate. The mixed veggies added a great acidity to the dish, and the rich red wine sauce tied it all together. We got the Bo Kaap Malay Seafood Curry (Lobster, Calamari, Red Shrimp, Mussels, Coconut-Curry Sauce, Saffron Rice). The seafood was infused with the flavor of the star of the show, the coconut-curry sauce. It was a nice, slightly sweet curry that blended well with the aromatic saffron rice. I have never ordered a dish like this (seafood slathered in warm sauce with rice or pasta) that there wasn't at least one piece of the seafood that was overcooked. Most surprisingly, the calamari was cooked well!"], ['118020893387833644953_6043749bb81264dfa846bc01', "It's a labor of love, it's accentuated by sauce, and it's usually very obvious which barbecue is better than another barbecue. They sell all the meat by weight, or you can buy a sandwich. I can't remember what it was all about word-for-word, but it was a brisket sandwich with some sauteed onions on there, but the special part of it was that it had fried crispy onion strips on there and a horseradish sauce. I skipped the sauce, sorry, but man, this brisket was out of this world. I think it might have been better than 4Rivers', but to be fair, it's been a long time since I've eaten anything from 4Rivers that wasn't their burnt ends, because those things are heaven. I also had a side of mac 'n' cheese, and it was also darling."], ['118020893387833644953_6055b33697d555cc6fb0ce82', 'After some careful consideration, I decide to get the special of the day, a New York Strip, some amazing mashed potatoes, and a bunch of grilled green onions and peppers of some sort. And the onions and peppers added a bunch of good veg. I also got to sample the Carnitas (24hr Dos Equis Slow Braised Pork, Grilled Onions, Mexican Rice, Refried Beans, Lettuce, Sour Cream, Pico de Gallo, Guacamole, Jalapeos, Flour Tortillas).'], ['118020893387833644953_604378448be5d4454df9d76d', "So on this trip, I got the Chicken N' Waffles (with Maple Bourbon drizzle). My two fixins of choice were Fresh Fried Okra and Creamed Corn. I gotta tell you, The Coop has some of the best chicken and waffles in all of Orlando. The breading on the tenders is light and flaky and adds that nice crunch you want. The waffles is obviously freshly made in a waffle maker. The okra was good. My girlfriend, on the other hand, got the New Orleans Po-Boy (shrimp) with a fixin of the Bread Pudding. The shrimp was cooked well, but the sandwich just wasn't bursting with flavor like you want."], ['118020893387833644953_6045ac1c10ec061e056b3386', 'I got the Vietnamese Ice Coffee (Vietnamese-Grown Dark Roasted Coffee Brewed into Sweetened Condensed Milk and poured over Ice), which was super sweet. Just imagine an iced coffee thickened with sweetened condensed milk. My girlfriend got the Spiced Lavender Mocha (Espresso, Dark Chocolate, Earthy Spices, Lavender, Steamed Milk), which tasted like we were drinking flowers. Brioche French toast, topped with tender pulled pork, tomato, poached eggs, hollandaise, crispy Cheshire Farms bacon) and the # Tag This Hash (Braised short rib hash, potato hash cakes, avocado smash, sauted squash topped with over easy egg and chimichurri served with sauted fresh vegetables).'], ['118020893387833644953_6043d04dcc4f7990c6579a4d', 'First thing\'s first, we ordered a half-dozen of the Char-Grilled Oysters (Romano, parmesan, Roux compound butter). For my entree, I ordered the Alligator Hash (Crispy beer-battered alligator bites, garlic potatoes, sunny-side up egg, hollandaise and red "remi" remoulade). I\'m used to gimmicky fried gator on a stick when it\'s all chewy and stuff, but this gator was tender and absolutely delightful. I also got to sample the Crawfish Hash (Andouille and crawfish hash, garlic potatoes, sunny-side up egg and hollandaise). There were a TON of crawfish tails. The sausage was a welcome Cajun taste. For dessert, we ordered the NOLA Style Beignets (Five light and puffy beignets covered in powdered sugar).'], ['118020893387833644953_604642d4882f4d1caf5fed3c', "We were putting on a charity event where a percentage of Burger Fi's profits were going towards our class organization, so we all pitched in and did the hard work. My girlfriend and I each got a burger and split an order of the Cry+Fry (Onion Rings + Hand-Cut Fries). The fries were good. Not just fries, because they're fried in peanut oil, just like at Chick-Fil-A. And the onion rings were absolutely fantastic. Now for the burgers. I got the Breakfast All Day Burger (Natural Angus Burger, American Cheese, Bacon, Maple Syrup, Fried Egg, Hash Brown, Grilled Onions, Ketchup), and my girlfriend got The CEO (Double Wagyu + Brisket Blend Burger, Homemade Candied Bacon-Tomato Jam, Truffle Aioli, Aged Swiss Cheese). My burger was very good. The beef patty was delicious, the cheese and the bacon were on point, the maple syrup I actually couldn't tell it was there honestly, the fried egg was good, and the hash brown was strangely enough the thing on the burger that I would be the saddest if it was missing. We've all had breakfast burgers before, but the hash brown was the unique twist here, and I am a big fan. The whole thing also wasn't too greasy, which surprised me consider it was a beef patty, bacon, and a fried egg. Well done, Burger Fi. My girlfriend's burger was very interesting. I understand that Wagyu is a premium ingredient, but when you cut it down with brisket and then make a patty so thin that you can't get anything more out of it than well done, it's honestly a little bit disappointing. It was ok, but I definitely wouldn't have guessed that it was made with Wagyu if I didn't already know. Also, there was nowhere near enough jam on that burger. Tomato jam is such a wonderful addition to meals sometimes, that I was excited, but alas, more disappointment. If you like burgers come here, but don't expect gourmet."], ['118020893387833644953_6043d146b81264dfa846ceef', 'On top of it being Valentine\'s Day, I\'m also on a conquest to see The Best of Orlando 2020, and Izziban won the best Korean restaurant in Orlando, according to the readers of Orlando Weekly. We got the All-You-Can-Eat Korean BBQ, which is a flat $37. You get access to their salad bar, along with 13 different meats you can cook, various sides, nigiri, and sushi rolls. I tried to go full meat at first, to "get my money\'s worth," and I found myself bored. What\'s a nice slice of brisket for if not to have with a bite of fried rice? What\'s the point of cooking a head-on shrimp if I can\'t put the results of it on a crunchy baguette? I recommend every meat they offer, but I will say, skip the rib-eye. The steak is too big, and it\'s not good enough to sacrifice that stomach space. Skip the rib-eye in favor of other meats. Speaking of stomach space, a tip is that you can order full portions of the meats, or you can ask for a half order. I had two sushi rolls, the Crunch Shrimp and the Yummi Yummi. Not top tier sushi by any means, but delicious and good relief from all the heavy meat and fried sides. Don\'t forget to start with the miso soup. Cooking your own meat on your personal grill was like an upgraded Melting Pot experience.'], ['118020893387833644953_605384c880c04bd7072f2129', "We split The Family Feast (1lb wangs, 1 Whole Chicken, 1lb Pork, 1lb Brisket, 1lb Serious Sausage, 1 Rack Baby Backs, 1 Rack Spare Ribs. It was really hard to decide on what meats we wanted to try, so we ended up deciding to try all the meats. The heaps of pickles and onions that the fest came with made for a great sandwich with some slices of the loaf of bread we got. -The chopped up brisket was the second best thing about the feast. I'm not really a spare ribs kind of guy, unless they're Korean sticky ones, but I ate a couple, and I liked them. For our sides we got french fries, sweet potato fries, mac & cheese, and the sweet potato casserole."], ['118020893387833644953_604f362388c7af3f893e635f', "The main dish I got was the Pad Thai (rice noodles, shrimp, chicken, eggs, bean sprouts, carrots, spring onions, red chili pepper, roasted peanuts, lime). Small Plate 1: Korean Twice Fried Wings (garlic Gochujang sauce, peanuts, sesame, cilantro). I didn't get a strong taste of gochujang, so it's not actually spicy, but the flavor was good, strong with sesame. The shrimp and the pork were formed into a solid mass, like a dense crab cake, and fried in strings and strings of batter rolled into balls. Order extra roti, though, for $1.50 each, because a lot of what you eat will have some extra sauce left over that you can sop up like a tortilla. Small Plate 4: Singapore 'Chilli' Crab (national dish of Singapore, soft-shelled crab, house-made chili garlic sauce, fried bao bun). The crab was fried to perfection and the sauce was so flavorful."]]

history_reviews: [['115795335915871262391_60486873f9e05764f1fa53b3', "Ruth's Chris is your typical higher end steak restaurant. I started the evening with the Fresh Mozzarella & Heirloom Tomato Salad, followed by the ribeye cooked medium with a side of Lyonnaise Fingerling Potatoes. The salad was a classic caprese salad which was a great light dish to leave room for the steak. The steak was cooked to perfection and was incredibly tender and juicy."], ['115795335915871262391_604fd15484d95314a9e43714', "I am typically very picky when it comes to sushi. Having lived in Japan for several years, I am very particular and I like to think that I really know good sushi. I usually gauge how great the restaurant is based on its sashimi and the taste of the fish. Does it taste or smell fishy? Does it melt in your mouth or is it gamey/chewy. The sashimi here ended up being pretty good. It didn't taste fishy or smell fishy which goes a long way. The fish itself seemed pretty fresh but did not really melt in the mouth as one would hope. We ordered the spicy edamame as well and the sauce on those is heavenly. We ordered the Vegas, volcano, California (not my idea), and the Paris rolls. We ended the night with the strawberry and chocolate mochis and the new york style cheesecake. The mochi ice cream was average. This is definitely one of the better sushi places in the area!"], ['115795335915871262391_6051303fa740b9d848c0a8eb', 'We followed it up with the 2 of the 4 lunchesque items that were being offered at 2 PM which were the carbonara pasta and the cacio e pepe.'], ['115795335915871262391_60512f5bd8c08f462b93e2d8', "Food & Presentation. I ordered the rose lassi, the cheese naan, the sweet nutty naan, and the butter chicken. The lassi wasn't as rose flavored as I had imagined but even still tasted delicious and was incredibly creamy. That way I could have more lassi than ice in my cup. The butter chicken was good. The cheese garlic naan was delicious, but the nutty sweet naan absolutely took the show."], ['115795335915871262391_605061435b4ccec8d5cae5c5', "We started with a delicious 3 cheese Kirsch liquor fondue that was a little tangy and very creamy perfectly accompanied the fluffy sourdough bread. Next we had the spicy thai tomango peanut soup. Litterally best most creative spin on a tomato soup ever. Cut with a little cream it had the peanuty flavor of curry, the sweetness of a mango, and the great original taste of a tomato soup. My main entree was the wagyu beef and my mother ordered the pork loin. Sweet strawberries, and perfectly season mashed potatoes, yet with a spicy kick from the wasabi. The beef was cooked to perfection and my mother's pork was incredibly tender. A creamy pudding, with carmolized apples walnuts and bourbon ice cream."], ['115795335915871262391_6046e489811be03312c4bd13', "I've never understood the appeal of waffles and chicken being eaten together and have tried it various places and have never loved it. Without a doubt, it is the best chicken and waffles that I have ever eaten and it was done right. The waffle almost matched the crispiness of the chicken on the outside but was quite fluffy and airy on the inside."], ['115795335915871262391_6043343ecc4f7990c65788f0', 'Beginning with the biscuits, they are mouthwateringly tasty, fluffy, and crispy all in one. I ordered the biscuit bread pudding french toast with a side of eggs and bacon and a hot chocolate to drink. The bread pudding was very dense and flavor-packed. I appreciated the almonds on top and the side of yogurt to dip it in. The yogurt really added another keynote of flavor to the plate. The eggs and bacon were typical of a diner and the hot chocolate was decent. Would have appreciated the hot chocolate having been made with milk/cream rather than with water, but I did enjoy the quantity of whipped cream on it.'], ['115795335915871262391_6050f713da79151bfc1255c7', "Definitely not the best pizza place in the world, but it's also not the worst. The pizza crust is usually slightly crunchy and pretty well flavored, but you can tell that it seems like they don't use fresh ingredients. The pizza is a little too greasy and doesn't really leave me wanting more. Their deep dish is a little bit better but also not very much. I beleive the best thing on their menu is their Italian cheese bread. It is extra cheesey with a crunchy outer crust that's also big and fluffy on the inside. My main issue with this particular location of Little Caesars, though is two fold. First, they've done a terrible job at cutting their pizza. I don't believe I have ever gotten a pizza from this location where the pizza was actually cut more than just through the cheese. Normally the pizza is still all completely together. Definitely not the best place for pizza but for the price and speed you can get it on, it's worth it if you're in a hurry or need to feed a lot of people."], ['115795335915871262391_6045427d9ae54ad76ed57490', 'This time around I ordered the lemon ricotta pancakes, a side of potatoes and some orange juice. review_text: One of the oldest pizzerias in NYC and a great take on a New York slice. Grimaldis prepares their pizzas in a large brick oven, which leaves the pizza with an authentic and rustic taste. Top 5 NYC pizza, in my opinion.
history_reviews: [['104285062634756642667_6054877d80c04bd7072f25b8', "Pizzeria in Carroll Gardens know for absolutely lip smacking delicious brick oven calzones and pizzas. Once youve finally been seated, your choices couldnt be any easier, the menu offers two dishes: pizza and calzone, or my personal favorite, both. We started our meal with the calzone, which was the highlight of the meal and is clearly in a league of its own. The calzones are generously stuffed with ricotta, mozzarella, and red sauce along with whichever additional toppings you choose to have baked into this luscious treat. The calzone is prepared with a ton of love and genuine expertise, you somehow manage to still feel like an adult as youre devouring this classic childhood dish. Youll enjoy every hearty bite as well as each emphatic dunk of your calzone into the sweet red sauce as garnish. As for the pies, theyre prepared with the same expertise and love, however they fall a tad short of the calzone in overall satisfaction. Its tough for pizza to truly standout in NYC considering there are so many Goliath's that make otherworldly pies, that said, this is still a worthy option. The pie is slathered with the homemade red sauce and peppered with both low moisture mozzarella and buffalo mozzarella, which is delicious. The pizza is garnished with a heap of fresh basil whichs adds a pleasant earthiness to the meal. I recommend adding some garlic and at least one more topping to the pie to maximize your experience."], ['104285062634756642667_605488427fec92c07c6440b9', 'Pennsy offers several notable dining options, including a personal favorite, Pat LaFriedas meat purveyors. The bar has a rotating top of NY beers and regional favorites. Youll find plenty of seating and bar space within the food hall along with additional seating options on the outdoor terrance.'], ['104285062634756642667_60435f27ad733fba1bcfd098', 'As you bite into the dumpling, savory flavors invade your mouth as the soup is blitzes your taste buds and paves the way for the delivery of the tender pork. Aside from their famous soup dumplings, they offer creative variations on classic Chinese dishes but Id recommend trying their Shanghai pan fried noodles.'], ['104285062634756642667_60560255f69c7b117806fe51', 'Shake Shack is a NY born and bred, fast food chain that specializes in fresh beef burgers and delicious milk shakes. The burger scene is competitive in NYC but given its natural limitations to compete with the heavyweight champs (JG Melon, PJ Clarkes, etc.) this is the best fast food burger in the city. The beef is sourced locally from Pat LaFrieda meat purveyors which is the trademark of their tasty creations. The burgers are cooked medium and are dressed with lettuce, tomato and shack sauce.'], ['104285062634756642667_604ca10e77e81aaed3cca14e', 'Outstanding fried chicken. Pies & Thighs is a Williamsburg staple that stands true to the name in delivering mouth watering fried chicken and homemade pies. The fried goodness is crispy, well seasoned and juicy to the bite. I recommend the three piece meal which comes with two sides and a flakey, buttery biscuit. Speaking of sides, youll have several worthy options to pair with your poultry. I am a big fan of the collard greens which have a hearty, meaty seasoning and are well salted. In addition, the macaroni and cheese is deliciously simple and pairs supremely well with any chicken dish. Dont even think about asking for the bill without trying a slice of pie. The pies taste like theyve been prepared by somebodys grandma, cooking with a recipe thats been in the family for generations. I recommend the classic apple, but you cant miss with any of their delicious options. Pies & Thighs is perfect whenever you have a hankering for fried chicken or feel like devouring well prepared (and well priced) fatty, comfort meal.'], ['104285062634756642667_604c38db77e81aaed3cc9d7f', 'Burger & Barrel Winepub is an excellent burger joint that also offers impressive wine pairings to satiate your palate. No item on the menu is merely present to check the box, so when you find the Fried Chicken sandwich or Prime Rib starting back at you, its totally safe to devour something that isnt the burger. I highly recommend the Kung Pow Chicken Lollipops for starters, they have an unbelievable tang flavor that accompanies the slight heat that the appetizer presents. Youll be shocked to hear that the burgers are noteworthy. First off, Im a fan of any establishment that uses Pat LaFrieda beef because its a clear sign that the establishment is committed to quality. As for their slew of burgers, all are solid but B&B has built a reputation around the city for its Bash Burger. The burger has been named a 6x New York Wine & Food Festival Winner for best burger. The Bash Burger is graced with caramelized onions, bacon jam, gooey American cheese and their special sauce served on brioche bun. Its a great tasting burger, my only reservation is the bun to meat ratio which I feel could be improved to favore the beef. If youre looking for a burger with more heft, try the Double Barrel burger which comes with two meat patties. As a final touch, all of the burgers are served with a few onion rings for good measure and a healthy portion of crispy fries. Burger & Barrel Winepub is a great burger alternative in a city that is saturated in burger options that differentiates itself with a well balanced menu.'], ['104285062634756642667_60444dc5cc4f7990c6579f42', 'Youre in for a treat...Emilys is a boutique pizzeria, based in Clinton Hill, that has built a tremendous reputation for their creative combination of toppings, flavors, and textures that grace their scrumptious pies. Surprisingly, Emilys is famous for crafting one of the best burgers in the city, the Emmy Burger. The burger is prepared with Pat LaFrieda dry aged beef, sweet caramelized onions, American cheese, EMMY sauce while sandwiches together wonderfully between a pretzel bun. Their burger is juicy, savory, and extremely flavorful. It seriously makes you wonder how Emilys is better known for the pizza! The pro-tip is to order a pie and a burger, which is perfect for two people. Weve discussed the burger at the pizza joint, lets dissect the greatness of their signature dish. Emily classifies its pies in four categories: red, pink, green, and white which translates to a number of offerings based in tomato, vodka, tomatillo, and cheese sauces. All of their creations are masterfully architected with a unique blend of toppings, like a pepperoni pie drizzled with honey (dont question it, just order). While all of the pies are tasty in their own right, I have an affinity for The Colony (red), The Big Ang (pink), and The Emily (white). Emilys an up and coming pizzeria giant in the city and is perfect for virtually any occasion.']]

review_text: For. instance, weve been used to a darker sauce for the Drunken Noodle at. other Thai restaurants from various states, but the difference could. depend on the region. - Dara Tofu: Mmmm, one of the best curries weve ever had, and the. potatoes were cooked perfectly. history_reviews: [['109096512932763928773_6047354490b81483d31ac6fb', "By the way, the refreshing, not overly sweet, Thai tea is the best I've ever had, and the delicious, fried egg rolls---with perfectly matching dipping sauce---and pho were great as usual."], ['109096512932763928773_604fd3b79755094ba8abe624', 'So far, the food here has been aMAZing; and the dimly-lit, casual ambience gives this place the feel as though one has shifted into a parallel reality within back in the day Italy. My husband loves Rosas Specialty Dumplings, and understandably so. At first glance, the dumplings look like grandmas big@$$, homemade meatballs, but once we took a bite, the mysterious, savory experience was unlike anything weve ever tasted before. review_text: My husband and I love steak (and food in general), so of course while we were in NYC we wanted to have a nice steak dinner! As soon as you walk in you see he neat locker where they dry age all their meats, which was super cool!! It was some time of banana or pumpkin style bread with nuts. We got clams, since I had never had them, which were beautifully plated. I prefer oysters. Then we ordered a wedge salad which was great, and an appetiser of the pork belly which was incredibly tender with a great sear, oh my goodness! We also got the tuna tartare which was pretty good. It had pickled carrots and daikon on top which was really refreshing. Of course, the star of the meal, were the steaks. I got a filet and my husband got a bone in ribeye. Cooked a perfect medium rare and the texture was great. They were very bland (I got the Mac n cheese and twice baked potato). For dessert we got the creme brle which had a hint of orange and it was fantastic! And they are apparently known for their key lime pie so we ordered a slice of that as well, and it did not disappoint!

One of my friends ordered the coconut JUICE, which is coconut water but comes with PIECES of COCONUT. review_text: The Peking duck dinner is really the only thing you should be coming for, because they roast a spectacular duck here and I haven't had better in the city. The rest of the food on the menu is just okay--Chinatown has better. For four people, one duck dinner is just about enough, which comes with a large plate of sliced duck, six bao buns, a plate of fried rice, and a large bowl of soup. I'd recommend ordering extra buns since the meat will definitely outnumber the pieces of buns that you have, and a vegetable dish for health. The server brings out the roasted duck whole, and will carve/slice it table-side. It's always a spectacle to watch, and the meat is always super juicy, fatty, and crispy, all in one bite. The fried rice and soup are average, but complements the duck meat nicely. If you have five or more people in your group, it'd be a good idea to get two ducks. Sometimes near the end of the day they run out of ducks which is just about the saddest thing the waiter can tell you after you've been seated.
history_reviews: [['107548322316470513394_60415a40c6fcf1fddba12e25', 'While browsing the menu, we were served some spicy picked cabbage which definitely had quite a kick to it. We got the Szechuan wontons, fish fillet in black bean sauce, and napa cabbage in wine sauce. All our food came out at once, and I really liked everything, but wished the wontons were spicier.'], ['107548322316470513394_6043932a8be5d4454df9db04', 'Their sangrias are TO DIE FOR!! Some other highly recommended dishes: buttermilk fried chicken, octopus a la plancha, hanger steak, short rib, bruschetta, and paella. I have yet to have a better paella dish in Chicago.'], ['107548322316470513394_60415df32e57ebdea29c3c0c', "I was so surprised by how much I liked my experience at Prosecco! We got Salsiccia (grilled Italian sausage), Tartufate (orecchiette, cremini, asparagus, sun-dried tomatoes, black truffle cream, Grana Padano, white truffle oil), and a farfalle pasta special that had smoked and fresh salmon. The sausage had good flavor and wasn't too salty, and the pastas were cooked perfectly al dente. We were surprised by how filling the portions were, both the antipasti and pastas. There was a ton of salmon in the farfalle special, and the Tartufate really hit the truffle-flavor craving I had without being too greasy or creamy."], ['107548322316470513394_604158cfc6fcf1fddba12da2', 'Every "classic" Chinese dish is super solid here, including the spicy beef noodles (not really spicy but noodles are super chewy), soup dumplings, mapo tofu, green beans, etc. One thing you MUST GET is the eggplant in garlic sauce. Best eggplant I\'ve ever had.'], ['107548322316470513394_60415b797dfa7f1871835f97', 'Compared with other Chinatown dim sum restaurants, everything just tastes more flavorful and larger portions, albeit with slightly higher prices (avg $15 per person). They put real shrimp in the har gow (not paste) and theres like 4 shrimp in each dumpling. The siu mai is ginormous as well and filled with whole shrimp. My favorite dim sum here are the beef short ribs and the pineapple bun custard buns that literally explode with that sweet, gooey filling every single time.'], ['107548322316470513394_6046e75705aec66848d1c66f', "Usually you're only able to do half pies of the classics (margherita, marinara, white, calzone), but we asked if we could do two half pies of the margherita and the no. Between two people a medium size was plenty, and you could definitely taste the freshness of the ingredients and the handiwork of the dough."], ['107548322316470513394_604ad57db1a0aaee3eefbead', "The quality of the food isn't as good as many other Indian restaurants but you're bound to be stuffed at the end of your meal. My favorite dish here is the lamb curry, and I like the butter chicken as well, but the chicken in it tends to be a bit dry. The parathas are a nice side order as they are humongous. The mango lassi isn't as mango-y as I would like, but again, I have no complaints based on how large the portions are and how cheap the food is."], ['107548322316470513394_60415fe17cd8bf130362511a', "Brunch is Asian inspired, and I've tried their Vietnamese iced coffee, corn elotes, pandan French toast, and catfish banh mi. As a fan of sweet and creamy treats, the coffee and French toast are must-gets!"], ['107548322316470513394_6050539bd2f0452c8736d412', 'After we were seated, we ordered the fried cod and shrimp tacos (this was where we made the mistake--should have just gotten the lobster roll). The cod came with fries and some coleslaw. Fish was fried well but so greasy and almost dripping with oil. I barely wanted to eat it and ended up peeling off the fried skin and just ate the fish inside. The fries and slaw were great though. The fried shrimp tacos were pretty big, but the shrimp was soggy and suuuper salty. The tortilla was very soggy as well, so I ended up just eating everything in the taco with a fork. The tacos also came with a bag of chips but we already felt so greased up by the fish that we ended up not opening the bag up.'], ['107548322316470513394_605082cdc53d98b3eace1645', 'We got a root beer float, Rubins Reubin sandwich, and a mac and cheese.'], ['107548322316470513394_60502a0e9755094ba8abe8c9', 'They serve the bread with this garlic olive oil and vinegar, and it was just sublime. For entrees, we got the angel hair aglio e olio, and the penne with chicken, mozzarella, and tomato cream, and a side of the sweet corn. The sweet corn was surprisingly good, it was popping with flavor and buttery goodness. The two pastas were great contrasts, but we didnt find either to be particularly strong-flavored.'], ['107548322316470513394_60415e4f2e57ebdea29c3c2a', "I'd especially recommend the lamb kefta, short rib shakshuka, and khachapuri, which was kind of like pizza but on puff pastry. The dark chocolate babka that we got was dry and hard, although the filling was soo good."], ['107548322316470513394_60415cfc7cd8bf1303624ffc', "Nonna's meatballs, bucatini, and the chocolate cake. The meatballs are a great dish to share, and and perfectly tender and juicy. The bucatini is definitely one of my favorite pasta dishes. The noodles are cooked to perfection, and the sauce and toppings are simple but strong in flavor. As with the other pasta dishes, you can get a half order instead of a full order, which is what I got, and I still left feeling very full. The chocolate cake is TO DIE FOR!!! It is quite literally the best slice of cake I have ever had. There are so many layers to this cake, and each layer showcases a different texture of chocolate, so there's crispiness in it, ganache, cream, sponge cake, and so on."], ['107548322316470513394_60415e8d7cd8bf13036250e4', "Firecakes is my favorite donut shop in Chicago. The prices are reasonable and hard the beat, and the quality of their donuts are just amazing. The donuts are humongous and it really doesn't get any better than this. These are miles better than the cake donuts (although those are pretty good too). I also love their filled donuts. I'm not usually a big fan of coffee or chocolate flavors, but their valrhona chocolate and espresso donut is particularly scrumptious. I don't think the ice cream donuts are particularly special, but they do make for a delicious treat to share."], ['107548322316470513394_60415dd32e57ebdea29c3bfc', 'For two people, we were recommended to get 5-6 dishes (though I think 4 would have been satisfactory), and got the brioche buns, green beans, salmon poke, pig face, pork shank, and two drinks. We loved the mezcaliforniacation and peachfuzz drinks, and our favorite dish of the night was the poke, which had a great mix of fresh salmon, strawberries, avocado, and a sesame-nuttiness to it.'], ['107548322316470513394_604159ca2e57ebdea29c39a3', "Love the ramen, and everything else here!!! The tonkotsu ramen is one of the best around, and you're in for a treat if you like a fatty cha siu pork belly. I think they give you a nice portion of meat with the noodles. The fried chicken and kimchi ramen tastes exactly what it sounds like. The bowls are usually big enough for me but my bf likes to get his with extra noodles. I'd recommend the beef over the salmon but both are really good."], ['107548322316470513394_60415d907dfa7f18718360a5', 'We came on a Monday night for the tantanmen ramen/Momo royale burger + beer + shot deal, and definitely plan to come back to try more cocktails and small plates in the future. Personally, I liked the burger a lot more than the ramen, since the bao bun and Japanese sweet potato fries really blew me away, but the ramen was delicious as well.'], ['107548322316470513394_6050fbf5da79151bfc1255e4', "Brought my family from out of town here after my friends recommended Lou's for a great deep dish experience. We got a Caesar salad to share, the trio of dips and pizza chips, and the Lou medium pizza for three of us to share. The salad was great and just the perfect appetizer. The chips were an indulgent sharing platter as well, but the dips were extremely greasy. The pizza was both what I expected and not. Our pizza was about 1/3 inch thick with toppings and all. Also, I'm not sure if because this pizza only had veggies, but the toppings seemed very watery. Nonetheless, this was pizza so it couldn't go wrong, and the crust was cooked through on the bottom and nice and crispy on the edges. Overall, we had a great time, didn't feel like the wait was long, and left feeling so full with half a pizza in hand."], ['107548322316470513394_604162797dfa7f18718362f0', 'The waiter mentioned the food is served family style, but we ended up getting individual entrees and shared the caramelized waffle dish. review_text: Try the spicy rabbit, whole fish swimming in black bean sauce, and Sichuan wontons. Spices imported from Chengdu, in southwestern China, give that famous tongue-numbing heat to almost everything from pig intestines to soft mapo doufu (grandmother's tofu) to cumin lamb chops.
history_reviews: [['116539891150848890325_6046ab483a1f1c2b73d6ff76', 'Irish cuisine is known for fish, and chef Mark ONeills dish called Foleys Finest Trout presents North Atlantic sea trout from Foley Fish in Boston, pan seared with a crisp skin and spooned with a tart caper dressing. In America its called Arctic char, he says. We call it sea trout. Its a light fish, quite elegant. Its served with pillows of dill gnocchi, zucchini ribbons, cherry tomatoes and samphire, a salty marine succulent that was actually mentioned in King Lear. And of note is the OMG Burger, Irish from start to finish with a stack of dry-aged ground prime burger, Irish bacon, Dubliner cheddar and opulent Jameson Irish whiskey BBQ sauce, crested with crispy potato straws. There is also a Boaring Burger thats a study in textures and tastes: savory grilled wild boar, tangy blue cheese from Cashel in Tipperary, the pepper taste of arugula, and full-bodied port and pear chutney.'], ['116539891150848890325_604c03fd77e81aaed3cc9b46', 'The menu consists of pizza, meatballs and octopus (all cooked in a very hot wood-fueled oven), along with a couple of salads. Nobody was doing it how I wanted to do it, says Zacchini, referring to a classic Neapolitan soft-dough pizza quite unlike the cracker-hard, foldable slice most of us know. Flour, crushed plum tomatoes, fresh cheesethats it, for a pizza subtle in taste and a great base for a spectrum of toppings including hot soppressata, clams or wood fired pineapple.'], ['116539891150848890325_6042c8d58be5d4454df9b583', 'At El Inka, tallarines verdes, Perus take on tagliatelle pasta, is served coated in bright green pesto with grilled chicken or skirt steak and cheese sauce. Lomo saltado is the Peruvian twist on Chinese stir-fried beef, tangy with vinegar, white wine and soy sauce, sauted onions and tomatoes, served with fries. Tacu tacu con mariscos is a wonderful hybrid of soy-salted fried rice, refried beans and shrimp croquetas that finds a global place between China, Mexico and Africa. Fried rice shows up mixed with seafood, chicken and beef. And of course, raw fish, so omnipresent in Peruvian culture that there are almost as many variations as there are potatoes (almost). Some gastrohistorians say that the influx of Japanese laborers brought the idea of eating raw and marinated fish with them. Ceviches wear all manner of colorful frocks: white fish in red pepper sauce; salmon in citrus; grilled lobster marinated in intense aji amarillo peppers. It shows up with fair regularity, from fried, crunchy cancha snacks to an ingredient in chupe de camaron, a national fish chowder with many regional variations. The beautiful creamy soup of shrimp is cooked in a colorful broth with rice, squash, potatoes (natch), and Spanish influences of poached egg and cream. El Inkas version starts with an aromatic fish broth, adding oregano, cilantro, cumin, green peas, cubes of queso fresco, a rich and savory taste that has echoes of caraway and a healthy dash of hot pepper.'], ['116539891150848890325_604f24709755094ba8abe0ca', 'Beautifully mild codfish fritter buuelos de bacalao; chili and garlic infused gambas al ajillo shrimp; the earthy flavors of huevos Bulla ($10), a fried egg on crisp potatoes, draped in Serano ham and potato foam. Arroz Marinero a dish of seafood rice like a paella lite, built on an ancient, short grain Spanish rice called Bomba. Clams, shrimp, chunks of hake fish, colored with bright green sofrito verde are seasoned with plankton, tiny lab-raised microorganisms that lend a briny ocean flavor and freshness to the seafood.']]

Lemon and Parmesan are commonly added to the breadcrumb mixture for extra flavour. I rounded out my meal with the Biaggi's famous Sherry Tomato soup, tomato soup with...well you guessed it, sherry and housemade croutons. First, off you pick your protein, whether its plant-based, bird-based or beef-based, Bob's selections are easy to navigate. The selections are beef, grilled chicken, fried chicken, quinoa patty and they have  Nathans hot dogs too. next up you pick your bun, your toppings, your cheese and then one of the hearty sides. Keeping the menu simple, you have fresh hand cuts fries, sweet potato fries, onion petals and you pick a small or large size. My choice on this visit was a Classic Hamburger with the classic trifecta of Lettuce, Tomato, Onions and good 'ole fresh locally sourced bacon with a slice of Pepper-jack cheese.. history_reviews: [['114589915198164681316_60532f337fec92c07c643a78', 'They also have seasonal menus, and as Im writing this review (September 2018), they have incredible pumpkin gnocchi that will leave you craving for more. Make sure you keep room for dessert: their banoffee pie and their sticky toffee pudding are to die for!'], ['114589915198164681316_60532f5088c7af3f893e79d5', 'We started with steak tartare, a tarte, and one of their homemade sausages with sauerkraut. The steak tartare was really well seasoned and served with toasted slices of baguette and a small salad. The tarte flamb - which was basically a flatbread, was topped with fresh veggies and cheese. The sausage was definitely homemade and super flavorful. We then went onto the entrees, our choices were the risotto with morels and asparagus (which is seasonal), the steak frites - that btw comes with bone marrow, and the chicken with mashed potatoes and veggies. The steak was very nicely cooked and flavorful, the fries werent the best ever but were pretty good nevertheless. The piece de resistance was without a doubt the profiteroles - perfect choux pastry filled with ice cream as well as homemade whipped cream, and topped with a delicious dark chocolate sauce.'], ['114589915198164681316_604989dbc7c8ee3104ba1a85', 'Not only is the location really pretty and very typical - you almost feel like being on the second floor of a korean market, where they cook what you bought - but the food is simply AMAZING. You can choose among many options, different beef or pork combos are a great option if youre  in a  group, or you can just pick your favorite cuts. They also have a few options if you want something other than bbq: Japchae, bibimbap, tteokbokki, pajeon, mul naengmyeon, just to name a few. What I recommend you guys to try for sure is the pork belly (samgyeopsal), perfectly layered and absolutely delicious with just a tad of salt or doenjang and made into a wrap with lettuce and kimchi (and raw garlic if you like it). Other dishes Id recommend are the marinated galbi, the bulgogi, and the ribeye. As far as other dishes Im a huge fan of their Japchae, their tteokbokki, and the cold green tea noodles. If you want something small(er) as an appetizer try the kimchi jeon, or the pajeon, theyre pretty good and always made fresh. The banchan dishes are delicious, always order raw garlic on the side if you want the authentic experience, and the pickle onion they bring is to die for. Their kimchi is also very good, and so are the sauces they give you for the meats - The teriyaki sauce with bean flour is sweet and sticky, while the doenjang is nice and salty.'], ['114589915198164681316_605637e03019cb0a47838c77', 'This is my absolute favorite place in NY for a classic lox and cream cheese bagel (but also for babka and dried fruit). I suddenly remembered we hadnt tried Russ & Daughters so we made our way there. My order, since then, has almost always stayed the same: toasted everything bagel with plain cream cheese, belly lox, capers, onion, and tomatoes.'], ['114589915198164681316_6049888a09c8186bc0fdf3cb', 'Love their Malaysian Roti and beef rendang, but they have so manu good options as well! Id definitely recommend the roti Canai, beef rendang, fish head soup, fried intestines, hainanese chicken, and def try their drinks too!'], ['114589915198164681316_604b91a777e81aaed3cc9631', 'Definitely get the soup dumplings and the pan fried buns - and try their delicious shredded pork with bamboo shoots, which is one of my go to every time Im here. The soup dumplings are really flavorful and with a great amount of filing and soup, my go to are the pork ones but they also have the ones with crab - both are delicious! Sweet and savory tender pork strips with crunchy but hard bamboo shoots - trust me youll come back for more!'], ['114589915198164681316_604372a3aab4c25a4e74e72f', "Knowing that - or at least with that pre conception in my brain - I made my way to Let's Meat, the first korean bbq ayce style that finally opened in Manhattan with no expectations at all, just to have a decent meal with my friends on a gloomy Saturday. The other has more premium cuts like skirt steak, short rib, gopchang, squid, shrimp, octopus... and comes at 38.99$. Either options are great, and I'd say that unless you want seafood the OG is perfect. We did want seafood (and gopchang) so we ended up going for the premium option. We also added a couple sides (most are included, just a few aren't): spicy rice cakes - aka tteokbokki, japchae, and sundubujjigae. The Berkshire pork belly is nice and thick and fatty, and goes perfect with lettuce, kimchi and onion (and garlic if you're not scared of it). The marinated bulgogi was very flavorful and not too sweet - which sometimes can be. The shrimp was nice as well, and every cut of meat was carefully prepared by our waiter who was super nice and made sure no cut was over cooked. We accompanied our meal with makgeolli and soju (they have a combo deal for 15$), that were much needed with such a meaty feast."], ['114589915198164681316_60415b3a7cd8bf1303624f33', "If you didn't know, Gopchang is a real delicacy in Korea and people really do crave it. Gopchang means small intestines and is usually eaten after it's cooked on a hot griddle and paired with chives, rice, and mandatory soju. This place not only has small intestines, but also my favorite: Daechang, which is the larger intestine and is completely different. They also have a plethora of other offal items, but also cater to those who are more into pork belly and beef. Do not dare to skip on other dishes like their fried rice (spicy, but so addictive and delicious), their stews and their soups as well!"]]

review_text: Came here to try the tsukemen noodles. Mashed potatoes I got, but is there a smoky flavor? Does it taste like tuna? We all ordered the Tokusei tsukemen. Came with buckwheat noodles, a dipping broth, a soft boiled egg, pork belly, and two rare slices of beef(?). The egg was perfectly cooked, the pork belly (definitely not cha siu) was soft, a bit sweet, but not much flavor or texture. The sliced meat was, well, sliced meat. The broth was thicker than ramen broth as it should be, not very salty, but didn't have much distinct flavor. Do we mix it into the broth, do we coat something, or just eat it? Broth had a citrus taste tasted ... The buckwheat noodles are difficult to grab with the chopsticks. Cooked well, but you either have to use the spoon to help "lift and carry" into the broth, or lift the noodles high and partially drag the out of the bowl and into the broth without looking like a 6 year old. Wasn't that part of the experience of tsukemen? Again, having had tsukemen at Tsujita in LA we were disappointed. We kinda had to fight the noodles because they were difficult to eat. The broth isn't bad, but not the robust flavor you'd expect from a concentrated broth. And the diluted the thick broth with water vs. clear broth at Tsujita.

review_text: Extra Notes:. -Accepts credit card. -Get their green Aji Verde Sauce! -----. Conclusion:  With authentic banh mi establishments everywhere in Orange County, NK's pork banh mi manages to rise above them in taste. ----The Food----. Pork Banh Mi ($5.95)- MUST TRY. A popular phrase coined by Charlie Sheen years ago is exactly what this modern Vietnamese eatery achieves with their fusion food offerings. The marinated pork is deliciously flavorful, tender, and non-tendinous throughout. It's then stuffed with fresh cucumber, cilantro, and pickled carrots in a lightly toasted baguette. The marination does tread the line of being too salty for some, but I fell in love. Although there is already a subtle kick in the pork, douse it in their green ahi verde sauce for more heat. Bulgogi Steak Banh Mi ($6.45)- TRY IT. While the seared short rib is marvelously tender as the pork, I feel the bulgogi sauce is too sweet. It masks the complimenting flavors of the other ingredients and conceals the distinctive char that I adored from the sandwich above. Still considered to be a very solid order, but the pork banh mi is the better choice. I appreciate the handpacked patties, but a shame it doesn't match the flavor profiles of their banh mi. Cajun Garlic Fries ($3.95)- TRY IT. I was mildly disappointed when the fries came out since I heard how this Kitchen bombards their fries with garlic cloves--I didn't get any of that. Thankfully, the fries were crispy and lightly seasoned with a small hint of garlic taste. I'd compare it to Boiling Crab's, but just a couple levels below the crawfish house's standard. Nevertheless, I'll definitely be back for the pork sandwiches and other affordable menu options, like their pasta, tea's, and popcorn chicken.

review_text: It's not very often that you see a dessert shop specializing in the decadent cheesecakes. The sweet potato added a nice essence and was not overpowering at all, but distinct enough to know it wasn't pumpkin. Cheesecake King!
history_reviews: [['110545043251394065521_60478a3eb1a0aaee3eef8d70', 'After being indecisive of what order, I ended up getting a chocolate-filled Cream Horn and a Bavarian Cream-Filled Long John. The Cream Horn was a flaky shell covered with crunchy sugar crystals that provided a good contrast with thee chocolate-filled center. The Bavarian Cream-Filled Long John was what I was really excited to try since it is one of my favorites, but was left a bit disappointed because it was really dry and a bit hard that made eating it not as worth-while as the Cream Horn.'], ['110545043251394065521_604158ee7cd8bf1303624d84', 'I ended up getting the Royal Sangria and Fried Chicken and Donuts from their brunch menu. The Royal Sangria was a beautiful deep red with a solid fruity flavor. The fried chicken dish was good with a lot of flavor, but a bit expensive for what I was hoping for with not enough actual substance for around $30.'], ['110545043251394065521_6056b0c2f69c7b1178070103', 'Regardless of this hiccup, these are some of the best tacos I have ever eaten hands down. I got the Fixie and Wayfarer. The Fixie had a tropical flair with the pineapple and coconut aioli. I also got Chips and Guac and went with the Flour Chips just to be different. The guacamole was outstanding too.'], ['110545043251394065521_604f25a6934f413e7cfc37a5', "Healthy never tasted so good! This vegan juice bar is a great place to grab a smoothie or a superfood bowl. For the superfood bowls, their base is blended up fruit and a non-dairy liquid such a nut-based milk or coconut water with various add ins (like blue algae or charcoal!). They have their classic bowls such as their Cloud 9, but you can customize and I think that's the best thing here! They also have a whole bunch of cold pressed juices that are super fresh. I ended up getting their Roots with Ginger drink and it had a bit ginger zing that can come across 'spicy' if you aren't sure what to expect. For the smoothie, I customized mine with Pitaya, Mango, Pineapple, and Banana for the base with Coconut Mylk. A beautiful pink from the Pitaya and a nice tropical feel."], ['110545043251394065521_60561c48f69c7b117806ff05', 'They have really healthy offerings such as acai bowls, sandwiches, power bowls, smoothies and more! On this trip, I got their "Welcome to Miami" Smoothie and Blue Majik Bowl. The smoothie was good with crunchy seeds blended in that give it texture. I\'ve been seeing this "blue spirulina" pop up at a lot of healthy food stores. It came with blueberries, coconut, and granola.'], ['110545043251394065521_6046f99cb0e2129e475359c0', 'They offer all the classic bbq choices including brisket, pulled pork, pulled chicken, turkey, and sausage as well as ribs and salmon. I ended up getting a Two Meat Sampler of the brisket and turkey and added-on one of each rib (Bay-B-Que and St Louis Spare). Each of the meats had a great smoked flavor that was well balanced and went nicely with any one of their sauces. I also got their Mac & Cheese and Coleslaw for sides and both were on point. Super cheesy and creamy mac and crisp and bright slaw that complemented the meal wonderfully.'], ['110545043251394065521_6046f6b6b3114911423b7df0', "This is a cute little bakery that makes sweets with that 'homemade with love' feel. Not pretentious or super fancy, but just downright simple and good desserts. I ended up getting the Oreo Cheesecake Bite and Salted Caramel Cupcake. The cheesecake bite was delish and not overly sweet with a good amount of creaminess and oreo balance. The cupcake was equally good as well."], ['110545043251394065521_60504a2688c7af3f893e6aac', 'I always go for something taro-based or cream-filled and enjoyed the ratio of filling to bread that they had. I ended up also getting an Oolong Boba Tea and I was amazed at the quality of their tapioca balls. To me, they were everything that I look for in a boba ball: chewy, but not tacky, gummy or hard and a hint of sweetness, yet with a depth to it.'], ['110545043251394065521_6047e634b1a0aaee3eef94d6', 'I also ended up getting a quick appetizer of their Cocktail de Camarones (Shrimp Cocktail).'], ['110545043251394065521_6047075ac5f52be2a51dbd7d', "I was surprised with how much tuna I got per taco and was living for it (also comes with a side of black beans). Each taco was a nice filet of tuna on a bed of slaw and simple creamy drizzle on top. Finish it off with a nice squeeze of a lemon wedge and you got seafood simplicity at its best! If seafood isn't your thing, they also have chicken tacos too. Aside of their bomb fish tacos, this place is your typical 'Florida seafood' restaurant that can be on the pricier side. Their other non-seafood dishes are fine, but I find that they shine with seafood. Also to note, try to catch their seasonal specials of rock shrimp (typically July-October) or lionfish (March-July) as well so try it out since it is a local special! The rock shrimp tastes like lobster, but in shrimp form."]]

review_text: Hambone's is a popular BBQ joint in Bellflower owned and operated by pitmaster Kenny Hamilton who has come to Los Angeles via Mississippi. What drew me here was that this is one of the restaurants around south Los Angeles that sells what has become known as "black tacos," which refer to tacos sold by black-owned businesses to predominantly black customers. Hambone's serves a very basic "black taco" with chopped barbecued meat with sauce on flour tortillas, dressed with lettuce, shredded yellow cheese, and diced tomatoes. I was a bit bummed on account of not being able to taste the difference between the "Pulled Pork Taco" from the "Beef Tri-Tip Taco" due to the BBQ sauce on the meats being so sweet and pervasive that it made both tacos taste the same. My fascination with "black tacos" aside, I could smell Hambone's hickory-smoked meats from my car as I entered the parking lot, which put me in a mood to have something more substantial than a taco. I'm often disappointed in Southern California's BBQ restaurants, so I crossed my fingers as I ordered a "Half Rack of Spare Ribs." The ribs were neatly trimmed in a way that made me a little skeptical (in my experience, "pretty BBQ" is usually bad BBQ), but only in the brief moment before I began eating them. I was delighted by a persistent hickory flavor throughout textured, dense pork that cleanly snaps off the bone with a tug of your teeth. My biggest fault is that, like the taco meats, these ribs are heavily sauced with a thin glaze that is sweet and sticky, reminding me of an Asian-style sauce one would eat on the magenta-hued spare ribs found in Cantonese restaurants across America. Don't get me wrong, the sauce tastes fine -- I just wish there was less of it and that I had an opportunity to apply it myself. It's a shame, because Hamilton is proud of his rub and speaks of if it as his most secret of weapons, but I could not discern where the rub stops and the sauce begins, and the sauce made everything sooooo sweet. I also ordered "Collard Greens" that were flat greens heaped on one other -- again, almost "too neat-looking" for collards -- but nonetheless tender, piquant, filled with pork flavor, and just a touch of acid. On the whole, a pretty good BBQ spot.

Make no mistake though, the Colonel is like Escoffier next to Chicken Charlie. I haven't yet mentioned the mashed potatoes and gravy, WHICH WERE MADE WITH SPOILED DAIRY AND TASTED RANCID!"], ['108685370139018629938_6055afe397d555cc6fb0ce6f', "One of San Diego's finest taco shops. Try the carnitas here. Cabeza tacos are also excellent."], ['108685370139018629938_6045b409604fc398f591ecf7', 'The pork burrito is great, consisting of shredded pork stewed in spices accompanied by cotija cheese and lettuce, wrapped in a homemade lard-heavy flour tortilla. The gloriously greasy rolled tacos are also a good choice, featuring meat in a crispy rolled tortilla shell, deep fried, and then smothered with queso fresco and crema.'], ['108685370139018629938_60421d502e57ebdea29c81eb', 'Yes, it\'s a real good burger, think "In-N-Out Burger on Steroids" - but Hodad\'s kitchen and wait staff, mostly stoned out of their ever-loving skulls, operate on "beach time." This slo-mo style doesn\'t quite scale up to the immense demand for their burgers due to the massive amount of media exposure they\'ve gotten both locally as a long-time beloved San Diego beach staple and nationally on Food Network and other outlets. As for the burgers? I typically order the "Single Bacon Cheeseburger," which is the house specialty if there is one. I sometimes need to compress the burger with my hands a bit before trying to eat it, otherwise I cannot fit enough of it into my mouth to take a proper bite. Like I said, it\'s a real good burger. In fact, this is the quintessential American burger turned up to "11." I usually get my burger with a "basket combo," so that it includes Hodad\'s crispy thick-cut French fries, which are some of my favorite fries in all of San Diego due to their crunchy skin, soft hot innards, and near-perfect amount of seasoning. All everyone talks about are Hodad\'s burgers and shakes, leaving their fries underrated.'], ['108685370139018629938_6046d164b0e2129e475356f6', 'We also both enjoy the "Baja Ceviche," where each ingredient (shrimp, fish, crab) is distinct, but work delectably well together. Perhaps our favorite appetizer is the "Smoked Fish Tacos," essentially smoked fish hash piped into egg-roll-like taco shells. If you\'re looking for something more traditional, try the "Salt and Pepper Calamari." My entre recommendation is the Miso-Glazed Sea Bass with Crab Fried Rice, which is an extraordinary dish that is similar to Nobu\'s Miso-Marinated Black Cod. The flavoring aside, the fish preparation at Truluck\'s is top notch, and the sea bass is moist, firm-fleshed, and cooked to a level where it remains mild and delicate. The crab fried rice is lightly flavored in what I can only describe as "essence" of crab, and complements the sea bass perfectly. If you\'re not ordering the sea bass, then try the "South African Lobster Tail" if it is on the menu. South African lobsters are sweeter than normal lobsters, and here they do all of the work of de-shelling the massive 12 ounce tail, and setting it aside a substantial portion of parmesan mashed potatoes and steamed asparagus.'], ['108685370139018629938_6051045f5b4ccec8d5cae9d5', 'I recommend the mushroom chicken dish first and foremost, though the tamales and the tacos (blackened fish especially) are excellent as well.'], ['108685370139018629938_60489685b3f169c178160577', 'Mitla Caf\'s tacos are the foundation of the Taco Bell empire. As you first bite into one of Mitla Caf\'s Beef Tacos (labeled as just "Taco" on the menu), you can\'t help but think of a Taco Bell\'s taco, except done 100 times better. As grease and juices fall out of the house-made misshapen fried tortilla, you\'ll taste the heavily-browned and spiced ground beef covered with shredded cheddar cheese, refreshing lettuce, and bright red tomatoes, and you will understand why someone would start a fast food company around this. Sometimes it\'s better to be lucky than good, because for as many billions of dollars that the Taco Bell brand is worth, Glen Bell ultimately failed to capture what makes this taco work. Mitla Caf\'s "Shredded Beef Taco" is probably a better taco than their regular "Taco," but it doesn\'t channel the same kind of nostalgia. The "Shredded Beef Taco" does, however, have a cleaner flavor and truer purity of purpose. Either taco greatly benefits from the red sauce (you need to ask for a side of it when you order), a fiery salsa that puts Taco Bell\'s little spicy ketchup packets to shame. During my visit, I also ordered the Pozole, which is served white (i.e. Pozole Blanco), with minimal garnishes (no oregano, for example), and pork that was over-cooked. My advice is to pass on the Pozole and eat more tacos. In fact, always eat more tacos.'], ['108685370139018629938_604e0a1471ced5c7554dda32', "I came here seeking the Korean Fried Chicken and the Panko-Crusted Japanese Fried Chicken. Both were boneless, sufficiently moist, and tasty. The Korean variant had been subjected to a char-sui/teriyaki-like magenta glaze before deep-frying, resulting in a piece of chicken tinged in a pleasant sweetness that didn't really need any saucing. Nonetheless, I enjoyed the sweet soy-infused katsu sauce, but didn't care as much for the lava sauce, which tasted like sweet and sour ketchup and, despite its name, didn't actually deliver any heat. Macaroni Salad is delicious -- much moreso than the Green Salad which is overpowered by an aggressively dark sesame-flavored dressing. The Malasadas (Portuguese fried dough) are also legit here, a great way to end your meal, even if they're not the larger, thinner variety I grew up with."], ['108685370139018629938_60561c8d97d555cc6fb0d0f3', 'My visit was short and I dined solo at the bar, eating some nigiri (Otoro and Hamachi) in addition to the Rock Shrimp Tempura.'], ['108685370139018629938_604da44a77e81aaed3cca9df', 'During my first trip here, I ordered the "Crispy Chicken Sandwich." I wish I had more fried chicken like this in my life, but I can\'\'t afford to. Yes, this is one of the best chicken sandwiches I\'ve had anywhere, but is it worth the $18 price tag? I am confident, however, that the juiciness of the chicken, the sturdy and well-seasoned fried batter, the creamy cole slaw, the earthy swiss cheese, and the fresh sesame-coated roll combine to make this almost as perfect as a fried chicken sandwich can be. Lastly, I had the "Honor Burger" on my second visit, which is a burger topped with a condiment mix that reminded me of Burger King\'s Whopper, but produced by a professional cook. The textural contrast was wonderful: crispy salty bits, spicy and sour chewy bits, fresh onions and cilantro, and a heavy, thick corn tortilla. The sweet tortilla tastes like fresh corn, which is how a good tortilla really ought to taste. This is, without a doubt, the best Buche Taco I\'ve eaten. The "Tripa Taco" was dispatched next, and I found it to be worth ordering as well, even if it is not as transcendent as the Buche Taco. The tripa taco also features onions, cilantro, and a snappy salsa verde.'], ['108685370139018629938_60548f4a6204e8cd294f2344', "The churros are decent, I'm just not sure this place is necessary in a city where you can't throw a taco without hitting a place that sells churros. Here you can order your Spanish donut sticks covered in Fruity Pebbles, matcha, Nutella, or just about any trendy sweet topping du jour; in other words, if someone with Snapchat puppy ears can put it on a scoop of conflict-free non-GMO gelato, you'll find it here. Perhaps I was expecting churros that were so extraordinary that they merited a fast-casual spot on Convoy that does nothing but churros. What I got was a warm, crispy, cinnamon-sugar pastry that was par for the course in this region, with some sweet, sticky dips on the side."], ['108685370139018629938_60464d69882f4d1caf5fee25', 'One of my favorites I\'ve visited has been "Tacos Tumbras a Tomas," an operation that has been around since 1995, run by Tomas Martinez with his brothers Jesus and Manuel. The "Carnitas Taco." Here, the pork shoulder is cooked confit-style in simmering lard in a large steel cazo. A generous amount of the resulting carnitas is piled onto double corn tortillas, with two extra tortillas given on the side for good measure -- there is, after all, a ton of meat involved here. Chopped onions, cilantro, salsa roja, and a full lime (halved) are provided on the taco if you say "yes" when you\'re asked if you want "the works" or "con todo." The entire thing cost me $4.50, tax included, but was easily the equivalent of more than two normal-sized carnitas tacos. I suggest Tacos Tumbras a Tomas for a satisfying, filling, affordable lunch served without the lines or fuss of some of the busier stalls in the vicinity.'], ['108685370139018629938_604749eab0e2129e47536090', 'My wife and I dined here recently, beginning our meal with the "Mother Board," a cutting board spread of a cured meats (Bresaola, Duck Pt, Salami) and cheeses (Camembert, Bucheron, Drunken Goat) with some familiar fixins\' mixed in with some not-so-familiar. The "Ahi Poke Tuna Tacos" were much enjoyed by my wife and me. The texture of the ahi is stunning and delicate, its tender, raw chunks will melt in your mouth. The Asian slaw is sweet, but not overly so, and the wonton "taco shell" is crispy but light, the combination of all of this coming across as decadent, but not heavy. Evaluating it strictly as a taco, it may not have conventional taco ingredients, but it is a very well-composed bite of food, balancing the fish, sauce, cabbage, and shell like a legit taquero would. My entre was the "Greater Omaha Prime Flat Iron," a half-pound steak that was cooked to a luscious medium-rare as I requested, its edges and surfaces blasted with heat so its seasonings and fat mix with charred outer-proteins to form a marvelous crust. A creamy parsnip pure, savory slices of grilled trumpet mushrooms, and crisp asparagus in herb butter complete a delectable steak dish that didn\'t break the bank, at just $34 all-in.'], ['108685370139018629938_60520101da79151bfc125c2d', "I'm usually alright with White Castle, but not when it immobilizes me on my Vegas vacation for a day and a half."], ['108685370139018629938_605676dc3019cb0a47838d38', 'The Pork Souvlaki was real good (and I recommend this if you come here), even if I thought the Gyros were so-so.'], ['108685370139018629938_604e0d8b71ced5c7554dda45', 'Obviously here in San Diego, most of the food at "On The Border" is awful compared to what you can get from a myriad of legit, authentic local Mexican restaurants. I say "most" and not "all" because the one thing On The Border has engineered of value are their complimentary chips and salsa, which stand up to the best chips and salsa that even a city like San Diego has to offer. Maybe order some guacamole (which they make in front of you, table-side.)'], ['108685370139018629938_60425ef37dfa7f187183c4de', 'While approaching this taco truck, my eyes were immediately drawn to a large trompo stacked with layers of well-manicured adobo-marinated pork spinning around, reflecting a flame off of a glistening surface sweating with achiote-infused meat juices. Upon ordering an "Al Pastor Taco" here, the taquero will carve off thin slices of pork directly off of this upside-down mountain of meat into single corn tortillas and top it off with a chunk of pineapple. Aside from the customary onions and cilantro, ensure your taco has El Flamin\'s red sauce on it. This is a hypnotic, mouth-numbing salsa roja that complements and completes the al pastor pork, and the "secret sauce" that keeps this truck doing brisk business. El Flamin\'s "Al Pastor Tacos" would be better with a more assertive marinade, so they do not reach the same heights as the al pastor served at Leo\'s or even the Ave 26 Taco Stand, but they are definitely in my "top 5" favorite pastor-style tacos in Los Angeles. review_text: We love a good burger, and while visiting Chicago, a friend highly recommended this restaurant to us saying it was the best burger in the city! Since the waffle sammies have a lot going on in them, I'd recommend getting regular fries, or just skipping the fries altogether."], ['103707591633272033722_604c406477e81aaed3cc9df1', "I asked for a cosmo, less sweet and they actually made it as such. They also have a few craft bottled Japanese beers (not on happy hour), which was a nice change of pace from the typical Sapporo and Kirin you see at Japanese restaurants. You can also get $5 select apps (sliders, chicken yakitori, california roll, edamame, gyoza, kani salad, fries). I had a fried chicken slider, which I absolutely loved. The chicken was juicy, and came with a spicy mayo sauce. The California rolls are California rolls - nothing special, and the kani salad was just okay. I guess I missed the part where the menu mentioned the salmon part because I was just expecting something like agedashi tofu. I went with the Dynamite Roll (wild blue crab, avocado topped w. seared spicy scallops, crunch, fried vermicelli - $17) and the Harajuku Roll (salmon, mango, cucumber topped wtih spicy salmon, crunchy flakes, scallion, caviar mango sauce - $15), to share. The first piece of the Dynamite roll tasted a bit off. And just in case we weren't already ordering too much food, we threw in a duck ramen for good measure. review_text: I got the "Salted Caramel Apple" which comes with a cinnamon apple sponge cake, green apple coulis, whipped cream and salted caramel gelato. The salted caramel gelato is SO BOOOMB.
history_reviews: [['110507600967459500396_604e3208b9a3d5528c50bd2e', "Ugh, the whiskey cake dessert is a 6 out of 5 - it's a dessert of the Gods.. All the flavors come together so well and each bite makes my heart so happy. The bourbon anglaise and the whipped cream are ahhhh-mazing. I could drink the bourbon anglaise. You definitely have to make sure each bite includes the bourbon anglaise AND whipped cream! You probably have to run 10 miles to burn off this cake but YOU GUYS, it is SO worth it! I had the chicken & cheese melt which was actually really good. The rotisserie chicken isn't dry and that combined with avocado and pesto mayo on sourdough is just a really great combination (also comes with BLT). We also also ordered the parmesan fries and adult mac n' cheese. Not really a fan of either - they were both pretty average."], ['110507600967459500396_60553a4d3019cb0a47838831', "Hong Kong Eatery is the first place in Boston I tried roast duck and crispy roast pork from. I love siu mei restaurants because seeing the array of meats hanging gets my mouth watering. The roast duck here is pretty delicious, I like the flavor and the meat was tender. I ordered half of a roasted duck and the pieces we got didn't have much meat on them. I ended up picking through a lot of bones but the flavor is there and some ducks are just meatier than others. The crispy roast pork was not too bad. The meat wasn't thick and cube-like like I am used to. While the pork was tender and not dry, it didn't hold together well and was easily separated. I'm used to thick, juicy, tender pieces of pork with a layer of fat and the crispy skin on top. Hong Kong Eater definitely has the layer of fat and crispy skin but as a whole the pieces just kind of fall apart. Overall their roast duck and crispy roast pork satisfies a craving and I'd get it again but it isn't my #1 option in Chinatown."], ['110507600967459500396_60503bc249d2a5e60e2d576a', 'The chili oil is a tasty mixture, however, it is lacking in heat. The Sandong style pan fried dumplings with pork & shrimp were good but I would have liked them more if they were even crispier. Each of our dumpling dishes came with their own dipping sauce. The scallion pancakes were perfect! My boyfriend and I are going through a phase where we are obsessed with salt & pepper chicken wings and calamari so we had to order them. Both the chicken wings and calamari sit on a bed of iceberg lettuce to add a different texture and balance out the saltiness. I love that the chicken wings were also seasoned with that special Chinese seasoning on top of the salt & pepper that really just enhances the whole dish.'], ['110507600967459500396_605101705266728eda27a548', 'It was everything great about the fall season in cupcake form. Copper Door provides popovers with butter which was pretty tasty. We started off with the calamari appetizer which was just okay. I got the "Stuffed Haddock Oscar" and it was super delicious! I was all about the fresh prime haddock with lump crab. The garlic fingerling potatoes were on point as well.'], ['110507600967459500396_6053c7af7fec92c07c643d52', "Village Burger Bar is pretty great. My brother and sister like their burgers. Although I don't come here for their burgers, I am a fan of their paninis, especially their Chicken Pesto Panini. I also love their fries. I am not a big fan of sweet potato fries but Village Burger Bar has good fries all around. Their sweet potato fries, shoestring fries, and parmesan truffle fries are all super tasty."], ['110507600967459500396_60569e863019cb0a47838ddd', 'For a breakfast & brunch place, they do have an interesting menu that has your classics as well as creative takes on the usual breakfast items. We started off with the "Nacho Business" and added barbacoa braised beef. I\'m a fan of all things Tex-Mex being a true Texas gal through and through but I thought these were alright. The barbacoa was not too shabby. I wasn\'t a huge fan of the chips but I couldn\'t put my finger on it as to why. The queso wasn\'t all too flavorful either ...probably because it\'s just melted jalapeo jack with nothing added to it. I definitely made use of the side of avocado-lime sauce to add some much needed freshness and contrast - I just wish there was more of it. I opted for the "Waffle" and added fresh berries & whipped cream. No complaints there but if you can\'t make waffles can you even establish yourself as a breakfast joint? Had I not added the berries and cream it would have been a super lackluster dish.']]
