review_text: Yes, the Al Pastor Taco from the Ave 26 Taco Stand, on any given day, could be just as good as an Al Pastor Taco from Leo's Taco Truck, or my long-time personal favorite down in San Diego, Tacos El Gordo. What could put it over the edge are the grilled onions cooked down until they sweeten and begin to caramelize, then blended with the meat carved from the trompo. You could be completely satisfied  NO, captivated  by a taco filled with ONLY the Al Pastor pork, without any additional sauces or garnishments. However, I recommend the chopped raw onions and cilantro from the salsa bar, and it would be criminal to not add at least a bit of Ave 26's rousing salsa roja. It will reinforce to you that you are indeed eating legit "street tacos as opposed to the heavily-garnished crapola fraudulently peddled as "street tacos" on this side of the border.
history_reviews: [['108685370139018629938_6051f93188c7af3f893e7394', "I ordered the 2 piece Chicken Meal with Mashed Potatoes ($6.95) with a pint of beer. Beyond the dryness, the chicken had an extremely salty, thin crust. The thin texture of the fried batter was similar to KFC's Original Recipe. Make no mistake though, the Colonel is like Escoffier next to Chicken Charlie. I haven't yet mentioned the mashed potatoes and gravy, WHICH WERE MADE WITH SPOILED DAIRY AND TASTED RANCID!"], ['108685370139018629938_6055afe397d555cc6fb0ce6f', "One of San Diego's finest taco shops. Try the carnitas here. Cabeza tacos are also excellent."], ['108685370139018629938_6045b409604fc398f591ecf7', 'The pork burrito is great, consisting of shredded pork stewed in spices accompanied by cotija cheese and lettuce, wrapped in a homemade lard-heavy flour tortilla. The gloriously greasy rolled tacos are also a good choice, featuring meat in a crispy rolled tortilla shell, deep fried, and then smothered with queso fresco and crema.'], ['108685370139018629938_60421d502e57ebdea29c81eb', 'Yes, it\'s a real good burger, think "In-N-Out Burger on Steroids" - but Hodad\'s kitchen and wait staff, mostly stoned out of their ever-loving skulls, operate on "beach time." This slo-mo style doesn\'t quite scale up to the immense demand for their burgers due to the massive amount of media exposure they\'ve gotten both locally as a long-time beloved San Diego beach staple and nationally on Food Network and other outlets. As for the burgers? I typically order the "Single Bacon Cheeseburger," which is the house specialty if there is one. I sometimes need to compress the burger with my hands a bit before trying to eat it, otherwise I cannot fit enough of it into my mouth to take a proper bite. Like I said, it\'s a real good burger. In fact, this is the quintessential American burger turned up to "11." I usually get my burger with a "basket combo," so that it includes Hodad\'s crispy thick-cut French fries, which are some of my favorite fries in all of San Diego due to their crunchy skin, soft hot innards, and near-perfect amount of seasoning. All everyone talks about are Hodad\'s burgers and shakes, leaving their fries underrated.'], ['108685370139018629938_6046d164b0e2129e475356f6', 'We also both enjoy the "Baja Ceviche," where each ingredient (shrimp, fish, crab) is distinct, but work delectably well together. Perhaps our favorite appetizer is the "Smoked Fish Tacos," essentially smoked fish hash piped into egg-roll-like taco shells. If you\'re looking for something more traditional, try the "Salt and Pepper Calamari." My entre recommendation is the Miso-Glazed Sea Bass with Crab Fried Rice, which is an extraordinary dish that is similar to Nobu\'s Miso-Marinated Black Cod. The flavoring aside, the fish preparation at Truluck\'s is top notch, and the sea bass is moist, firm-fleshed, and cooked to a level where it remains mild and delicate. The crab fried rice is lightly flavored in what I can only describe as "essence" of crab, and complements the sea bass perfectly. If you\'re not ordering the sea bass, then try the "South African Lobster Tail" if it is on the menu. South African lobsters are sweeter than normal lobsters, and here they do all of the work of de-shelling the massive 12 ounce tail, and setting it aside a substantial portion of parmesan mashed potatoes and steamed asparagus.'], ['108685370139018629938_6051045f5b4ccec8d5cae9d5', 'I recommend the mushroom chicken dish first and foremost, though the tamales and the tacos (blackened fish especially) are excellent as well.'], ['108685370139018629938_60489685b3f169c178160577', 'Mitla Caf\'s tacos are the foundation of the Taco Bell empire. As you first bite into one of Mitla Caf\'s Beef Tacos (labeled as just "Taco" on the menu), you can\'t help but think of a Taco Bell\'s taco, except done 100 times better. As grease and juices fall out of the house-made misshapen fried tortilla, you\'ll taste the heavily-browned and spiced ground beef covered with shredded cheddar cheese, refreshing lettuce, and bright red tomatoes, and you will understand why someone would start a fast food company around this. Sometimes it\'s better to be lucky than good, because for as many billions of dollars that the Taco Bell brand is worth, Glen Bell ultimately failed to capture what makes this taco work. Mitla Caf\'s "Shredded Beef Taco" is probably a better taco than their regular "Taco," but it doesn\'t channel the same kind of nostalgia. The "Shredded Beef Taco" does, however, have a cleaner flavor and truer purity of purpose. Either taco greatly benefits from the red sauce (you need to ask for a side of it when you order), a fiery salsa that puts Taco Bell\'s little spicy ketchup packets to shame. During my visit, I also ordered the Pozole, which is served white (i.e. Pozole Blanco), with minimal garnishes (no oregano, for example), and pork that was over-cooked. My advice is to pass on the Pozole and eat more tacos. In fact, always eat more tacos.'], ['108685370139018629938_604e0a1471ced5c7554dda32', "I came here seeking the Korean Fried Chicken and the Panko-Crusted Japanese Fried Chicken. Both were boneless, sufficiently moist, and tasty. The Korean variant had been subjected to a char-sui/teriyaki-like magenta glaze before deep-frying, resulting in a piece of chicken tinged in a pleasant sweetness that didn't really need any saucing. Nonetheless, I enjoyed the sweet soy-infused katsu sauce, but didn't care as much for the lava sauce, which tasted like sweet and sour ketchup and, despite its name, didn't actually deliver any heat. Macaroni Salad is delicious -- much moreso than the Green Salad which is overpowered by an aggressively dark sesame-flavored dressing. The Malasadas (Portuguese fried dough) are also legit here, a great way to end your meal, even if they're not the larger, thinner variety I grew up with."], ['108685370139018629938_60561c8d97d555cc6fb0d0f3', 'My visit was short and I dined solo at the bar, eating some nigiri (Otoro and Hamachi) in addition to the Rock Shrimp Tempura.'], ['108685370139018629938_604da44a77e81aaed3cca9df', 'During my first trip here, I ordered the "Crispy Chicken Sandwich." I wish I had more fried chicken like this in my life, but I can\'\'t afford to. Yes, this is one of the best chicken sandwiches I\'ve had anywhere, but is it worth the $18 price tag? I am confident, however, that the juiciness of the chicken, the sturdy and well-seasoned fried batter, the creamy cole slaw, the earthy swiss cheese, and the fresh sesame-coated roll combine to make this almost as perfect as a fried chicken sandwich can be. Lastly, I had the "Honor Burger" on my second visit, which is a burger topped with a condiment mix that reminded me of Burger King\'s Whopper, but produced by a professional cook. The meat, ordered and prepared medium rare, had plenty of life in it and is not entirely overwhelmed by the melted cheddar, mix of slaw, special sauce, and tomatoes, but I feel they could scale down the condiment-to-beef ratio just a tad and have twice as good of a burger.'], ['108685370139018629938_60412b777cd8bf1303623e48', 'Hambone\'s is a popular BBQ joint in Bellflower owned and operated by pitmaster Kenny Hamilton who has come to Los Angeles via Mississippi. What drew me here was that this is one of the restaurants around south Los Angeles that sells what has become known as "black tacos," which refer to tacos sold by black-owned businesses to predominantly black customers. Hambone\'s serves a very basic "black taco" with chopped barbecued meat with sauce on flour tortillas, dressed with lettuce, shredded yellow cheese, and diced tomatoes. I was a bit bummed on account of not being able to taste the difference between the "Pulled Pork Taco" from the "Beef Tri-Tip Taco" due to the BBQ sauce on the meats being so sweet and pervasive that it made both tacos taste the same. My fascination with "black tacos" aside, I could smell Hambone\'s hickory-smoked meats from my car as I entered the parking lot, which put me in a mood to have something more substantial than a taco. I\'m often disappointed in Southern California\'s BBQ restaurants, so I crossed my fingers as I ordered a "Half Rack of Spare Ribs." A generous amount of the resulting carnitas is piled onto double corn tortillas, with two extra tortillas given on the side for good measure -- there is, after all, a ton of meat involved here. Chopped onions, cilantro, salsa roja, and a full lime (halved) are provided on the taco if you say "yes" when you\'re asked if you want "the works" or "con todo." The entire thing cost me $4.50, tax included, but was easily the equivalent of more than two normal-sized carnitas tacos. review_text: Best ramen in the bay area that I have tried thus far, including Orenchi and Santouka. Broth is super flavorful and the meat is very tasty! For now, as this is currently the best ramen place I have tried in the bay area I guess I will have to learn to wait.
history_reviews: [['100844871389719797306_604b7b0a77e81aaed3cc954e', 'Only pho place I know that puts ox tail into the pho, really love the added flavor and meatiness of the ox tail in the #1. The calamari was tender, the breading was not overwhelming, and the accompanying sauce was a touch spicy and very flavorful, definitely recommend! The kids enjoyed their flank steaks with Sprites, I did not try it, but based on the speed at which the steaks were consumed I have to assume it was cooked decently. I tried a bite of my wife's sea bass, and I must say it was perfectly cooked, very flakey and just the right amount of seasoning, not too over powering where you couldn't enjoy the quality of the fish. I did not try the crab cake, but it did look good. I love the flavor of stewed ox tail so stewing it in a tomato sauce really made sense adding flavor to both the sauce and adding a nice tangy and sweet flavor to the ox tail, a very nice combination!"]]

review_text: Boudin Balls: many times, people will over cook the rice, not realizing that after you prepare the rice, it still has to be fried and therefore will turn to Mush up on service. Collard Greens: all too often, people resort to using canned greens, which are mushy and chops to a fine Mash. These were obviously fresh, local greens that were treated with love and care, being cooked for hours. Mac and Cheese: not just cheese with with some noodles. They obviously use the rich, and flavorful, bechamel sauce before topping it with more cheese and placing it in their wood fired oven. Layers of flavor, something so experts for just something as simple as mac and cheese. Pork Cheek and Hominy Cake: if there was a bone, I would have fell off. The Hominy cake was creamy, and cut into a circle with the meat placed upon X and having the sauce drizzled over. Lima Beans: as evident from the other side items, it was actually done. The beans were Al Dente, not crunchy, but just enough to texture and toothyness so that it wasn't lost in the rich beany gravy. The pork shoulder that has been smoked and season was informed into a Patty, seared, and then heated in the oven until hot enough to enjoy. On the day we went we were able to enjoy a patty melt on rye swirl bread. The patty melt and sauteed mushrooms, onions and peppers. Also included was a special sauce, and cheese, served with a mandolin sliced broccoli salad.

review_text: I usually hear about these donuts from Portland travelers, but when I saw there was one in Denver (two actually), I obviously had to try it on my trip. My husband and I decided to split three donuts because we couldn't narrow what to get down more than that. We got Mango Tango, Key Lime Crush, and Guava Colada. I think Mango Tango was my favorite followed very closely by the Key Lime Crush. The key lime filling wasn't quite as good to me (which isn't surprising given how much I love mango), but the toppings were the best. The graham cracker, vanilla frosting, caramel drizzle was the perfect crunch/flavor enhancer. The Guava Colada was my least favorite. I enjoyed the guava filling and the vanilla frosting. The coconut didn't really enhance the donut for me, but I'm also not a huge coconut person. The donut carousel would be perfect for deciding what flavor to get. If you're a donut lover, this is definitely a place you need to check out!

The strawberry daiquiri was dangerous as you cant really taste the alcohol and it just seems like a smoothie.'], ['105853218368004682403_604e0202b9a3d5528c50bc5b', 'I could wax poetic about the virtues of the Mexican chocolate pie at The Pie Hole, but to put it simply, the Pie Hole consistently has delicious desserts that are indulgent and rich. You should split the pies with loved ones, although its certainly doable to eat an entire slice by yourself. You can order a whole pie if youd like, and they do offer drinks like matcha tea and coffee. The cashier was very friendly and mentioned that they have happy hour from Monday through Friday where pie slices are $5 and whole pies are ~$30.'], ['105853218368004682403_604913b3b1a0aaee3eefa92e', 'The cheesecakes are a 5 but the food is a solid 3. For a family of four, we got an egg roll sampler, a regular size farfalle pasta with chicken and a garlic cream sauce, and two cheesecakes. The egg roll sampler was a good order since theres a variety to try and theres plenty of dipping sauce to choose from. My favorite was the avocado one, but everyone else really liked the hamburger egg roll dipped into the pink sauce (which I think is thousand island dressing). The pasta was disappointing - it was super oily with sparse amounts of chicken and accoutrements. The cheesecakes were the highlight - the godiva one is so decadent and rich, so its perfect for a chocolate fanatic. The white chocolate macadamia nut with the blondie brownie crust was also a surprise hit. The macadamia nuts were a bit soggy, but paired well with the white chocolate chunks. The bottom layer brownie was nice and and chewy, and complemented the creaminess of the cheesecake.'], ['105853218368004682403_6057007d6fce2069470c60cf', 'I used to love going to Raising Canes when I lived in Phoenix, so I was excited to get my chicken tender fix. Its an extra 30 something cents per sauce but they do keep well if you want to use them for some home cooked chicken tenders. The fries are crinkle-cut and were under seasoned. The Texas toast was very good - it was still warm and buttery by the time we got to eat it. The combo also comes with coleslaw although you can request another piece of toast in lieu of it.'], ['105853218368004682403_60442190b81264dfa846d73c', 'Tried the Chicago hot dog - while it was a good hot dog, it certainly wasnt life changing. The chicken seasoning on the skin is good but the meat itself is bland, so get the hot sauce. I ended up getting a Tavern Burger and a side of fries and sat at a table in the back area outside. When it comes to the food, the Tavern Burger is $5 and the fries were $3, so an affordable meal in Seattle nowadays. The value is through the roof when you take into account of how great the burger is. review_text: Hong Kong Eatery is the first place in Boston I tried roast duck and crispy roast pork from. I love siu mei restaurants because seeing the array of meats hanging gets my mouth watering. The roast duck here is pretty delicious, I like the flavor and the meat was tender. I ordered half of a roasted duck and the pieces we got didn't have much meat on them. I ended up picking through a lot of bones but the flavor is there and some ducks are just meatier than others. The crispy roast pork was not too bad. The meat wasn't thick and cube-like like I am used to. While the pork was tender and not dry, it didn't hold together well and was easily separated. I'm used to thick, juicy, tender pieces of pork with a layer of fat and the crispy skin on top. Hong Kong Eater definitely has the layer of fat and crispy skin but as a whole the pieces just kind of fall apart. Overall their roast duck and crispy roast pork satisfies a craving and I'd get it again but it isn't my #1 option in Chinatown.

I had the chicken & cheese melt which was actually really good. The rotisserie chicken isn't dry and that combined with avocado and pesto mayo on sourdough is just a really great combination (also comes with BLT). We also also ordered the parmesan fries and adult mac n' cheese. We started off with the "Nacho Business" and added barbacoa braised beef. I\'m a fan of all things Tex-Mex being a true Texas gal through and through but I thought these were alright. The barbacoa was not too shabby. I wasn\'t a huge fan of the chips but I couldn\'t put my finger on it as to why. I liked how the chicken was breaded and it was still crunchy even after the 20 minute car ride home. The sandwich does come with pickles, and you can get a non-spicy sandwich (although the spicy sandwich is definitely manageable, and in the same level as hot Cheetos).'], ['105853218368004682403_6048c7438b84f513e32cdad6', 'He made sure to countdown so we could capture the giant flame he made for the bananas foster for the gram. They have aperitifs as well, and the Irish coffee was nicely sweet with a kick.'], ['105853218368004682403_6051e16bc53d98b3eace1d8b', 'The poutine was good, although I felt the gravy couldve couldve used a tad more salt and the cheese curds werent chewy.'], ['105853218368004682403_60570118c4674474cff9120f', 'I liked that the broth was separated from the noodles so you can mix it up yourself when youre ready to eat. The broth for the beef curry udon was watery and only had a hint of curry. The broth for the spicy pork ramen was better but it was not spicy at all. I would say the ABC ramen was the best of the three we had, although there were less pieces of meat than they typically provide.'], ['105853218368004682403_605680a03019cb0a47838d6b', 'The real MVP were the Irish coffee and strawberry daiquiris. The Irish coffee was mixed well with the coffee overpowering the whiskey (for the most part) but without being overly sweet. The strawberry daiquiri was dangerous as you cant really taste the alcohol and it just seems like a smoothie.'], ['105853218368004682403_604e0202b9a3d5528c50bc5b', 'I could wax poetic about the virtues of the Mexican chocolate pie at The Pie Hole, but to put it simply, the Pie Hole consistently has delicious desserts that are indulgent and rich. The Mexican chocolate pie is thick and creamy, while the earl grey pie is more light and airy, but grounded by the toasted pistachios that adorn its top. You should split the pies with loved ones, although its certainly doable to eat an entire slice by yourself. You can order a whole pie if youd like, and they do offer drinks like matcha tea and coffee. The cashier was very friendly and mentioned that they have happy hour from Monday through Friday where pie slices are $5 and whole pies are ~$30.'], ['105853218368004682403_604913b3b1a0aaee3eefa92e', 'The cheesecakes are a 5 but the food is a solid 3. For a family of four, we got an egg roll sampler, a regular size farfalle pasta with chicken and a garlic cream sauce, and two cheesecakes. The egg roll sampler was a good order since theres a variety to try and theres plenty of dipping sauce to choose from. My favorite was the avocado one, but everyone else really liked the hamburger egg roll dipped into the pink sauce (which I think is thousand island dressing). The pasta was disappointing - it was super oily with sparse amounts of chicken and accoutrements. The cheesecakes were the highlight - the godiva one is so decadent and rich, so its perfect for a chocolate fanatic. The white chocolate macadamia nut with the blondie brownie crust was also a surprise hit. The macadamia nuts were a bit soggy, but paired well with the white chocolate chunks. The bottom layer brownie was nice and and chewy, and complemented the creaminess of the cheesecake.'], ['105853218368004682403_6057007d6fce2069470c60cf', 'I used to love going to Raising Canes when I lived in Phoenix, so I was excited to get my chicken tender fix. This might be an LA thing, but the chicken tenders were a lot smaller and they really skimped on the fries. The chicken tenders are pretty bland, but the sauce is good. Its an extra 30 something cents per sauce but they do keep well if you want to use them for some home cooked chicken tenders. The fries are crinkle-cut and were under seasoned. The Texas toast was very good - it was still warm and buttery by the time we got to eat it. The combo also comes with coleslaw although you can request another piece of toast in lieu of it.'], ['105853218368004682403_60442190b81264dfa846d73c', 'Tried the Chicago hot dog - while it was a good hot dog, it certainly wasnt life changing. I liked the sesame seed bun and how soft it was. I liked the chili dog more - it wasnt soggy but still soft and I like the flavor of the chili.'], ['105853218368004682403_60497a77c7c8ee3104ba1994', 'Your typical fast food restaurant serving fried chicken and biscuits. For the four of us we got the family combo which comes with 8 pieces of chicken, a large side, and four buttermilk biscuits for ~$29. The chicken seasoning on the skin is good but the meat itself is bland, so get the hot sauce. Fries were really good and salty, and the biscuits were too dry.'], ['105853218368004682403_60562767f69c7b117806ff40', 'They only do either chicken tenders or sliders, but they do them extremely well. You can get a combo of 2 tenders plus crinkle cut fries (which were also well-seasoned) for ~$11 and add an extra tender for ~$3 more.'], ['105853218368004682403_6042604f7dfa7f187183c59a', 'I had the pasta pancetta ($16)which I wish had more pancetta pieces, but was very good. I liked the chewiness of the pasta, and the caramelized onions lent a nice mellow flavor. The sauce was a little bit too oily but for those that like a creamy sauce, this pasta is a good call.'], ['105853218368004682403_605636f03019cb0a47838c6d', 'Truffled egg sandwich: Simple yet flavorful, the mushrooms, cheese, soft scrambled eggs, and crispy bacon come together in a tantalizing bite on buttery bread. Chicken fried steak: the steak was very large and nicely fried. Prime rib hash: The prime rib is cut finely but theres a good amount. Corned beef hash: the corned beef is cut pretty small, but this was a good savory option and good for those who are on the hungrier side.'], ['105853218368004682403_6047348cb1a0aaee3eef858c', 'Local burger joint that uses English muffins for buns. Mexican Coke was $2.95 and the burgers ranged from ~$13 to $16. The veggie burger was better than I expected and comes with two toppings. I got grilled onions and thousand island dressing plus sharp cheddar for an extra 50 cents. The veggie burger was hearty and full of flavor though a tad bit dry. The fries were my favorite - theyre Belgian style and so tasty. We all preferred the fries over our burgers. The Blake Burger came with green chilies that were more salty than flavorful. The Wrigley Field Burger came with bacon (always a plus) and all the burgers had a lettuce, tomato, and pickle spear on the side. The English muffin in lieu of a burger bun seems like a good idea in theory as it holds the patty more firmly but it was also a bit dryer. I like that the beef is grass fed but it also means that the more well-cooked it is, the dryer the meat becomes.'], ['105853218368004682403_604e53656c0a991ff657c0a3', 'Oysters - One is my favorites. Crispy fried quail - Comes in two pieces. House made pasta - I was a bit disappointed but it was still high quality pasta with good texture (cooked al dente). Sweet and spicy glazed duck leg - has an XO sauce and is apparently Szechuan-inspired. Cornbread - underwhelming - I preferred the free house bread rolls provided at the start of the meal. Crispy catfish - came in two pieces and lightly breaded & fried. Flat iron steak - recommended to be medium rare. Reminds me of the Diddy Riese one. Its on the more bitter side and the accompanying biscotti is surprisingly spicy (I liked its unexpected nature). Drinks - The Papa holiday tasted like grapefruit, while the fist of berries has a licorice taste.'], ['105853218368004682403_605616813019cb0a47838bc6', 'Some positives: the bacon wrapped scallops were good.'], ['105853218368004682403_60535e0c88c7af3f893e7af9', 'Popular Cuban bakery with delectable cheese roll pastries. If I could subsist just on these cheese rolls, I would. The cheese filling inside is a good balance of salty and sweet, and the flaky pastry in the outside is melt-in-your-mouth delicious. The guava pastries are also a popular thing to bring in - the jam inside the pastry is sweet and they smell strong of guava (which some like, I personally dont, but Ill eat then anyways). They also have savory items like croquettes and sandwiches. They have cakes which you can pre-order for special events. Overall its truly an LA institution and I love eating one (or two or three) of their pastries.'], ['105853218368004682403_604c780d5a9e6adec8bf8af8', 'We got the chow mein and fried rice (because were unhealthy) but they do have a vegetables option. For the entrees we got the kung pao chicken, honey walnut shrimp (extra cost, and mushroom chicken. I think paying extra for the honey walnut shrimp was worth it, as the shrimp was still crunchy and I enjoyed the glazed walnuts that were mixed in.'], ['105853218368004682403_604a661dd863393130a41496', 'We chose the cha cha chicken half chicken that was marinated in mix sauce, and it wasnt spicy. It comes with your choice of two sides, but black beans & rice and plantains are the way to go. For the coconut fried chicken, the pieces were on the smaller side but the coconut chicken batter was crispy and had a robust coconut flavor. The spicy fries were cut potato rounds and werent spicy, but theyre good dipped into the jerk sauce.'], ['105853218368004682403_604e9d7b7ce15821f39750eb', 'Had the laksa with chicken (you can pick the meat) and the egg noodles (you also customize the noodles) (~$18). Its not spicy at all; there is another option of laksa that Anthony Bourdain likes and was described by the waitress as medium spicy.'], ['105853218368004682403_6057277af69c7b1178070351', 'Food - We got some mimosas (its brunch - we had to) which were well-crated and the strawberry on the stick was sweet. My friend also got the cappuccino which she really enjoyed (very light and fluffy but not too sweet). We split the cheese truffle fries for an appetizer and that was certainly a highlight. The fries were so crispy despite being covered in a cheesy truffle sauce. I had the crab Benedict, which came with breakfast potatoes and was made of blue crab. We ended the meal with the pot du creme - highly recommend getting this. It was very smooth, almost like a mousse, and contested with a smattering of coarse sea salt on the top. There were fresh berries that popped in your mouth that accompanied it, and it came in three dollops.'], ['105853218368004682403_604bf91077e81aaed3cc9ae2', 'My sister and I split an order of the gumbo, which was a bit lacking in the chicken and more heavy on the oysters. The fried chicken sandwich wasnt anything to write home about. The fried seafood platter was pretty big and can easily be shared by two people.'], ['105853218368004682403_604650cc882f4d1caf5feecc', 'She said the chicken paitan was one of the most popular choices and has a rich broth, so I went with that option. The noodles were thinner than I thought they would be (like a miswa texture) but chewy. The chicken was shredded and there wasnt a lot, but there was a good amount of broth. My friend ordered the spicy ramen, which the waitress cautioned was spicy, but it wasnt actually spicy according to my friend. Overall its a decent ramen place, but there are other good options in NYC.'], ['105853218368004682403_60415f44c6fcf1fddba13088', 'We split a single cheeseburger and the crispy fries. The burger was good and came with two patties (~$15) plus cheese. The crispy fries were good too but I wasnt a fan of the cheese sauce - there wasnt really flavorful and I preferred the garlic aioli sauce.'], ['105853218368004682403_605404377fec92c07c643e3c', 'My favorite is the fried chicken sandwich on Thursdays. The chicken is moist on the inside but perfectly crunch on the outside and complemented by the coleslaw accompaniment. On this visit, we tried the ahi tuna burger which was cooked rare and was so very good. I liked the brioche bun and there was a slight level of spiciness that went well with the pickle provided.'], ['105853218368004682403_6045d7d03ed2666ae7ac1ea5', 'Gourmet doughnut shop with coffee. Its definitely pricey (about $3-6 for a doughnut) but well get a box for birthdays. The pumpkin spice latte was straightforward but the doughnuts are the star of the show. If youre feeling particularly hungry, Id recommend getting the basil egg Benedict which is a savory breakfast item (~$6) that has a warm, runny egg inside a soft, malasada type bread. For those with a sweet tooth, you really cant go wrong with any of the doughnuts.'], ['105853218368004682403_604c059977e81aaed3cc9b58', 'Popular ramen and tsukumen (dipping ramen) spot on Sawtelle. The tsukumen options just vary in toppings, but the broth and noodles are the same. You are able to specify medium or large noodles, but note that the medium is already very filling. It was about a 25 minute wait, but the perfectly cooked noodles are so wonderfully chewy its okay to wait.'], ['105853218368004682403_6043493eb81264dfa846b11d', 'Burgers and freak shakes (those really heavy milkshakes) can be found here. We split a Greg Norman cheeseburger (its hard to resist wagyu) (~$20) and a Brooklyn Blackout shake (~$15)The shake came out first, and it was massive. Be careful when you try to take the brownie out because it almost completely fell to the table when we tried to take a bite, so we ended up just putting them on a plate and eating it alongside the shake. The shake is super thick, and we mostly just ate it like it was regular ice cream. I thought the brownie was a bit dry, but I really liked scraping the chocolate chips with the Nutella from the side of the glass. The burger was large and already cut in half so it was easy to split - a solid burger, and we did like having it medium rare. The fries were more thickly cut and came with ketchup on the side.'], ['105853218368004682403_604b6eb577e81aaed3cc9456', 'The pork belly had a different type of kimchi that tasted more smoky, and also had two different sauces. We had a bowl of rice to share, and it was good to offset the fattiness of the pork.'], ['105853218368004682403_6056dcdd3019cb0a47838ec7', 'I ordered a beef shawarma and it was well-seasoned but some might find there to be a lot of cumin. The lamb inside the kebab wrap was a bit tough but had good flavor. The baklava ($1.99) was small but sweet, and they have pistachio available!'], ['105853218368004682403_604935bb55041a127f88a880', 'Even the free cheese bread (that came in a little cute bag) tasted amazing. Bucatini: Noodles were cooked al dente and when you mix in the uni, you get an interesting mix of Italian and Japanese flavors. Cavatelli: My favorite dish - the pasta was perfectly squishy and the pork sugo was well seasoned with Calabrian chilis. Parker rolls: Yes its $6 for bread, but its worth it. The rolls are so soft and chewy, and we fought over the last bits of date butter that came with it. Liberty duck: The best way to describe it would be if you combined the crispy skin of Peking duck with the meat of holiday ham, nestled next to wild rice pilaf with a sweet XO sauce. Wild boar: Definitely not a boar-ing dish. The meat was tender and the gnocchi mixed with greens dripping in a mustard jus was interesting but comforting.'], ['105853218368004682403_60415cb47cd8bf1303624fe4', 'Its a little bakery/cafe located in Greektown that we came across after lunch, so we decided to stop by for coffee and dessert. The woman working behind the counter was very funny - when I asked her what the best pastry was, she said they all were. Theres traditional Greek desserts like baklavas the size of my palm and other pastries like cakes and tarts. We ended up getting the strawberry shortcake and a walnut baklava. The barista there was also very funny and asked a lot of questions to make sure we got the flavor we wanted from our iced Greek coffees (I got sweet with milk, my friend got black). The strawberry shortcake was light and fluffy, and had real strawberry pieces inside. There was a fair amount of white frosting but it wasnt overly sweet. It was sweetened with a generous portion of honey and the crushed walnuts lent such a lovely texture against the phyllo dough. The bill was ~$23 for the two frappes and two desserts. Its authentic, family-owned, the desserts are delicious, and the coffee is strong - what more do you want?'], ['105853218368004682403_60544e9580c04bd7072f24bc', 'Every time I have a friend in town I always take them to Pie Hole to share the delights of the Mexican Chocolate pie. The crust is perfectly crumbly and complements the filling so well. You can share with one or two other people, or you could also just enjoy a slice on your own if you feel up to the task ($6). You can order whole pies in advance for about $40 I believe. I have also tried the Earl Grey pie, pumpkin pie, and chess pie, but my heart belongs to the Mexican chocolate pie. The place is family-run and they have locations in Hollywood and Venice, but I like the Arts District one the best since I think it has the most character. Order the Mexican chocolate pie.'], ['105853218368004682403_6048911af9e05764f1fa564f', 'They specialize in fish tacos, and are definitely among one of the best places to get fish tacos in the LA area. The fish tacos are huge - two is enough for a dinner. The crispiness of the fish against the chopped tomatoes & onions the perfect match. The salsa is deep and husky, and with a squirt of fresh lime, each bite is a little piece of utter bliss. The shrimp ceviche was also good, although the one at Marisco Jalisco is still my favorite.'], ['105853218368004682403_6051ab53c53d98b3eace1c79', 'My go-to is the salmon bowl ($15) which has brown rice, salmon cooked medium rare, a salad, and corn medley that I really enjoy along with cotija cheese. The vegan brownie is surprisingly good and has bits of peanut brittle that add a bit more interesting texture to an otherwise very soft brownie ($4). I also love the chocolate chip cookies - I think theyre some of the best and I love it whenever our office caters tender greens (TG as its affectionately known) and theres leftover chocolate chip cookies to munch on. Theyre the size of my palm and have big round chunks of chocolate embedded throughout. Depending on the batch, they can either be pretty crispy but I like them best when theyre slight chewy. Another favorite of mine is the buttermilk fried chicken - its not as heavy as you think and you could always get it in a salad. The salt and pepper chicken is also a solid bet if you want to get it in a salad or plate. You order at the cash register and move down the line sideways, then you have the option of getting drinks and dessert. The kombucha is $5 and its tall glass of pink fizziness. Green juice is $3.5 and is decent. Theres also wine for $7 if youre looking to have some alcohol. The blueberry dessert is really moist and light.'], ['105853218368004682403_604317cdcc4f7990c65781e7', 'For three girls, we split two appetizers - the nachos and the fries with cheddar cheese and bacon. The nachos were surprisingly spicier than I thought they would be, and they had a generous portion of guacamole. For the fries, we opted not to get the one with the chili since we had already gotten chili exposure with the nachos, so we got the chives and bacon one.'], ['105853218368004682403_6053b83e4b7f30a9c0a50adf', 'The onion rings and fries were standard. My chicken and waffles were good but I prefer the fried chicken at the Misfit.'], ['105853218368004682403_60497bd6b1a0aaee3eefaf3a', 'We got the artichoke crab cake ($15) which was my favorite dish. The buffalo cauliflower had a nice crisp ones around it and good amount of buffalo sauce. I got the boujee pep pizza ($17) for my entree but only ate two slices because it was pretty full from the apps alone. The pizza is vegan and has vegan soppresata which was really thin and crispy and looked like big brown pepperonis. Thin crust and made for good leftovers (I suggest heating it up one slice at a time for 30 seconds so it doesnt get too hard).']]

review_text: We had a variety of dishes, but everyone agreed the pizza was the best. I ordered the mussels.
history_reviews: [['117594715851042192940_6050ce8fd8c08f462b93e02b', 'Great sushi spot. The fish was as fresh as possible for a landlocked area and obviously prepared with care. If you are looking for great sushi that is also affordable (for sushi that is), then this place is a must go.'], ['117594715851042192940_60570da4d2ad6b7a67e27f52', 'Burgers were great, but everything else just okay and fries forgettable. I had the turkey burger which was delicious. DH has the portobello burger which he also thoroughly enjoyed. I also ordered the elote as I know he likes elote. I enjoyed this elote which was really more of a creamed corn with a little spice on top. Its not inexpensive, but its a good quality, extremely juicy burger.'], ['117594715851042192940_60564c2297d555cc6fb0d1fb', 'Some staples we love to order: goat cheese fondue (cant skip), mussels, chicken and cheese melt. Recently tried the short rib with rutabaga mash for the first timeabsolutely sublime. The cocktails are also amazing.'], ['117594715851042192940_604f6c8c88c7af3f893e64bb', 'I had the garden omelet.'], ['117594715851042192940_605309d55266728eda27ab45', 'I had the pitch black gin cocktail. My favorite thing of the night was the whole duck we shared as a table.'], ['117594715851042192940_60569647f69c7b11780700b2', 'I ordered the grilled onion and Swiss chicken sandwich. The bun was great, and you cant go wrong with grilled onions. Which brings me to the turkey burger my husband ordered. Not sure if they need to try a marinade for it or just not over cook it. I would even go as far as to suggest management take a trip to Twisted Root where one may find and awesomely juicy turkey burger. Id recommend a full burger for 8-10+ depending on their general appetite.'], ['117594715851042192940_604de2ae77e81aaed3ccab95', 'The pancakes were honestly meh. I didnt love the corn bread but I prefer a sweet cornbread which this wasnt. My trout was delicious and buttery. But two filets and three sides is a ton. But the green beans were delicious as were the mashed potatoes with brown gravy. My H had the fried chicken which was top notchespecially the white meat.'], ['117594715851042192940_6051e15e88c7af3f893e72fe', 'My only complaint was the shrimp that came with my steak and shrimp was a bit rubbery. My steak, however, was cooked to a perfect med-rare and was tender and juicy. I also enjoyed the vegetable gnocchi side I chose. But the Brussels sprouts were delicious. I also enjoyed the baked Brie appetizer. My husband also enjoyed his steak and it was cooked perfectly as well. The cocktail I had (a gin one, forgot the name) was quite delicious as well. review_text: For appetizers, we had the Chef PB & J, fried deviled eggs and braised pork belly. We also had the king crab & avocado stack which is on their raw bar menu. First, the Chef PB&J was so good. It's pate with a kind of nutty flavor and slight jam served over a crispy slice of baguette. The fried deviled eggs were also very good. Braised pork belly was only so so. The king crab and avocado stack was very refreshing and light. For my meal, I had the 18 oz bone in filet mignon medium rare. The steak came out perfectly cooked and so tender. 18 oz is HUGE so I think the price of $63 was relatively fair for a high end steak restaurant. If you think about it, most steak restaurants serve 6-8 oz sirloins for probably 10-15$ and this steak is a better cut of meat, was cooked professionally, is more delectable and is 3 times the size of the average steak. We ordered the Alaskan king crab and rock shrimp mac and cheese, potato au gratin, roasted sweet potatoes and brussel sprouts for the sides. Brussel sprouts were very good (though I wish they were a little more crisp). The sweet potatoes though- WOW. I'm not a huge sweet potato marshmallows on top person, but these potatoes were so uniquely done, so intricate almost like a dessert. For dessert, we had the grilled banana split and smores in a jar. The grilled banana split was not especially unique. I didn't really taste the grill on the banana. Any grill that occurred was only evident as the banana was brown (like an over ripened appearance). The smores in a jar was ok. I almost wish they roasted the marshmallow on top just a little more. What a delightful meal and worth a visit if you love steak!

We split a Greg Norman cheeseburger (its hard to resist wagyu) (~$20) and a Brooklyn Blackout shake (~$15)The shake came out first, and it was massive. Be careful when you try to take the brownie out because it almost completely fell to the table when we tried to take a bite, so we ended up just putting them on a plate and eating it alongside the shake. We had a bowl of rice to share, and it was good to offset the fattiness of the pork.'], ['105853218368004682403_6056dcdd3019cb0a47838ec7', 'I ordered a beef shawarma and it was well-seasoned but some might find there to be a lot of cumin. The lamb inside the kebab wrap was a bit tough but had good flavor. The baklava ($1.99) was small but sweet, and they have pistachio available!'], ['105853218368004682403_604935bb55041a127f88a880', 'Even the free cheese bread (that came in a little cute bag) tasted amazing. Bucatini: Noodles were cooked al dente and when you mix in the uni, you get an interesting mix of Italian and Japanese flavors. Cavatelli: My favorite dish - the pasta was perfectly squishy and the pork sugo was well seasoned with Calabrian chilis. Parker rolls: Yes its $6 for bread, but its worth it. The rolls are so soft and chewy, and we fought over the last bits of date butter that came with it. Liberty duck: The best way to describe it would be if you combined the crispy skin of Peking duck with the meat of holiday ham, nestled next to wild rice pilaf with a sweet XO sauce. Wild boar: Definitely not a boar-ing dish. The meat was tender and the gnocchi mixed with greens dripping in a mustard jus was interesting but comforting.'], ['105853218368004682403_60415cb47cd8bf1303624fe4', 'Its a little bakery/cafe located in Greektown that we came across after lunch, so we decided to stop by for coffee and dessert. The woman working behind the counter was very funny - when I asked her what the best pastry was, she said they all were. Theres traditional Greek desserts like baklavas the size of my palm and other pastries like cakes and tarts. We ended up getting the strawberry shortcake and a walnut baklava. The barista there was also very funny and asked a lot of questions to make sure we got the flavor we wanted from our iced Greek coffees (I got sweet with milk, my friend got black). The strawberry shortcake was light and fluffy, and had real strawberry pieces inside. There was a fair amount of white frosting but it wasnt overly sweet. It was sweetened with a generous portion of honey and the crushed walnuts lent such a lovely texture against the phyllo dough. The bill was ~$23 for the two frappes and two desserts. Its authentic, family-owned, the desserts are delicious, and the coffee is strong - what more do you want?'], ['105853218368004682403_60544e9580c04bd7072f24bc', 'Every time I have a friend in town I always take them to Pie Hole to share the delights of the Mexican Chocolate pie. The crust is perfectly crumbly and complements the filling so well. You can share with one or two other people, or you could also just enjoy a slice on your own if you feel up to the task ($6). You can order whole pies in advance for about $40 I believe. I have also tried the Earl Grey pie, pumpkin pie, and chess pie, but my heart belongs to the Mexican chocolate pie. The place is family-run and they have locations in Hollywood and Venice, but I like the Arts District one the best since I think it has the most character. Order the Mexican chocolate pie.'], ['105853218368004682403_6048911af9e05764f1fa564f', 'They specialize in fish tacos, and are definitely among one of the best places to get fish tacos in the LA area. The fish tacos are huge - two is enough for a dinner. The crispiness of the fish against the chopped tomatoes & onions the perfect match. The salsa is deep and husky, and with a squirt of fresh lime, each bite is a little piece of utter bliss. The shrimp ceviche was also good, although the one at Marisco Jalisco is still my favorite.'], ['105853218368004682403_6051ab53c53d98b3eace1c79', 'My go-to is the salmon bowl ($15) which has brown rice, salmon cooked medium rare, a salad, and corn medley that I really enjoy along with cotija cheese. The vegan brownie is surprisingly good and has bits of peanut brittle that add a bit more interesting texture to an otherwise very soft brownie ($4). I also love the chocolate chip cookies - I think theyre some of the best and I love it whenever our office caters tender greens (TG as its affectionately known) and theres leftover chocolate chip cookies to munch on. Theyre the size of my palm and have big round chunks of chocolate embedded throughout. Depending on the batch, they can either be pretty crispy but I like them best when theyre slight chewy. Another favorite of mine is the buttermilk fried chicken - its not as heavy as you think and you could always get it in a salad. The salt and pepper chicken is also a solid bet if you want to get it in a salad or plate. You order at the cash register and move down the line sideways, then you have the option of getting drinks and dessert. The kombucha is $5 and its tall glass of pink fizziness. review_text: For two people, we were recommended to get 5-6 dishes (though I think 4 would have been satisfactory), and got the brioche buns, green beans, salmon poke, pig face, pork shank, and two drinks. We loved the mezcaliforniacation and peachfuzz drinks, and our favorite dish of the night was the poke, which had a great mix of fresh salmon, strawberries, avocado, and a sesame-nuttiness to it.
history_reviews: [['107548322316470513394_60415a40c6fcf1fddba12e25', 'While browsing the menu, we were served some spicy picked cabbage which definitely had quite a kick to it. We got the Szechuan wontons, fish fillet in black bean sauce, and napa cabbage in wine sauce. All our food came out at once, and I really liked everything, but wished the wontons were spicier.'], ['107548322316470513394_6043932a8be5d4454df9db04', 'Their sangrias are TO DIE FOR!! Some other highly recommended dishes: buttermilk fried chicken, octopus a la plancha, hanger steak, short rib, bruschetta, and paella. I have yet to have a better paella dish in Chicago.'], ['107548322316470513394_60415df32e57ebdea29c3c0c', "I was so surprised by how much I liked my experience at Prosecco! We got Salsiccia (grilled Italian sausage), Tartufate (orecchiette, cremini, asparagus, sun-dried tomatoes, black truffle cream, Grana Padano, white truffle oil), and a farfalle pasta special that had smoked and fresh salmon. The sausage had good flavor and wasn't too salty, and the pastas were cooked perfectly al dente. We were surprised by how filling the portions were, both the antipasti and pastas. There was a ton of salmon in the farfalle special, and the Tartufate really hit the truffle-flavor craving I had without being too greasy or creamy."], ['107548322316470513394_604158cfc6fcf1fddba12da2', 'Every "classic" Chinese dish is super solid here, including the spicy beef noodles (not really spicy but noodles are super chewy), soup dumplings, mapo tofu, green beans, etc. One thing you MUST GET is the eggplant in garlic sauce. Best eggplant I\'ve ever had.'], ['107548322316470513394_604157bd7cd8bf1303624c81', "The Peking duck dinner is really the only thing you should be coming for, because they roast a spectacular duck here and I haven't had better in the city. The rest of the food on the menu is just okay--Chinatown has better. For four people, one duck dinner is just about enough, which comes with a large plate of sliced duck, six bao buns, a plate of fried rice, and a large bowl of soup. I'd recommend ordering extra buns since the meat will definitely outnumber the pieces of buns that you have, and a vegetable dish for health. The server brings out the roasted duck whole, and will carve/slice it table-side. It's always a spectacle to watch, and the meat is always super juicy, fatty, and crispy, all in one bite. The fried rice and soup are average, but complements the duck meat nicely. If you have five or more people in your group, it'd be a good idea to get two ducks. Sometimes near the end of the day they run out of ducks which is just about the saddest thing the waiter can tell you after you've been seated."], ['107548322316470513394_60415b797dfa7f1871835f97', 'Compared with other Chinatown dim sum restaurants, everything just tastes more flavorful and larger portions, albeit with slightly higher prices (avg $15 per person). They put real shrimp in the har gow (not paste) and theres like 4 shrimp in each dumpling. The siu mai is ginormous as well and filled with whole shrimp. My favorite dim sum here are the beef short ribs and the pineapple bun custard buns that literally explode with that sweet, gooey filling every single time.'], ['107548322316470513394_6046e75705aec66848d1c66f', "Usually you're only able to do half pies of the classics (margherita, marinara, white, calzone), but we asked if we could do two half pies of the margherita and the no. Between two people a medium size was plenty, and you could definitely taste the freshness of the ingredients and the handiwork of the dough."], ['107548322316470513394_604ad57db1a0aaee3eefbead', "The quality of the food isn't as good as many other Indian restaurants but you're bound to be stuffed at the end of your meal. My favorite dish here is the lamb curry, and I like the butter chicken as well, but the chicken in it tends to be a bit dry. The parathas are a nice side order as they are humongous. The mango lassi isn't as mango-y as I would like, but again, I have no complaints based on how large the portions are and how cheap the food is."], ['107548322316470513394_60415fe17cd8bf130362511a', "Brunch is Asian inspired, and I've tried their Vietnamese iced coffee, corn elotes, pandan French toast, and catfish banh mi. As a fan of sweet and creamy treats, the coffee and French toast are must-gets!"], ['107548322316470513394_6050539bd2f0452c8736d412', 'After we were seated, we ordered the fried cod and shrimp tacos (this was where we made the mistake--should have just gotten the lobster roll). The cod came with fries and some coleslaw. Fish was fried well but so greasy and almost dripping with oil. I barely wanted to eat it and ended up peeling off the fried skin and just ate the fish inside. The fries and slaw were great though. The fried shrimp tacos were pretty big, but the shrimp was soggy and suuuper salty. The tortilla was very soggy as well, so I ended up just eating everything in the taco with a fork. The tacos also came with a bag of chips but we already felt so greased up by the fish that we ended up not opening the bag up.'], ['107548322316470513394_605082cdc53d98b3eace1645', 'We got a root beer float, Rubins Reubin sandwich, and a mac and cheese.'], ['107548322316470513394_60502a0e9755094ba8abe8c9', 'They serve the bread with this garlic olive oil and vinegar, and it was just sublime. For entrees, we got the angel hair aglio e olio, and the penne with chicken, mozzarella, and tomato cream, and a side of the sweet corn. The sweet corn was surprisingly good, it was popping with flavor and buttery goodness. The two pastas were great contrasts, but we didnt find either to be particularly strong-flavored.'], ['107548322316470513394_60415e4f2e57ebdea29c3c2a', "I'd especially recommend the lamb kefta, short rib shakshuka, and khachapuri, which was kind of like pizza but on puff pastry. The dark chocolate babka that we got was dry and hard, although the filling was soo good."], ['107548322316470513394_60415cfc7cd8bf1303624ffc', "Nonna's meatballs, bucatini, and the chocolate cake. The meatballs are a great dish to share, and and perfectly tender and juicy. The bucatini is definitely one of my favorite pasta dishes. The noodles are cooked to perfection, and the sauce and toppings are simple but strong in flavor. As with the other pasta dishes, you can get a half order instead of a full order, which is what I got, and I still left feeling very full. The chocolate cake is TO DIE FOR!!! It is quite literally the best slice of cake I have ever had. There are so many layers to this cake, and each layer showcases a different texture of chocolate, so there's crispiness in it, ganache, cream, sponge cake, and so on."], ['107548322316470513394_60415e8d7cd8bf13036250e4', "Firecakes is my favorite donut shop in Chicago. The prices are reasonable and hard the beat, and the quality of their donuts are just amazing. The donuts are humongous and it really doesn't get any better than this. These are miles better than the cake donuts (although those are pretty good too). I also love their filled donuts. I'm not usually a big fan of coffee or chocolate flavors, but their valrhona chocolate and espresso donut is particularly scrumptious. I don't think the ice cream donuts are particularly special, but they do make for a delicious treat to share."], ['107548322316470513394_604159ca2e57ebdea29c39a3', "Love the ramen, and everything else here!!! The tonkotsu ramen is one of the best around, and you're in for a treat if you like a fatty cha siu pork belly. I think they give you a nice portion of meat with the noodles. The fried chicken and kimchi ramen tastes exactly what it sounds like. The bowls are usually big enough for me but my bf likes to get his with extra noodles. I'd recommend the beef over the salmon but both are really good."], ['107548322316470513394_60415d907dfa7f18718360a5', 'We came on a Monday night for the tantanmen ramen/Momo royale burger + beer + shot deal, and definitely plan to come back to try more cocktails and small plates in the future. Personally, I liked the burger a lot more than the ramen, since the bao bun and Japanese sweet potato fries really blew me away, but the ramen was delicious as well.'], ['107548322316470513394_6050fbf5da79151bfc1255e4', "Brought my family from out of town here after my friends recommended Lou's for a great deep dish experience. We got a Caesar salad to share, the trio of dips and pizza chips, and the Lou medium pizza for three of us to share. The salad was great and just the perfect appetizer. The chips were an indulgent sharing platter as well, but the dips were extremely greasy. The pizza was both what I expected and not. Our pizza was about 1/3 inch thick with toppings and all. Also, I'm not sure if because this pizza only had veggies, but the toppings seemed very watery. Nonetheless, this was pizza so it couldn't go wrong, and the crust was cooked through on the bottom and nice and crispy on the edges. Overall, we had a great time, didn't feel like the wait was long, and left feeling so full with half a pizza in hand."], ['107548322316470513394_604162797dfa7f18718362f0', 'The waiter mentioned the food is served family style, but we ended up getting individual entrees and shared the caramelized waffle dish. review_text: Started with fried calamari cooked perfectly and then fried oysters nicely done although 8 are weren't enough! It was filled with crab, shrimp and pieces of lobster; two stuffed flounder filets come with dinner. The grouper bisque was nice and allowed the flavor of the fish come through without being over spiced. The other dish was New Orleans style shrimp and grits. history_reviews: [['115610078984514634239_604fdef484d95314a9e43757', 'The good: the seafood rolls were fantastic with crunch on the outside and soft in the middle with great taste yet mild; the crab fritters were awesome much the same on the outside yet sweet and full of flavor fulfilling the promise of coastal crab. Two guests both had the grilled mahi, one served with fried green tomatoes and the other with cheese grits. Both loved the mahi that was cooked perfectly; flavorful and tender. Fried green tomatoes were not mushy and his favorite but the cheesy grits could have been a little more cheesy (or buttery). I had the fried seafood combination with option to have the scallops grilled which was pleasantly suprising. The flounder was great, tender and fried just right. The oysters were full of flavor but a tad overcooked IMO but still good and the scallops cooked perfectly. Scallops cut easily in half and not rubbery at all.....perfect!!!'], ['115610078984514634239_60471d5bb0e2129e47535c69', 'The fish was cooked perfectly and atmosphere was outstanding.'], ['115610078984514634239_6053739188c7af3f893e7b69', "We both had Bloody Mary which is very good and above standard and our appetizer was the calamari. It was cooked perfectly neither overcooked or over breaded. We ordered crab cakes and a fish and oyster combo. The crab cakes were delicious with a little breading and the combo tight was just the right amount. I ordered oysters with flounder and both were cooked perfectly! If you're trying to avoid the seafood buffets that overpriced with low-quality food this is a recommendation that you will not regret."], ['115610078984514634239_6052c3f088c7af3f893e7747', 'Okay I enjoyed the atmosphere and the best Bloody Mary I probably have ever drank and almost forgot to capture pictures of the plates! Our server was pleasant and very attentive and I will say again I had several of the best Bloody Marys! Salad was fresh and I went 4 one of the burger dishes.'], ['115610078984514634239_6055c1bef69c7b117806fcf8', 'Fried pickles are spears and not chips and enjoyed by all. The calamari was good, medium portion with medium to small rings but they included the tentacles which are the most tender! The grilled mahi salad was awesome. The lobster roll was not liked by my older guest; he said it was bland. The hush puppies nice and crispy with a hint of sweet but it would have been nice to have seen them bigger or more for the price of the appetizer. The Grouper basket was the special of the day (fried) and my guest liked it. I had the fish basket of cod, two thick fillets served with fries only, I liked it. Our first visit we took advantage of what their overall specialty is; peel and eat shrimp, broiled crab legs, clams and oysters. Their oyster shooter selection is impressive! The food was broiled correctly so the shells peeled off easily and crab legs snapped when cracked. They have a great selection of heat on each table and buckets hole\'ed in the middle of the table for shells. NOTE to seafood newbies or folks from Ohio, shrimp shells that stick and hard to peel are overcooked, reheated or old and crab legs that dont "snap" are the same...so this place can be considered one of the higher rated seafood restaurants in the area but my three star is for the (possible frozen ) shipped in seafood.']]

history_reviews: [['107548322316470513394_60415a40c6fcf1fddba12e25', 'While browsing the menu, we were served some spicy picked cabbage which definitely had quite a kick to it. We got Salsiccia (grilled Italian sausage), Tartufate (orecchiette, cremini, asparagus, sun-dried tomatoes, black truffle cream, Grana Padano, white truffle oil), and a farfalle pasta special that had smoked and fresh salmon. Best eggplant I\'ve ever had.'], ['107548322316470513394_604157bd7cd8bf1303624c81', "The Peking duck dinner is really the only thing you should be coming for, because they roast a spectacular duck here and I haven't had better in the city. The rest of the food on the menu is just okay--Chinatown has better. For four people, one duck dinner is just about enough, which comes with a large plate of sliced duck, six bao buns, a plate of fried rice, and a large bowl of soup. I'd recommend ordering extra buns since the meat will definitely outnumber the pieces of buns that you have, and a vegetable dish for health. The server brings out the roasted duck whole, and will carve/slice it table-side. It's always a spectacle to watch, and the meat is always super juicy, fatty, and crispy, all in one bite. The fried rice and soup are average, but complements the duck meat nicely. If you have five or more people in your group, it'd be a good idea to get two ducks. Sometimes near the end of the day they run out of ducks which is just about the saddest thing the waiter can tell you after you've been seated."], ['107548322316470513394_60415b797dfa7f1871835f97', 'Compared with other Chinatown dim sum restaurants, everything just tastes more flavorful and larger portions, albeit with slightly higher prices (avg $15 per person). They put real shrimp in the har gow (not paste) and theres like 4 shrimp in each dumpling. The siu mai is ginormous as well and filled with whole shrimp. My favorite dim sum here are the beef short ribs and the pineapple bun custard buns that literally explode with that sweet, gooey filling every single time.'], ['107548322316470513394_6046e75705aec66848d1c66f', "Usually you're only able to do half pies of the classics (margherita, marinara, white, calzone), but we asked if we could do two half pies of the margherita and the no. The mango lassi isn't as mango-y as I would like, but again, I have no complaints based on how large the portions are and how cheap the food is."], ['107548322316470513394_60415fe17cd8bf130362511a', "Brunch is Asian inspired, and I've tried their Vietnamese iced coffee, corn elotes, pandan French toast, and catfish banh mi. Mexican Coke was $2.95 and the burgers ranged from ~$13 to $16. The veggie burger was better than I expected and comes with two toppings. Bucatini: Noodles were cooked al dente and when you mix in the uni, you get an interesting mix of Italian and Japanese flavors. Cavatelli: My favorite dish - the pasta was perfectly squishy and the pork sugo was well seasoned with Calabrian chilis. Parker rolls: Yes its $6 for bread, but its worth it. Liberty duck: The best way to describe it would be if you combined the crispy skin of Peking duck with the meat of holiday ham, nestled next to wild rice pilaf with a sweet XO sauce. Wild boar: Definitely not a boar-ing dish. The meat was tender and the gnocchi mixed with greens dripping in a mustard jus was interesting but comforting.'], ['105853218368004682403_60415cb47cd8bf1303624fe4', 'Its a little bakery/cafe located in Greektown that we came across after lunch, so we decided to stop by for coffee and dessert. The woman working behind the counter was very funny - when I asked her what the best pastry was, she said they all were. The barista there was also very funny and asked a lot of questions to make sure we got the flavor we wanted from our iced Greek coffees (I got sweet with milk, my friend got black). The strawberry shortcake was light and fluffy, and had real strawberry pieces inside. There was a fair amount of white frosting but it wasnt overly sweet. It was sweetened with a generous portion of honey and the crushed walnuts lent such a lovely texture against the phyllo dough. The bill was ~$23 for the two frappes and two desserts. Its authentic, family-owned, the desserts are delicious, and the coffee is strong - what more do you want?'], ['105853218368004682403_60544e9580c04bd7072f24bc', 'Every time I have a friend in town I always take them to Pie Hole to share the delights of the Mexican Chocolate pie. You can order whole pies in advance for about $40 I believe. I have also tried the Earl Grey pie, pumpkin pie, and chess pie, but my heart belongs to the Mexican chocolate pie. The place is family-run and they have locations in Hollywood and Venice, but I like the Arts District one the best since I think it has the most character. Order the Mexican chocolate pie.'], ['105853218368004682403_6048911af9e05764f1fa564f', 'They specialize in fish tacos, and are definitely among one of the best places to get fish tacos in the LA area. The fish tacos are huge - two is enough for a dinner. The crispiness of the fish against the chopped tomatoes & onions the perfect match. The salsa is deep and husky, and with a squirt of fresh lime, each bite is a little piece of utter bliss. The shrimp ceviche was also good, although the one at Marisco Jalisco is still my favorite.'], ['105853218368004682403_6051ab53c53d98b3eace1c79', 'My go-to is the salmon bowl ($15) which has brown rice, salmon cooked medium rare, a salad, and corn medley that I really enjoy along with cotija cheese. I also love the chocolate chip cookies - I think theyre some of the best and I love it whenever our office caters tender greens (TG as its affectionately known) and theres leftover chocolate chip cookies to munch on. Theyre the size of my palm and have big round chunks of chocolate embedded throughout. Depending on the batch, they can either be pretty crispy but I like them best when theyre slight chewy. Another favorite of mine is the buttermilk fried chicken - its not as heavy as you think and you could always get it in a salad. The salt and pepper chicken is also a solid bet if you want to get it in a salad or plate. You order at the cash register and move down the line sideways, then you have the option of getting drinks and dessert. The kombucha is $5 and its tall glass of pink fizziness. Green juice is $3.5 and is decent. Theres also wine for $7 if youre looking to have some alcohol. The blueberry dessert is really moist and light.'], ['105853218368004682403_604317cdcc4f7990c65781e7', 'For three girls, we split two appetizers - the nachos and the fries with cheddar cheese and bacon. My chicken and waffles were good but I prefer the fried chicken at the Misfit.'], ['105853218368004682403_60497bd6b1a0aaee3eefaf3a', 'We got the artichoke crab cake ($15) which was my favorite dish. I got the boujee pep pizza ($17) for my entree but only ate two slices because it was pretty full from the apps alone. The pizza is vegan and has vegan soppresata which was really thin and crispy and looked like big brown pepperonis. Thin crust and made for good leftovers (I suggest heating it up one slice at a time for 30 seconds so it doesnt get too hard).']]
