review_text: I came here seeking the Korean Fried Chicken and the Panko-Crusted Japanese Fried Chicken. Both were boneless, sufficiently moist, and tasty. The Korean variant had been subjected to a char-sui/teriyaki-like magenta glaze before deep-frying, resulting in a piece of chicken tinged in a pleasant sweetness that didn't really need any saucing. Nonetheless, I enjoyed the sweet soy-infused katsu sauce, but didn't care as much for the lava sauce, which tasted like sweet and sour ketchup and, despite its name, didn't actually deliver any heat. Macaroni Salad is delicious -- much moreso than the Green Salad which is overpowered by an aggressively dark sesame-flavored dressing. The Malasadas (Portuguese fried dough) are also legit here, a great way to end your meal, even if they're not the larger, thinner variety I grew up with.
history_reviews: [['108685370139018629938_6051f93188c7af3f893e7394', "I ordered the 2 piece Chicken Meal with Mashed Potatoes ($6.95) with a pint of beer. Beyond the dryness, the chicken had an extremely salty, thin crust. The thin texture of the fried batter was similar to KFC's Original Recipe. Make no mistake though, the Colonel is like Escoffier next to Chicken Charlie. I haven't yet mentioned the mashed potatoes and gravy, WHICH WERE MADE WITH SPOILED DAIRY AND TASTED RANCID!"], ['108685370139018629938_6055afe397d555cc6fb0ce6f', "One of San Diego's finest taco shops. Try the carnitas here. Cabeza tacos are also excellent."], ['108685370139018629938_6045b409604fc398f591ecf7', 'The pork burrito is great, consisting of shredded pork stewed in spices accompanied by cotija cheese and lettuce, wrapped in a homemade lard-heavy flour tortilla. The gloriously greasy rolled tacos are also a good choice, featuring meat in a crispy rolled tortilla shell, deep fried, and then smothered with queso fresco and crema.'], ['108685370139018629938_60421d502e57ebdea29c81eb', 'Yes, it\'s a real good burger, think "In-N-Out Burger on Steroids" - but Hodad\'s kitchen and wait staff, mostly stoned out of their ever-loving skulls, operate on "beach time." This slo-mo style doesn\'t quite scale up to the immense demand for their burgers due to the massive amount of media exposure they\'ve gotten both locally as a long-time beloved San Diego beach staple and nationally on Food Network and other outlets. As for the burgers? I typically order the "Single Bacon Cheeseburger," which is the house specialty if there is one. I sometimes need to compress the burger with my hands a bit before trying to eat it, otherwise I cannot fit enough of it into my mouth to take a proper bite. Like I said, it\'s a real good burger. In fact, this is the quintessential American burger turned up to "11." I usually get my burger with a "basket combo," so that it includes Hodad\'s crispy thick-cut French fries, which are some of my favorite fries in all of San Diego due to their crunchy skin, soft hot innards, and near-perfect amount of seasoning. All everyone talks about are Hodad\'s burgers and shakes, leaving their fries underrated.'], ['108685370139018629938_6046d164b0e2129e475356f6', 'We also both enjoy the "Baja Ceviche," where each ingredient (shrimp, fish, crab) is distinct, but work delectably well together. Perhaps our favorite appetizer is the "Smoked Fish Tacos," essentially smoked fish hash piped into egg-roll-like taco shells. If you\'re looking for something more traditional, try the "Salt and Pepper Calamari." My entre recommendation is the Miso-Glazed Sea Bass with Crab Fried Rice, which is an extraordinary dish that is similar to Nobu\'s Miso-Marinated Black Cod. The flavoring aside, the fish preparation at Truluck\'s is top notch, and the sea bass is moist, firm-fleshed, and cooked to a level where it remains mild and delicate. The crab fried rice is lightly flavored in what I can only describe as "essence" of crab, and complements the sea bass perfectly. If you\'re not ordering the sea bass, then try the "South African Lobster Tail" if it is on the menu. South African lobsters are sweeter than normal lobsters, and here they do all of the work of de-shelling the massive 12 ounce tail, and setting it aside a substantial portion of parmesan mashed potatoes and steamed asparagus.'], ['108685370139018629938_6051045f5b4ccec8d5cae9d5', 'I recommend the mushroom chicken dish first and foremost, though the tamales and the tacos (blackened fish especially) are excellent as well.'], ['108685370139018629938_60489685b3f169c178160577', 'Mitla Caf\'s tacos are the foundation of the Taco Bell empire. As you first bite into one of Mitla Caf\'s Beef Tacos (labeled as just "Taco" on the menu), you can\'t help but think of a Taco Bell\'s taco, except done 100 times better. As grease and juices fall out of the house-made misshapen fried tortilla, you\'ll taste the heavily-browned and spiced ground beef covered with shredded cheddar cheese, refreshing lettuce, and bright red tomatoes, and you will understand why someone would start a fast food company around this. Sometimes it\'s better to be lucky than good, because for as many billions of dollars that the Taco Bell brand is worth, Glen Bell ultimately failed to capture what makes this taco work. Mitla Caf\'s "Shredded Beef Taco" is probably a better taco than their regular "Taco," but it doesn\'t channel the same kind of nostalgia. The "Shredded Beef Taco" does, however, have a cleaner flavor and truer purity of purpose. Either taco greatly benefits from the red sauce (you need to ask for a side of it when you order), a fiery salsa that puts Taco Bell\'s little spicy ketchup packets to shame. During my visit, I also ordered the Pozole, which is served white (i.e. Pozole Blanco), with minimal garnishes (no oregano, for example), and pork that was over-cooked. My advice is to pass on the Pozole and eat more tacos. In fact, always eat more tacos.'], ['108685370139018629938_60561c8d97d555cc6fb0d0f3', 'My visit was short and I dined solo at the bar, eating some nigiri (Otoro and Hamachi) in addition to the Rock Shrimp Tempura.'], ['108685370139018629938_604da44a77e81aaed3cca9df', 'During my first trip here, I ordered the "Crispy Chicken Sandwich." I wish I had more fried chicken like this in my life, but I can\'\'t afford to. Yes, this is one of the best chicken sandwiches I\'ve had anywhere, but is it worth the $18 price tag? I am confident, however, that the juiciness of the chicken, the sturdy and well-seasoned fried batter, the creamy cole slaw, the earthy swiss cheese, and the fresh sesame-coated roll combine to make this almost as perfect as a fried chicken sandwich can be. Lastly, I had the "Honor Burger" on my second visit, which is a burger topped with a condiment mix that reminded me of Burger King\'s Whopper, but produced by a professional cook. The meat, ordered and prepared medium rare, had plenty of life in it and is not entirely overwhelmed by the melted cheddar, mix of slaw, special sauce, and tomatoes, but I feel they could scale down the condiment-to-beef ratio just a tad and have twice as good of a burger.'], ['108685370139018629938_60412b777cd8bf1303623e48', 'Hambone\'s is a popular BBQ joint in Bellflower owned and operated by pitmaster Kenny Hamilton who has come to Los Angeles via Mississippi. What drew me here was that this is one of the restaurants around south Los Angeles that sells what has become known as "black tacos," which refer to tacos sold by black-owned businesses to predominantly black customers. Hambone\'s serves a very basic "black taco" with chopped barbecued meat with sauce on flour tortillas, dressed with lettuce, shredded yellow cheese, and diced tomatoes. I was a bit bummed on account of not being able to taste the difference between the "Pulled Pork Taco" from the "Beef Tri-Tip Taco" due to the BBQ sauce on the meats being so sweet and pervasive that it made both tacos taste the same. My fascination with "black tacos" aside, I could smell Hambone\'s hickory-smoked meats from my car as I entered the parking lot, which put me in a mood to have something more substantial than a taco. I\'m often disappointed in Southern California\'s BBQ restaurants, so I crossed my fingers as I ordered a "Half Rack of Spare Ribs." The ribs were neatly trimmed in a way that made me a little skeptical (in my experience, "pretty BBQ" is usually bad BBQ), but only in the brief moment before I began eating them. I was delighted by a persistent hickory flavor throughout textured, dense pork that cleanly snaps off the bone with a tug of your teeth. My biggest fault is that, like the taco meats, these ribs are heavily sauced with a thin glaze that is sweet and sticky, reminding me of an Asian-style sauce one would eat on the magenta-hued spare ribs found in Cantonese restaurants across America. Don\'t get me wrong, the sauce tastes fine -- I just wish there was less of it and that I had an opportunity to apply it myself. It\'s a shame, because Hamilton is proud of his rub and speaks of if it as his most secret of weapons, but I could not discern where the rub stops and the sauce begins, and the sauce made everything sooooo sweet. I also ordered "Collard Greens" that were flat greens heaped on one other -- again, almost "too neat-looking" for collards -- but nonetheless tender, piquant, filled with pork flavor, and just a touch of acid. On the whole, a pretty good BBQ spot.'], ['108685370139018629938_6049809fb1a0aaee3eefaf8b', 'TJ Oyster Bar is a family-run San Diego mariscos institution that has been in operation since opening up a small restaurant in Bonita in 2002 and subsequently expanding with two additional locations in South Bay. I began my recent visit with their "Aguachile Verde," a traditional preparation of raw shrimp, cucumbers, and red onions cured in lime juice with serrano chiles. The spicy and sour broth would endear itself with Wilbur Scoville and is not to be trifled with -- it will not only clear out your sinuses but melt them down as well. The flavor is off the hook, and I could eat a bowl of just the red onions marinated in this aguachile broth. Save some for your tacos. I give two thumbs (eight arms?) up to the "Octopus Taco," a petite corn tortilla stuffed with grilled chopped tentacle that is slightly sticky and slightly charred, sweet and chewy, but crispy-edged. Despite this stuff being nothing short of creamy heroin, it is wisely applied sparingly on this taco. Cilantro and onions round out a wonderful octopus-forward taco that you\'ll remember for its chunks of meat rather than its garnishments. The "Grilled Fish Taco" is the same as the "Octopus Taco," but with very soft grilled fish instead. If you must do one or the other, go octopus. I suggest adding TJ Oyster Bar\'s salsa roja to these tacos. Like the other tacos served at TJ Oyster Bar, the "Baja Fish Taco" is compact and petite, but it is everything a fish taco ought to be: crunchy beer-battered fried fish, reasonably ratio\'d vegetal accoutrements (cabbage, onion, tomato, cilantro), and the mysterious white sauce. The tortilla could be better, but wherever they source them from do a decent job as packaged tortillas go -- you can taste and smell corn in them, as you should. The last taco I tried was the "Shrimp Taqueso," which is similar to a "taco gobernador" in that it consists of shrimp that have been grilled so their surfaces brown in a corn tortilla with melted cheese. It was alright, kind of a shrimp quesadilla de maiz. This taco needed something else to really "pop," and I would suggest going full-on gobernador-style with sauted veggies, or providing chipotle sauce on the side. The tortilla is grilled to melt the cheese and make the taco sturdier, which I appreciated because I could sense that this gooey filling, combined with gravity, would otherwise be determined to fall all over my shirt. As with the other tacos, using the salsa roja available here is recommended.'], ['108685370139018629938_6041b9cfc6fcf1fddba14afb', 'For me, there is no more interesting "regional" taco in Los Angeles than the "black taco," a type of taco that has been invented and evolved over the past 40+ years in black neighborhoods located within the urban sprawl beginning in South Central Los Angeles and ending in Compton. Black tacos have their own unique distinctive style, look, taste, and nomenclature, yet are not found outside of this micro-region. Don\'t get me wrong, there are different varieties of black tacos, but the basics are a tortilla (usually a white corn tortilla, but flour can be used as well) filled with ground beef or turkey, lots of shredded yellow cheese, lettuce, diced tomatoes, and either sour cream or some kind of sweet barbecue-like "sauce" or both. There are no onions or cilantro in a typical black taco. Sr. Cliff\'s "Turkey Taco" is what I just described, with seasoned clumps of ground turkey that are grilled until they\'re browned and deposited into a soft corn tortilla with tomatoes, cheese, lettuce, and sour cream. Sr. Cliff\'s can also serve their tacos with onions and cilantro on double corn tortillas, eschewing all of the other toppings. I ordered a "Ground Beef Taco" of this variety, and it was exactly what you would expect it to be, though the grilling technique that Sr. Cliff\'s cooks use for their ground meats imparts plenty of flavor due to the thick browning picked up through the process. Nonetheless, these are not much more than the kind of tacos that have made billions of dollars over the past 80 years for General Mills\' "Old El Paso" brand. However, the combination of soul food and Mexican food on the menus of black-owned restaurants continues to evolve black tacos in South L.A. and Compton. The "Soul Man Taco" served at Sr. Cliff\'s uses pastrami in addition to ground beef for its meat, and has similar toppings to their regular black taco, but it also comes with a legit salsa roja on the side that wouldn\'t be out of place in a Boyle Heights taqueria. Indeed, Sr. Cliff\'s "Soul Man Taco" veers towards an intriguing direction for black tacos, using and combining ingredients that one wouldn\'t think to combine in a taco, but make sense due to local culture. Sr. Cliff\'s may not have invented the black taco, nor do they make the best black taco in L.A., but this is probably the best restaurant to go to for understanding what black tacos are, and how they have become essential eats in the communities they can be found in.'], ['108685370139018629938_60458393882f4d1caf5fd86a', 'Like many barbecue restaurants across the country, Phil\'s uses mesquite wood in the preparation of their meat dishes. The ribs, tri-tip, chicken, and pulled pork offered at Phil\'s are not "mesquite smoked," (which requires a unique skill-set, aptitude, patience, and expertise) but rather they are baked in an oven, slathered in sweet sauce to cover up any problems, and then "mesquite grilled." This is a key distinction, because one method is American BBQ, and the other is not. I don\'t know why anyone would go to Phil\'s BBQ more than once. Sticky and dirty silverware, sticky and dirty floors, sticky and dirty table tops. Also, I may like your potato salad more, by the way, if you actually bothered to fully cook the potatoes and apply appropriate seasoning. Your beef ribs would be better if they weren\'t so difficult to bite into with human teeth, and your baby backs would improve if you stopped cooking them past the point of cosmic heat death. I\'d consider not spitting your onion rings into my napkin if they were fried in such a way that the fried coating did not taste and feel like stale cereal. Imma give Phil\'s a decent rating. Take your 3 stars, Phil\'s BBQ.'], ['108685370139018629938_6055f35e97d555cc6fb0cfc5', 'Yes, the Al Pastor Taco from the Ave 26 Taco Stand, on any given day, could be just as good as an Al Pastor Taco from Leo\'s Taco Truck, or my long-time personal favorite down in San Diego, Tacos El Gordo. What could put it over the edge are the grilled onions cooked down until they sweeten and begin to caramelize, then blended with the meat carved from the trompo. You could be completely satisfied  NO, captivated  by a taco filled with ONLY the Al Pastor pork, without any additional sauces or garnishments. However, I recommend the chopped raw onions and cilantro from the salsa bar, and it would be criminal to not add at least a bit of Ave 26\'s rousing salsa roja. It will reinforce to you that you are indeed eating legit "street tacos as opposed to the heavily-garnished crapola fraudulently peddled as "street tacos" on this side of the border.'], ['108685370139018629938_6049ae05d4b3ada4982e7ab2', 'These are outstanding, plump diver scallops that taste as clean as the plate beneath them. The accompaniments change from season-to-season, with my favorite being the vinegar-spiked frise and chorizo salad with roasted fingerling potatoes. But Mrs. K and I prefer to order their "Cheese Plate," which is always satisfying, and consists of a sharp blue cheese, a funky soft cheese (such as camembert), and a piece of hard, nutty cheese with notes of caramel or butterscotch (like an aged gouda or comt).'], ['108685370139018629938_604979f4aaa2b0649c59c08e', 'Burritos La Palma is a tough restaurant for me to review, because they are such a unique operation, and they do a few key things unexpectedly well. Rather than a deep-dive into why this Zacatecan restaurant serves slender burritos that can fit into one\'s palm that many people (myself included) also would consider to be tacos, I\'ll simply leave it at that. Also, I\'ll save the burrito history lesson for another review. And as much as other reviewers and food critics alike want to write about how Burritos La Palma somehow brought beef birria to Southern California, this notion is mistaken and, in fact, not even close to being accurate -- but since I don\'t have a better or more definitive answer, I\'m avoiding that one as well. The first burrito I tried at Burritos La Palma was their "Tinga de Pollo Burrito." The chicken tinga recipe they use here results in a juicy, mildly-spiced tinga that is dominated by pork nectar and smokiness from its chipotle chiles. It is a messy, drippy guisado that demands a strong tortilla. The hand-pressed flour tortillas used at Burritos La Palma are based on a family recipe and are indeed both stout and fantastic: substantial, moist, a little chewy, with a flavor that makes me think "biscuits" not "burritos." The "Birria, Frijoles y Queso Burrito" makes even better use of the tortilla: they lay it on a griddle for a bit to help melt the cheese inside the burrito. The toasted surface creates a different flavor and texture on one side of the burrito, making it distinctively quirky. The feisty beef birria inside is well-spiced and decadently soft. The combination of their beef birria, refried beans, and salty, creamy queso in their half-toasted flour tortilla creates a whole that is superior to the the sum of its parts. I would avoid ordering the "Flautas de Maiz," basically bone-dry taquitos with a small bit of shredded beef and a mild runny green sauce on it. As with many taquitos, the predominant flavor of these flautas was the deep-fried corn tortilla shell. This dish desperately needs more meat and less tortilla. I wanted to throw something when I realized the same restaurant that makes wonderful little burritos was also capable of producing something like this. Burritos La Palma now operates several stores across L.A. county and Orange County, but this location in El Monte is their original restaurant that opened in 2012. Upon completion of my visit here, I found that the hype and praise this operation receives is legitimate, and next time I\'ll solely stick to the burritos, which is what I advise you to do as well.'], ['108685370139018629938_604a46831ec03878d66c834c', 'My first steak here was the classic "Tournedos Rossini": a butter-basted rare filet mignon served on a crouton, topped with seared foie gras, finished with a Madeira demi-glace sauce, and garnished with shaved black truffles. The whole of this is a buttery, well-crusted steak supported by strong complimentary flavors that will leave you wondering why every steakhouse doesn\'t serve this dish. On my second visit, I enjoyed an 8-ounce "Miyazaki A5 New York Strip," a pre-sliced Japanese black wagyu steak that may be the best steak I\'ve eaten in San Diego, with only Provisional\'s Hokkaido A5 challenging it. You can\'t go wrong with Born & Raised\'s "Coal-Roasted Leeks," or the crispy "Charred Broccoli," or especially the baked breadcrumb-covered "Mac & Cheese" with its tangy mix of cheddar and gruyere cheeses. But my favorite side was the half-pound "Butter-Poached Lobster," a pricey but worthwhile indulgence of melted butter riding on the back of expertly cooked, taut lobster tail meat.'], ['108685370139018629938_6056600f3019cb0a47838d06', "Knowing that the restaurant's chef de cuisine, Scott Pajak, is a Buffalo native, I ordered the Signature Stadium Buffalo Wings. Having attended college in western New York, I'm picky when it comes to buffalo wings and consider any wings I've ever eaten on the west coast to be substandard -- until now. Chef Pajak's wings are massive, have an ultra-crispy skin (sans breading, of course), with moist, juicy white meat inside. The sauce was a just a tad sweeter and thinner than most buffalo sauces I remember from the east coast, the heat level was right, and most importantly the sauce tightly clung to the wings. The creamy dipping sauce, made of Point Reyes' award-winning blue cheese and loaded with garlic, was a nice touch. These were certainly the best wings I've had west of the Mississippi River. I somewhat enjoyed the Spicy Meatloaf Po Boy, which featured meatloaf, a spicy ketchup/BBQ sauce, fontina cheese, black pepper mayonnaise, lettuce, pickle, and tomato on a New Orleans-style French bread roll. While not the best meatloaf sandwich I ever had, it had good enough flavor, and made for a satisfying lunch."], ['108685370139018629938_604dacb677e81aaed3ccaa20', 'Guerrilla Taco\'s chicano chef, Wes Avila, is a taquero after my heart, proudly declaring his own food "inauthentic," and having been quoted as saying "I couldn\'t give a sh*t about authenticity, especially when it comes to tacos. The truth is, there\'s no such thing as an authentic taco." The name "Guerrilla Tacos" was the idea of Avila\'s wife, as he was constantly threatened with being shutdown in his early days as a less-than-legal food stand prior to opening this brick and mortar restaurant in the Arts District, now possibly the most well-known and critically-acclaimed taqueria in the city of Los Angeles. Between the "Grilled Steak Taco" here, Salazar\'s "Carne Asada Taco," and the "Arrachera Taco" at Taco Mara, Southern California doesn\'t lack for delicious ultra high-end steak tacos. The seared, heavily charred edges of the tender, smoky short loin are what makes Guerrilla Taco\'s "Grilled Steak Taco" one of L.A.\'s best tacos. The meat releases flavor galore when you bite into it, and the red and green salsas slathered on in the kitchen provide a heavy dose of piquancy and acidity to help neutralize the richer (but essential) elements in the dish: the well-marbled USDA Prime steak, the melted jack cheese, and the sturdy blue corn tortilla grilled in butter. I also loved the "Baja Cod Taco," which consisted of a large filet of rock cod in a crispy tempura batter with chipotle crema, Japanese mayo, sour pickled red cabbage, and heirloom cherry tomatoes that were both sweet and acetic. The "Sweet Potato Taco" is certainly interesting, even if it is not my thing at all. To make this well-known taco, the sweet potatoes are boiled, and then sauted in butter with thyme and deposited onto a corn tortilla before being smothered with a salsa made of almonds, tomatillos, chiles de rbol, habanero chiles, and fried garlic. Garnishments include feta cheese, chopped scallions, and pulverized corn nuts. A few problems: 1) Too much "tang" and not enough salt in the salsa, 2) The corn nuts are gritty like sand and thus unappetizing, and 3) I personally don\'t enjoy "mushy" tacos so much. Guerrilla Taco\'s "Pork Belly Taco" is garnished with smoked caviar, but is otherwise about what I expected. It\'s a strip of pork belly cooked so it crisps up on the outside and is greasy within, but could probably use a glaze or sauce beyond the charred habanero and chives added to this taco. That said, like all of the tacos here, I\'d almost order it just for the fresh hand-made corn tortilla, which could make a believer out of anyone in $5 tacos. This is a "fast casual" setup, where you order your tacos, then find a table to occupy while your food is prepared and delivered to you.'], ['108685370139018629938_6052e5b625ef3e77019421a7', 'My eyes bathed in the luxurious beauty of the tasting\'s initial offering: the delicate Le Caviar Imperial is perhaps better known as caviar araignee de mer, or caviar "spider of the sea," and is a work of art sprinkled with flakes of gold. The fresh, buttery caviar was so plentiful in my mouth, it felt like I was chewing a caviar steak coated with the flavorful jellied crustacean consomm it sat in. Some of the other tasting stand-outs included the delightful squid ink risotto served with the fish fillet, the rose shrimp served in the umami-rich ocean-y broth, the refreshing shaved ice with hibiscus syrup, and the heavenly chocolate hazelnut dessert with its glamorous edible butterflies made of sugar.'], ['108685370139018629938_6055f38b3019cb0a47838b3a', 'I\'ve never had Al Pastor pork so tasty in the U.S.. . As great as the Al Pastor pork was, I was disappointed by the fact they use packaged corn tortillas that smell less like corn and more like talcum powder. If I was desperately trying to convince someone to love Los Angeles, I\'d probably first take that person to Leo\'s Tacos. Leo\'s Tacos is a highly-esteemed fleet of trucks serving $1 tacos across L.A. This location in a gas station parking lot at Venice and LaBrea is the original truck and known to be the one to visit if you were looking for the very best version of Leo\'s tacos. During my recent visit, I ordered the "Al Pastor Taco" (pork shoulder marinated in adobo, shaved off of a spinning trompo) and the "Cabeza Taco" (braised cow head meat). First of all, forget about the Cabeza Taco: despite having some interesting varying textures within the small pile of meat on the tortilla, the overall flavor is too muddy and the cabeza is not appropriately seasoned, resulting in a below-average cabeza taco in Los Angeles. I implore everyone to instead focus 100% of their attention on Leo\'s "Al Pastor Taco." Think of your typical good Al Pastor pork: some pieces ultra-crispy, others ultra-tender, and the best of those magenta-glazed meat strips share both textures in one piece of meat. That\'s Leo\'s secret: through excellent knife-work, they maximize the amount of crusted, sticky edges in their tortillas. Additionally, you will need to dress these tacos yourself: for the Al Pastor Taco, I recommend onions, cilantro, and their salsa roja (deep red sauce) from the salsa bar; for the Cabeza Taco, a tangy salsa verde is more appropriate. My above quibbles are very minor, and I bring them up only because when you\'re talking about a taco this good, you are talking about the very best tacos you can find, and this invites contextualization and comparison against other tacos in this tier. I have not found a better Al Pastor Taco in L.A.'], ['108685370139018629938_60478d5c90b81483d31acd76', 'Tajima is a Convoy ramen-ya with a craptacular parking situation, but superb ramen. My favorite appetizer is the "Beef Tataki with Jalapeo," described on Tajima\'s menu as "thinly-sliced seared beef sashimi served with ponzu sauce, grated radish and jalapeo," and also features enough bonito flakes to provide a surprisingly crunchy textural layer to this dish. I also like to order the "Omurice" as an appetizer and split it among my party. Omurice is a unique Japanese dish consisting of an omelette stuffed with rice, typically ketchup fried rice. It\'s not what I\'d consider to be authentic Omurice based on what I\'ve had elsewhere, but it\'s tasty! The reason you come to Tajima, however, is the ramen. The "Ramen with Tonkotsu" (Pork Bone Broth) is what to order. Tajima\'s slurpable, soulful tonkotsu broth is thick, gelatinous, and salty, while enriched by tiny bits of pork fat, scallions, deep garlic flavor, and sesame. San Diego provides a myriad of options for ramen -- some of which I\'d advise sophisticated diners to stay clear of (I\'m looking at you, Underbelly), but most of which are at least OK. Tajima is in the top tier, above most other San Diego ramen-yas.'], ['108685370139018629938_6056362cd335d0abfb415a77', 'The first course I ordered at Sinatra was the Polipo, which featured octopus in a roasted red pepper emulsion. This was the best part of the meal for me -- of particular delight was the tenderness of the octopus which, according to my waiter, is due to the octopus being vigorously beaten after it is caught and before its muscles tighten up. (I have a running theory that no two chefs tenderize their octopus the same way, which is why I always get a different answer when I ask.) The red pepper sauce served with the octopus was umami-rich, and featured fried capers with a crispy texture, providing a nice contrast to the soft Mediterranean octopus. My next course was Pennette Pasta (half-sized) with a rag of Italian sausage, bell peppers, and basil. Pasta was cooked al dente. I much enjoyed swirling the fork-tender meat around to pick up more veal broth reduction and lip-smacking collagen. On recommendation of my waiter, I paired the ossobuco with the silky 2011 Masi Costasera Amarone, which was a delicious, medium-bodied wine that paired perfectly with the veal.'], ['108685370139018629938_605677d63019cb0a47838d3c', 'Fajitas are average. My favorite thing to get here is probably the "Southwest Egg Rolls," which feature chicken, black beans, corn, jalapeo jack cheese, red peppers, and spinach in fried flour tortillas with a \'not horrible\' avocado-ranch sauce for dipping.'], ['108685370139018629938_60571756d2ad6b7a67e27f83', 'Tacos y Birria el Guero is a low-key taqueria sharing a parking lot with a nail spa in Santa Ana. I love their "Asada Taco." Like most carne asada street-style tacos, it features thinly-sliced marinated beef mixed with chopped onions and cilantro deposited into back-to-back double corn tortillas. For as much as I believe typical carne asada to be a grossly overrated taco filling, this is the good stuff, the Hennessy XO of carne asada. There is a smooth and tasty avocado-chile salsa at the salsa bar that this taco wears perfectly. The "Birria de Res Taco" is also quite fantastic. This taco features juicy braised beef rib meat pervaded with small luscious specks of salty fat. I drizzled some of the Salsa de Aceite (spicy chile oil) onto this taco and it dialed up the intensity and heat of the birria considerably.'], ['108685370139018629938_604f472088c7af3f893e63fc', 'I couldn\'t leave here without ordering the grilled fish that is Mitch\'s raison d\'tre, if all of the reviews are to be believed. On a Tuesday in March, Mitch\'s "Grilled Market Halibut" featured a grilled and nearly blackened half-pound halibut filet from the Sea of Cortez. The fish\'s snow-white flesh tasted fine, had firm and dense texture, but a delightful taste aside from a bitterness imparted by whatever they\'re using for their seasoning blend, or the grill itself. I\'d rather have had the fish better-salted prior to cooking than the unctuous salsa verde sauce. The "Grilled Oysters" are pretty good -- not New Orleans good, but San Diego good. On the day I had them, they were six briny oysters from Hawk\'s Point (Washington), grilled with breadcrumbs, bacon, parmesan, corn, and leeks. The reason I came to Mitch\'s was to try their fish tacos. The first taco I ordered was the "Beer Battered Alaskan Cod Taco," which featured one big chunk of cod, both juicy and flaky, deep-fried until crispy but still light in color and flavor. The fish is put in a double layer of middling corn tortillas and topped with lime crema, shredded cabbage, tomatoes, and onions. There\'s no heat in this taco, so I used the glass bottles of "Mitch\'s Pineapple Habanero Salsa" provided at each table to liven it up. Thankfully, however, it added a sweet and sour flavor element to help cut through the batter and tortillas and everything else. I wish Mitch\'s was as good at taco construction and achieving an appropriate balance of ingredients inside tortillas as they were at frying fish. They\'re a seafood restaurant first and foremost, which is why their fried battered fish taco is not the best in the city, despite the actual fish itself arguably being the best. Similarly, the "Grilled Wild Shrimp Taco" - made with same ingredients as the Beer Battered Alaskan Cod taco -- suffers from poor overall taco construction. Also, the shrimp is grilled in the same way as the grilled fish, making the surface a bit bitter. These achingly middling shrimp tacos are another example of "taquero" being a truly skilled role - and that even the best ingredients and meats don\'t always make the best tacos.'], ['108685370139018629938_6042b93ec6fcf1fddba18c0b', 'King Taco has been blessed by the legendary Jonathan Gold as "the first important proliferator of the modern L.A. King Taco introduced a large segment of L.A.\'s population to what was once called "soft tacos" but they now just call "tacos." Even more crucially, King Taco brought the "al pastor taco" and the "carnitas taco" to the SoCal masses. Tacos in the U.S. have evolved, of course, and we live in a quasi-capitalist society, so those who come into something first can\'t always be relied upon to always be the best at it. In the case of King Taco, they\'re not serving bad tacos. In fact, any of their stores would be the best taco shop in 99% of American cities. But we\'re talking about Southern California, and their tacos are middle-of-the-road for the region in 2019.'], ['108685370139018629938_6055f2003019cb0a47838b35', 'The specialty of Tito\'s La Especial are "tacos al vapor," aka steamed tacos. This delicious Mexican street food is also known as "tacos de canasta" (basket tacos) because they\'re traditionally layered in a big basket and sold by street vendors, many of whom hawk them from their bikes. Tito\'s "Carne Deshebrada Taco Al Vapor" is excellent. Aside from steamed double corn tortillas comprising each taco\'s "shell," the chile-steeped shredded beef inside is soft, luscious, and as juicy as you\'d want any meat to be. Despite the fact they traditionally would be drizzled in oil (to help preserve them) and served out of a basket over the course of a day, these tacos are best made-to-order. I would also recommend the "Papas Taco Al Vapor," consisting of seasoned potatoes in a ranchera sauce, a loose mash of creamy crushed potatoes and firmer chunks, all colored orange from the sauce. The "Taco Dorado de Carne Deshebrada" served here is the complete opposite of the al vapor tacos, as the tortilla is instead a crunchy deep-fried shell that is stuffed with stewed beef, lettuce, chopped tomatoes, and shredded cheese. Tito\'s does a decent job with this style of taco, but you really should stick to the al vapor tacos here, which are indeed "especial." Tito\'s La Especial\'s salsa roja is made of fire and miracles and I recommend it be used on everything you eat here.'], ['108685370139018629938_604e40f277e81aaed3ccae6d', 'I\'ve ordered several dishes at the Caf 21 location in Gaslamp, but my favorite has been the "Curry Seared Scallops," served in a cast iron skillet, featuring large sauteed scallops covered in a zesty yellow yogurt curry sauce and bread crumbs, served over a potato leek puree that crisps up and sticks to the pan in a GOOD way. The "Shrimp Corn Cakes" are a great breakfast. This creative and lively take on eggs benedict is one of my favorite breakfast items served in Gaslamp. Strawberry sauce is drizzled into small dots on the plate, and a sweet blueberry compote is served on the side.'], ['108685370139018629938_6050dec5c53d98b3eace1889', 'Bring me slushy frozen margaritas in glasses with sugar-brushed rims! Bring me your booziest blueberry-pom-acai mojitos! I have no palate for these types of drinks, so it tasted a bit like what I actually remember of my last Hand Grenade in New Orleans. I decided to push my boundaries a bit and ordered the "La Familia," an inebriating tipple containing tequila, mezcal, cinnamon syrup, lime juice, and grapefruit juice. This drink was strong with cinnamon and had a clearer and more on-the-nose flavoring scheme than the Bro Tai. I\'ve woken up with enough brutal hangovers from cinnamon spirits like Goldschlger and Fireball that I should have hated this, but perhaps it\'s because I am such a bad drinker that this cocktail ended up being my favorite at Miss B\'s. I\'ve also tried their riff on the Rum & Coke, "Cuba Libre," bottled in-house and containing cane cola, spiced rum, and lime juice. I\'ve had the "Curried Coconut Shrimp," which is closer in style to a southeast Asian curry dish than a Jamaican curry, and the smoky "El Cubano" with crispy fries.'], ['108685370139018629938_6050acea9c93e55e75b72174', "Initially, my favorite thing about Anna's burritos? The beautiful, tasty juices that'd drip from the tortilla into the foil that I'd then slurp out when no one was looking. The steamed flour tortillas, a trick stolen by both Anna's and Boca Grande from the celebrated taquerias of the San Francisco Mission. The steaming process helps make the tortilla edges sticky enough to bind and seal everything in, so that the burrito can be eaten vertically, and that the mixture of hot sauce, vegetable juices, melted cheese, and meat fat mingle and combine. My burrito of choice is a Super Burrito with Carnitas, Pinto Beans, Rice, Cheese, Salsa (Cilantro, Onion, Tomato), all wrapped in a flour tortilla.. I live in San Diego, a city known for its burritos, and I can't enjoy them because they're all both objectively and subjectively inferior to Anna's. In this way, Anna's has ruined burritos for me."], ['108685370139018629938_6041ba6b2e57ebdea29c5e16', 'All of the customers here submit their orders in Spanish, the place makes its own fresh corn tortillas in front of you, it is open 24x7, and they give away blistered chile toreados at the front counter. These are all tell-tale signs of a legit taco operation. My first victim during my visit was the "Buche Taco," (Pork Stomach) a combination of crispy buche and soft buche, marinated and smothered in one of the most flavorful and beautiful sauces I\'ve ever tasted on a taco. The textural contrast was wonderful: crispy salty bits, spicy and sour chewy bits, fresh onions and cilantro, and a heavy, thick corn tortilla. The sweet tortilla tastes like fresh corn, which is how a good tortilla really ought to taste. This is, without a doubt, the best Buche Taco I\'ve eaten. The "Tripa Taco" was dispatched next, and I found it to be worth ordering as well, even if it is not as transcendent as the Buche Taco. The tripa taco also features onions, cilantro, and a snappy salsa verde.'], ['108685370139018629938_60548f4a6204e8cd294f2344', "The churros are decent, I'm just not sure this place is necessary in a city where you can't throw a taco without hitting a place that sells churros. Here you can order your Spanish donut sticks covered in Fruity Pebbles, matcha, Nutella, or just about any trendy sweet topping du jour; in other words, if someone with Snapchat puppy ears can put it on a scoop of conflict-free non-GMO gelato, you'll find it here. Perhaps I was expecting churros that were so extraordinary that they merited a fast-casual spot on Convoy that does nothing but churros. What I got was a warm, crispy, cinnamon-sugar pastry that was par for the course in this region, with some sweet, sticky dips on the side."], ['108685370139018629938_60464d69882f4d1caf5fee25', 'One of my favorites I\'ve visited has been "Tacos Tumbras a Tomas," an operation that has been around since 1995, run by Tomas Martinez with his brothers Jesus and Manuel. The "Carnitas Taco." Here, the pork shoulder is cooked confit-style in simmering lard in a large steel cazo. A generous amount of the resulting carnitas is piled onto double corn tortillas, with two extra tortillas given on the side for good measure -- there is, after all, a ton of meat involved here. Chopped onions, cilantro, salsa roja, and a full lime (halved) are provided on the taco if you say "yes" when you\'re asked if you want "the works" or "con todo." The entire thing cost me $4.50, tax included, but was easily the equivalent of more than two normal-sized carnitas tacos. I suggest Tacos Tumbras a Tomas for a satisfying, filling, affordable lunch served without the lines or fuss of some of the busier stalls in the vicinity.'], ['108685370139018629938_604749eab0e2129e47536090', 'My wife and I dined here recently, beginning our meal with the "Mother Board," a cutting board spread of a cured meats (Bresaola, Duck Pt, Salami) and cheeses (Camembert, Bucheron, Drunken Goat) with some familiar fixins\' mixed in with some not-so-familiar. The "Ahi Poke Tuna Tacos" were much enjoyed by my wife and me. The texture of the ahi is stunning and delicate, its tender, raw chunks will melt in your mouth. The Asian slaw is sweet, but not overly so, and the wonton "taco shell" is crispy but light, the combination of all of this coming across as decadent, but not heavy. Evaluating it strictly as a taco, it may not have conventional taco ingredients, but it is a very well-composed bite of food, balancing the fish, sauce, cabbage, and shell like a legit taquero would. My entre was the "Greater Omaha Prime Flat Iron," a half-pound steak that was cooked to a luscious medium-rare as I requested, its edges and surfaces blasted with heat so its seasonings and fat mix with charred outer-proteins to form a marvelous crust. A creamy parsnip pure, savory slices of grilled trumpet mushrooms, and crisp asparagus in herb butter complete a delectable steak dish that didn\'t break the bank, at just $34 all-in.'], ['108685370139018629938_60520101da79151bfc125c2d', "I'm usually alright with White Castle, but not when it immobilizes me on my Vegas vacation for a day and a half."], ['108685370139018629938_605676dc3019cb0a47838d38', 'The Pork Souvlaki was real good (and I recommend this if you come here), even if I thought the Gyros were so-so.'], ['108685370139018629938_604e0d8b71ced5c7554dda45', 'Obviously here in San Diego, most of the food at "On The Border" is awful compared to what you can get from a myriad of legit, authentic local Mexican restaurants. I say "most" and not "all" because the one thing On The Border has engineered of value are their complimentary chips and salsa, which stand up to the best chips and salsa that even a city like San Diego has to offer. Maybe order some guacamole (which they make in front of you, table-side.)'], ['108685370139018629938_60425ef37dfa7f187183c4de', 'While approaching this taco truck, my eyes were immediately drawn to a large trompo stacked with layers of well-manicured adobo-marinated pork spinning around, reflecting a flame off of a glistening surface sweating with achiote-infused meat juices. Upon ordering an "Al Pastor Taco" here, the taquero will carve off thin slices of pork directly off of this upside-down mountain of meat into single corn tortillas and top it off with a chunk of pineapple. Aside from the customary onions and cilantro, ensure your taco has El Flamin\'s red sauce on it. This is a hypnotic, mouth-numbing salsa roja that complements and completes the al pastor pork, and the "secret sauce" that keeps this truck doing brisk business. El Flamin\'s "Al Pastor Tacos" would be better with a more assertive marinade, so they do not reach the same heights as the al pastor served at Leo\'s or even the Ave 26 Taco Stand, but they are definitely in my "top 5" favorite pastor-style tacos in Los Angeles. As with the other two al pastor purveyors I mentioned, bagged corn tortillas are used here.']]

The Irish coffee was mixed well with the coffee overpowering the whiskey (for the most part) but without being overly sweet. The strawberry daiquiri was dangerous as you cant really taste the alcohol and it just seems like a smoothie.'], ['105853218368004682403_604e0202b9a3d5528c50bc5b', 'I could wax poetic about the virtues of the Mexican chocolate pie at The Pie Hole, but to put it simply, the Pie Hole consistently has delicious desserts that are indulgent and rich. The Mexican chocolate pie is thick and creamy, while the earl grey pie is more light and airy, but grounded by the toasted pistachios that adorn its top. You should split the pies with loved ones, although its certainly doable to eat an entire slice by yourself. You can order a whole pie if youd like, and they do offer drinks like matcha tea and coffee. The cashier was very friendly and mentioned that they have happy hour from Monday through Friday where pie slices are $5 and whole pies are ~$30.'], ['105853218368004682403_604913b3b1a0aaee3eefa92e', 'The cheesecakes are a 5 but the food is a solid 3. For a family of four, we got an egg roll sampler, a regular size farfalle pasta with chicken and a garlic cream sauce, and two cheesecakes. The egg roll sampler was a good order since theres a variety to try and theres plenty of dipping sauce to choose from. My favorite was the avocado one, but everyone else really liked the hamburger egg roll dipped into the pink sauce (which I think is thousand island dressing). The pasta was disappointing - it was super oily with sparse amounts of chicken and accoutrements. The cheesecakes were the highlight - the godiva one is so decadent and rich, so its perfect for a chocolate fanatic. The white chocolate macadamia nut with the blondie brownie crust was also a surprise hit. The macadamia nuts were a bit soggy, but paired well with the white chocolate chunks. The bottom layer brownie was nice and and chewy, and complemented the creaminess of the cheesecake.'], ['105853218368004682403_6057007d6fce2069470c60cf', 'I used to love going to Raising Canes when I lived in Phoenix, so I was excited to get my chicken tender fix. Its an extra 30 something cents per sauce but they do keep well if you want to use them for some home cooked chicken tenders. The fries are crinkle-cut and were under seasoned. The Texas toast was very good - it was still warm and buttery by the time we got to eat it. review_text: The BBQ sauce was not good, it pretty much tasted like ketchup with stuff added. The entrees were the Tx Haystack BBQ burger, my hubs had them take off the sauce and put the smoked gouda instead of the cheddar cheese. I had the ribs and they were not good at all, it had the same BBQ sauce which I didn't know the flavor until I tasted the wings. Their slaw had an odd mix of, what looked like fennel, bell peppers, and other veggies but it was bland and did not really taste good.
history_reviews: [['100730701747595128613_604153f5c6fcf1fddba12bd2', "The fries gator tasted like chicken and the oysters were delish. The entrees for me were just okay, I had the New Orleans sampler which was the red beans and rice, crawfish etoufee, and jambalaya but I've had better. The seafood gumbo though was definitely not our fav. It had too much of a seafood/fishy-shrimpy flavor and nothing else in it."], ['100730701747595128613_60572686d2ad6b7a67e27fc4', "I ordered the Mozzarella Bread, which was a French bread loaf cut with a garlic or butter topping and cheese with tomatoes, there wasn't really any seasoning. For the main dish, I ordered the Works thin crust."], ['100730701747595128613_6050bd804cd354c57204c176', "First time in this Asian bakery and the items we chose were delish. They were not overly sweet and who doesn't like bread with little hidden gems inside lol. The coconut roll/log had a subtle coconut flavor with almond slivers and pockets of a dense coconut filling. The purplish roll was a Taro roll that was not tart like I thought it was going to be. Then the Chocolate bread, I think was my favorite because I love me some chocolate. It was light with pieces of chocolate like shavings baked in it and lightly dusted with powdered sugar...yummm. Lastly, the strawberry cake with a light custardy center was cool and refreshing and light. The icing was like a whipped meringue type cream, it was good but maybe my least favorite of the items."], ['100730701747595128613_6041e2dec6fcf1fddba15a0c', "Hubby and I tried Velvet Taco for the first time Friday because it was a recommendation and the establishment is a quaint, intimate, and a cool chill vibe. We ordered the plain queso blanco (bc I don't like spicy), even with it plain we really liked the flavor of the cheese, it was not too salty. We ordered one picnic chicken and three barbacoa tacos. The picnic chicken was really good and the rotisserie chicken was tender and had a really good flavor and the crispy chicken skin toppings made it have a great texture. The barbacoa taco had a goid flavor but to me the heat from the spice or sauce was too spicy for me but I still ate it and it was still delish! Hubbs really liked that taco. We ended the meal with their famous red velvet cake which was moist and tasty but very rich so we saved half to eat the next day ."], ['100730701747595128613_604bc96320f26f37fb9d7ea4', "We ate the mediterranean (lamb gyro and the bowl) they were pretty good, we had to eat outside though and unfortunately couldn't find a spot under a heater so my food got cold fast but the flavor was still good. For dessert we went to the donut shop and had the red velvet donuts but for 3.25 each it was not good. I snagged some macaroons and a strawberry cheesecake ice cream at a different spot and that made up for the donuts."], ['100730701747595128613_60571649c4674474cff91275', 'The sushi was really good and tasted fresh and my husband was able to find out what fish came in that day for the sushi. So I am not sure if our bill was decent for sushi and hibachi but 3 sushi rolls and a teriyaki chicken hibachi and a soda was $58 before tip.'], ['100730701747595128613_6050fa9f5b4ccec8d5cae994', "The waffles were good also, I think it could have just been just a tad firmer/better crunch. The eggs were good and the grits were perfectly thick like I like. So my meal was the #1 which was 2 large waffles 3 huge pieces of chicken (and you can request the pieces) eggs and grits and a soda, which how adorable it's in a huge mason jar, for $19 and some change."], ['100730701747595128613_60570da4d2ad6b7a67e27f52', 'My family all had burgers and we split the fries and onion rings. My husband and son both ordered the Bacon Burger and my husband was pleasantly surprised by the shallot compote paired with the chilli sauce, our waiter stated that you have to eat them together because they balance each other out but if you try them separately they are not good and my husband agrees. I had the Cowboy burger with no jalapenos and it was quite tasty. They did not over BBQ sauce the burger and the brisket was a nice touch. The onion rings though were pretty great, it had a great batter to where it stuck to the onion. The fries were also crispy which surprisingly was good. You order the burger and sides separate which is common nowadays, the burgers themselves are a little on the pricey side.']]

review_text: We had Guacamole to start. We ordered 4 Tacos . The Rock Shrimp Taco is a must try. It's got a great flavor and the lemon , parsley slaw is fresh and adds texture. The Pork Belly is my favorite. Carne Asada is another "go to" taco and the Cauliflower taco gives vegetarians a unique,  slightly spicy option. I was initially surprised the meat was shredded, however, it makes sense when you think about making sure the duck absorbs the flavor of the tamarind glaze. They do not have sour cream and it doesnt matter,  the aioli amazing to add moisture and flavor to the tacos.
history_reviews: [['113001727079928746403_6049fb0fb1a0aaee3eefb525', 'We ordered Spanish bean soup and a 1905 salad to share. The salad would have been enough for three and their homemade dressing fit well with  the meat, cheese and greens. For dinner we shared the Grouper in a light Citrus broth with crab meat. The grouper was tender and smooth, not fishy and the crab was sweet and fresh. The rice was good, not great, however I really enjoyed the asparagus on the side.'], ['113001727079928746403_6042504ab9a6829e686e9003', 'The 2 large salads had bottled dressing on the side and there were serving utensils for each dish. The Chicken Parm we ordered was very tender, seasoned well and cut in sections for a larger group. We really liked the Shrimp Primevera, a lighter option,  with the vegetables and sweet Shrimp. The toasted Ravioli were a little over cooked, however they still tasted great.'], ['113001727079928746403_604a88033ebca1b150aa16e9', 'I had the Parmasean Garlic wings and they were plump and flavorful, a little dry. We also ordered a Chicken Ceasar Wrap with Grilled Chicken. The lettuce was crisp and the Chicken was well seasoned.'], ['113001727079928746403_6042ca47c6fcf1fddba190e5', "My Chicken quesadilla was just okay. The top inch or so of the tortilla was rawish, not crisp and lacked filling. Okay let's try wings. I will say the garlic parmesan bone in wings were pretty good. They had a nice flavor and the chicken was still moist."], ['113001727079928746403_6049bd4ad863393130a40be6', 'Gator is one of my favorites and the menu says marinated with fried pickles, okay sounds great. 3 of everything - 3 croutons, 3 cucumber slices, 3 tomatoes and 3 pieces of onion on iceberg for $3.99. The Gator is dry inside and the breading just falls off many of them it\'s so crispy over fried and it\'s flavorless. $14.99 for the Gator pieces and $3.99 for the salad made me agree with all the "over priced" comments I\'ve heard.'], ['113001727079928746403_6047818c48e7cc5a9ce289ef', 'The San Francisco Eggs Benedict and Monte Cristo Sandwhich. I have to say the Eggs Benedict was great. The combination of avocado with a most perfectly  poached egg and a light hollandaise sauce was delicious.'], ['113001727079928746403_6050dc004cd354c57204c1f9', 'They had cream based clam chowder for the soup today and that sounded great.'], ['113001727079928746403_60509c815b4ccec8d5cae761', 'The bartender recommended a drink for me and the Salmon, I have  been looking for another Salmon place do I ordered Cajun Style Atlantic Salmon. The fish was amazing and I am a picky Salmon person. I liked to sauce  with it and the fish was moist and not fishy. It was all good though and the Salmon was a superstar.'], ['113001727079928746403_6042d355c6fcf1fddba19243', "I ordered a drink from her, she gave me a menu and I selected the tacos. I have to say I was very disappointed in the Tacos, the tortillas were raw and  chewy and they were not filled with much of anything. The pork belly taco, and I was very much looking forward to, was more like a piece of crisp bacon. Around Tampa Bay a really good taco is about $2.50 to $3 a piece. Yes, I'm on the river so I said okay $13.50 for three tacos let's do it. The highlight of the meal were the sauces that the bartender went to get me from the kitchen they made the tacos much more edible. I will definitely give it some time and maybe I'll go back and try again however, I definitely not order the  Tacos or the Pork Belly Sandwhich if it's going to be crisp bacon."]]

review_text: We ordered the 2 lobster special for dinner ($22), 2 shrimp cocktails, and the garden salad with lobster meat. We are on vacation- just came from Bar Harbor, and we came to the conclusion that the Porthole had the best lobster all trip!!
history_reviews: [['105707422252637657645_6049595cc7c8ee3104ba1750', 'The wings were fresh, hot, saucy, but small.']]

review_text: Rice, cabbage, crushed peanuts, and a peanut mango sauce were all mixed in the bowl. If it werent for the slight hint of mango and the cilantro sprinkled in, it would have tasted very similar to phad thai.
history_reviews: [['104266121831233393715_60564a793019cb0a47838caf', "They have po'boys, boils by the pound and all the traditional cajun style stuff. The po'boys are like a foot long, so be aware of the amount of food you are getting before you order. Crab, shrimp, and lobster boils available. You choose your protein, choose the seasoning of the sauce it is boiled in and then choose the heat level. Be aware, you eat Cajun style, which means with your hands! They do have red beans and rice and gumbo, but they are prefixed with their own custom names, so they are hard to find on the menu. I don't recall seeing any jambalaya but I can't swear to that."], ['104266121831233393715_605062a65b4ccec8d5cae5c9', "Check out the new vegan sandwich - the Captain Jack - I won't describe it here, but check out their online menu for deets."], ['104266121831233393715_6045cdb2882f4d1caf5fe17e', 'The bacon was overcooked bacon and so was the ahi. The seasoning was also too heavy on the ahi.'], ['104266121831233393715_604a7b71672e5ba60a383695', 'Corned beef hash ($10.50) with over easy eggs and toast was good. Huevos rancheros ($9.75) was interesting because the eggs, ranchero sauce, and pico de gallo were served on TOP of the tortillas. I like black beans, but I like my huevos rancheros with refried beans. Aside from committing those two cardinal sins, the dish was decent and the eggs were cooked sunny side up as I ordered them. Most of the veggies and sauces are .75 each, but avocado is $2.50, and there is a sausage gravy you can add for $3.00. I added chopped chipotle peppers to my huevos rancheros for 75 cents, but I could hardly tell they were there. I went with the brewmosa (a Belgian style wheat beer & fresh OJ). Mainly because of the prices for breakfast items, and also because of their non traditional take on huevos rancheros.'], ['104266121831233393715_60551d20d335d0abfb415749', 'I ordered the grilled Mahi Mahi Alto Cocina. It was topped with generous slices of avocado, jumbo lump crab, pico de gallo and some sort of cream based sauce. I opted for the vegetable medley, mainly consisting of squash, fresh green beans, and a few grilled onions. My dinner companion ordered the Pan Seared Pecan Encrusted Redfish with Mango Honey Butter and I tried a few bites of it. It was very good, fresh fish with a sweet honey coating. The fish on each dish was fresh, and all of the sides were wonderfully seasoned and perfectly cooked.'], ['104266121831233393715_604d215b77e81aaed3cca5d5', 'Description of my dish from the menu follows:. . Whole wheat tortilla-lined bowl filled with quinoa tabouli, kale salad, vegan tzatziki, green olives, falafel patties, cucumbers, tomatoes, carrots, dolmas, and pecan hummus I had the Mediterranean Bowl and it was good. Included two hush puppy sized falafels that I dipped in the tzatziki and hummus - very good!'], ['104266121831233393715_604c7fc93ada919c27677a99', "The Ensalada de Casa ($8.50) includes bacon and mango vinaigrette - very nice size with plenty of bacon slices in it. Fresh mixed greens (none of that iceberg lettuce here), tomatoes, and cucumbers. You can add smoked turkey for $2.95 or grilled shrimp for $5.95. The Baja Fish Tacos ($13.50) Blackened mahi mahi tacos served on doubled up corn tortillas like God intended them to be. The fish is topped with shredded carrots and cabbage, cotija cheese, and a flavorful chipotle crema. The tortillas weren't anything special, nor were they anything to brag about. But the quality of the mahi mahi fish was good and perfectly cooked - the toppings really added to the flavor of this entree. This plate includes refried beans and Spanish rice. You usually don't find this in refried beans, but they seemed to have just a tad of jalapeno flavor to them, just to make it interesting. The Spanish rice was undercooked, but they when we mentioned it, they substituted the veggies with no problem and no additional charge."], ['104266121831233393715_6051f4d0da79151bfc125bf7', 'Now lets talk about the drink situation. . 32 ounce schooners of draft beer, margaritas or micheladas. Great food, lots of choices to select from, including a la carte items for your weekly Taco Tuesday visits where you just want to hang out with friends for a couple of brews and have a light meal instead of a full meal. For those of you who want a full meal, they have plenty of enchilada dishes, taco dishes with rice and refried beans or borrachos beans. Chips and salsa are very good - the default salsa consists of roasted tomatoes, with a really good flavor and a slight kick to it. The green salsa (if you ask for it) is a bit hotter but not by much. I prefer the flavor of the roasted red salsa. Fish taco plate is HUGE, but the fish is a tad on the dry side. Its loaded down with veggies and theres not much fish on it. The carne guisada taco is ok, but a bit too salty. You can also get a flight of mini margarita flight and sample SIX different flavors.'], ['104266121831233393715_604d1bba77e81aaed3cca5ac', 'Had the Penne con Polpette e Salsiccia ($24) generous portions of meatballs and Italian sausage with penne pasta. It consisted of mushrooms, onion, bell pepper, asparagus, and a tomato based cream sauce. It was good, but it could have used more shrooms, and the asparagus could have been cooked to a more tender state. We also had the caprese salad as an appetizer ($9).'], ['104266121831233393715_604a7984c6dc737bce7e5acc', 'Next up:. Each table chooses two different broths to cook your entrees in, but each person can choose their own entree (this is the part I was confused about before I went - I thought each table had to share the same entree, but you dont). Each table of six chooses two different types of cheese to dip various types of bread, fruits, and veggies in. Then they bring out rice crispy treats, banana slices, waffle pieces and other delectable desserts for your dipping desires. I went with the veggie - kinda sucked because most of the veggies fall off of the skewers while they are in the broth, but oh well. In addition to the courses ordered, they also brought a couple of baskets of broccoli, new/red potatoes, and mushrooms to the table - those shrooms were THE BOMB after cooking them in the broth! I hear its a great place for date night, but I think you only get one burner so you have to agree on the cheese, broth, and chocolate flavor. They let us bring our own cake in and even brought out a knife so we could cut it up!'], ['104266121831233393715_604356bfaab4c25a4e74e00e', 'Includes your choice of a side: fries, potato chips, a cup of soup or a side salad. . Off the menu special - queso covered grilled chicken breast with jalapeno spices, rice and beans - this was so good, it should be a regular item on the menu, instead of just making the occasional guest appearance. Veggie sandwich - Texas toast, stuffed with LOTS of fresh spinach, lettuce, onions, mushrooms, tomatoes, onions, and avocado. The chicken was very juicy and the queso had just the right amount of spice to it. It even includes a drink and a freshly baked cookie.'], ['104266121831233393715_605649acd335d0abfb415a98', 'The weiner schnitzel was decent but didnt have a lot of flavor to it. By default, it comes with sptzle and some sort of cabbage, but I substituted the sauted veggies and the grilled asparagus for my sides. The veggies and grilled asparagus were sehr gut!'], ['104266121831233393715_604d23cd77e81aaed3cca5e5', 'Their main focus is on burgers and sandwiches, but they do have several salad choices, a grilled veggie wrap, a couple of chicken options and pasta options, and a flatbread pizza. I had the Impossible Burger with tater tots ($13.99 - ouch). The Impossible Burger is a veggie burger that can be found at several other restaurants (Google it to find it). This burger can even fool a carnivore - Im not kidding.'], ['104266121831233393715_6051d135c53d98b3eace1d2d', 'It included tofu (duh), snap peas, carrot slices, a few green onions, cilantro, and cabbage swimming in a tasty lemon juice. More mushrooms (I love my shrooms) and snap peas would have really helped out.'], ['104266121831233393715_605653b497d555cc6fb0d217', 'I had the veggie burger and a side salad with tomato vinaigrette dressing (Id skip this dressing folks, it tasted like it was just ketchup). The veggie patty was made from black beans, quinoa, and roasted red pepper.'], ['104266121831233393715_6049b7811ec03878d66c7ce8', 'I had the Schnitzel Burger with hot German potato salad. The pork schnitzel was perfectly breaded, and the pork was very moist but not oily or greasy, especially since it was fried  duh. The German potato salad had a really good flavor, but it was kind of watery and it was sliced potatoes instead of chopped potatoes  Ive never seen it like this before. Other dishes ordered that REALLY looked appealing were The Rueben, the Schnitzel Wiener Art, someone had the Hungarian Goulash, two in our party had the Stuffed Portobello which looked SO, SO GOOD! From seafood, to soup, to burgers, steak dishes, and even salads.'], ['104266121831233393715_60571437c4674474cff9126c', 'Fries were VERY bland, burger was nothing special at all.'], ['104266121831233393715_6050af869c93e55e75b72186', 'The beef fajita nachos are out of this world. Tender, flavorful fajita meat on top of a nice layer of cheese and refried beans on fresh, crisp tortilla chips. A hefty scoop of guac and sour cream is included in the middle of the plate. They dont have the best salsa bar in town, but it holds up fairly well. Unlimited (free) chips, several varieties of salsa, and free jalapeno slices for your nachos. Ice cold beer and good margaritas for sure.'], ['104266121831233393715_6047566cb3114911423b8765', 'I had the Superfood salad which was humongous and full of superfoods such as blueberries, kale, etc. The GF had the Mediterranean chicken tacos on pita bread and it looked so good and she said it was good too. Crazy dessert options too - try the baked beignet loaded with ice cream, strawberries and whipped cream. Devilishly delicious but like half the calories of the Pizookies that they have on their menus.']]

review_text: The peach pie was my favorite item here. The chili cheese dog was pretty good, and the chili cheeseburger was average.

I also got a Seoul steak bowl which has bulgogi on rice.'], ['105475010061777012769_6040ad8d65e4ba0588bb525c', "I ordered the Rapine e'nduja pizza which was 2nd place in the 2016 World Pizza Championship."], ['105475010061777012769_6056683a97d555cc6fb0d290', 'I went during the week they had the state fair theme, and I got the donut burger and poutine. The donut burger was delicious, and I loved how crisp the bacon was.
